items.body:
David Tibet reawakens his landmark ’84 debut, proper, as Current 93; a primordial stew of tape loops, atonal electronics, blood curdle exhortations and altogether ill-willed heck on the A-side, countered by a flip of more sepulchral spatialisation and a bewitching Annie Anxiety that calves off into the abyss, all captured during a time when they lived in a squat and danced with Youth at goth crucible, The Batcave. Sacred stuff for anyone into NWW, earliest Coil / Zos Kia, Psychic TV...

"Current 93’s first and last album, NATURE UNVEILED dragged together my obsessions, as I had decided to make a pop album that dealt with my (then—as now!) primary fascinations: Christian apocalyptic and eschatological Christian texts. In my Speed-Ridden Soul and Mind, I thought I was reinventing The Ronettes, and that the 2 long sides of NATURE UNVEILED were A- and B- Sides of a Wall Of Soundhogs HIT! But the reality is that I was sharing a squat in Vauxhall with Little Annie Anxiety, and hanging out with Youth in The BatCave, with chickens rescued by The Animal Liberation Front in our backyard. Or did that come soon after, soon later? The album was recorded at The Roundhouse Studios in London’s Chalk Farm, home of Bronze Records, the label of my heroes (then—as now!) Uriah Heep, and Motörhead too, for whom I had moved stage-gear on their tour promoting their debut single on Chiswick Records. Anyway, anyway—I had not reinvented The Ronettes, though every time, every place, I listen to NATURE UNVEILED it Hits.

- David Tibet, Hastings, 11 March 2026."
items._cn_summary: Current 93 1984年首张专辑的正式再版，A面以磁带循环、无调性电子声响与近乎嘶吼的人声交织，形成原始而暴烈的听觉冲击；B面转向更具空间感的低回氛围，Annie Anxiety 的人声如漂浮在深渊之上的呢喃。专辑录制于伦敦 Chalk Farm 的 Roundhouse Studios，彼时乐队成员蜗居 Vauxhall 的一处公社院落中，与 Youth 出入传奇哥特俱乐部 BatCave，后院还养着动物解放阵线救下的鸡。David Tibet 试图用末日启示录式的基督教文本重塑 Ronettes 的音墙美学，结果产出的是一张介于工业、暗黑民谣与后朋克之间的原始文献。整张作品既是个人信仰执念的投射，也是英国地下音乐场景特定时空下的声音化石，对于研究早期工业、哥特与实验音乐谱系的听众而言具有不可替代的史料与美学双重价值。

items.body:
If the casual's choice is 'A Love Supreme', the head's favorite has to be Coltrane's game-changing free jazz masterpiece 'Ascension', which Verve now presents remastered from the original tapes, in a complete edition featuring both explosive takes. If you're into Peter Brötzmann, Glenn Branca, John Zorn or Joe McPhee, consider it required listening.

Coltrane didn't invent free jazz - that was Ornette Coleman, who coined the term on his landmark 1960 album - but he certainly helped the New York City-centric movement gain an extra level of respectability when he released 'Ascension' in 1966. Because just a year prior, he'd released his most successful album ever, 'A Love Supreme', perfecting the post-bop/spiritual jazz sound he'd been refining for the last few years. At this stage, he was one of the most recognisable figures in jazz, certainly the most critically acclaimed, so his opinion held unimaginable weight. And unlike onlookers who saw Coleman and Albert Ayler as cacophonous noise, Coltrane was fascinated; he cites Coleman specifically as a direct influence and had been orbiting Ayler in the months before recording 'Ascension', scouring the East Coast for young players who might have the chops to keep up with his ideas. He picked fellow horn players Pharoah Sanders, Marion Brown, John Tchicai and Archie Shepp, trumpet players Dewey Johnson and Freddie Hubbard, bassists Jimmy Garrison and Art Davis, pianist McCoy Tyner and drummer Elvin Jones - all of whom are now household names.

And the group entered the Van Gelder Studio in New Jersey on June 28th 1965 without rehearsing beforehand. They recorded two sessions and weren't sure what to make of it at first. Even Coltrane admits he was overwhelmed at the time, worried about how it might be received and worked half to death. And when the album was released, despite its acclaim, Coltrane still wasn't sure; the second take of the day had been used, so a new edition was released labeled 'Ascension (Edition II)', using the first take. But it's splitting hairs, really - both takes capture Coltrane at the height of his powers as both a performer and a bandleader. Not only was he able to assemble some of the scene's most passionate, skillful players and corral them into refining a sound that hadn't yet been properly codified, he recorded one of the jazz scene's most volatile, influential and enduring avant-garde sets, an album that braided history with modernity and Black American culture with ideas informed by Coltrane's deep knowledge of African, Asian and Indian musical forms.

It's one of those records that's no doubt easier to digest now, six decades after its original release. 'Ascension' is still uncompromisingly eccentric, but its innovations have at the very least informed the direction of the avant vernacular, inspiring later jazz fusion experiments, noise artists, even certain strains of post-punk. And with a new remaster from Sterling Sound's Ryan K. Smith, it's really never sounded better. Timeless shit, really.
items._genre: free jazz / avant-garde / spiritual jazz / post-bop
items._cn_summary: 这张1965年录音、1966年发行的专辑是自由爵士史上的里程碑之作。Coltrane在录制前没有排练，召集了当时纽约前卫爵士圈最顶尖的乐手——Pharoah Sanders、Archie Shepp、Marion Brown、John Tchicai、McCoy Tyner、Elvin Jones等——在Van Gelder Studio进行了两场充满不确定性的即兴录制。专辑深受Ornette Coleman影响，同时吸收了Albert Ayler的能量，将非洲、亚洲、印度音乐元素与黑人美国音乐文化编织在一起。乐评详细介绍了两个版本的由来（初版用第二take，后发行Edition I用第一take），并指出该作对后世噪音艺术、爵士融合、后朋克产生的深远影响。本次由Sterling Sound的Ryan K. Smith从原始母带重新母带处理。

items.body:
Mexican sound artist Concepción Huerta presents a carefully crafted new album - "both a tribute to the literary work of Eduardo Galeano and a howl from the Lacandon jungle in Mexico".

"This album, crafted entirely on a subharmonic framework and meticulously processed through tape manipulation, stands as Concepción Huerta’s sharpest work to date, undoubtedly her most abrasive, intense, and exhilarating. Her signature remains intact: an approach deeply rooted in drone, musique concrète, and hauntingly visceral textures.

Conceptually, Huerta’s sonic vision evokes an image of open veins, not human veins, but those of the earth itself, the open veins of Latin America. These nervures are, in truth, rivers of lava; fury transmuted into fire coursing beneath the land until it erupts. The album is, in a way, a reflection on dispossession, resource extraction, and colonization. But beyond being a historical commentary—one that some might relegate to a forgotten past—it is also a reminder of the present, of how these practices persist in contemporary, postmodern guises.

It serves as both a tribute to the literary work of Eduardo Galeano, one of the most influential voices of Latin American leftist thought, and a howl from the Lacandon jungle in Mexico, resonating with the Zapatista struggle, the resistance of the Guaraní people in Paraguay and Argentina, and the voices of Indigenous communities across Latin America.

In the 16th century, a book titled Visión de los vencidos (The Broken Spears) was published in Mexico, compiling Nahuatl texts that presented the unofficial history, the account of the defeated. Concepción Huerta’s album El Sol de los Muertos (The Sun of the Dead) is not a call to action nor a reactionary manifesto, but an invitation to reflection, a historical reexamination. It urges us not to accept the official narrative at face value and serves as a warning, to remain vigilant and, within our capacities, resist the resurgence of fascism and colonialism in all its modern forms.

Recorded by Concepción Huerta in 2024 between Berlin, The Hague, and Mexico City. Volcano photography by Magaly Ugarte. Mastered by Rafael Anton Irisarri at Black Knoll Studio, New York. The tapes were duplicated in Avranches, France, and the cover was risograph printed in Barcelona by Mateo Barbuzzi aka Club del Prado. Design by Daniel Castrejón in Mexico City."
items._genre: drone / musique concrète / experimental / ambient / tape manipulation
items._cn_summary: 墨西哥声音艺术家Concepción Huerta的专辑《El Sol de los Muertos》完全建立在次低频框架之上，经磁带处理精心雕琢而成，是其迄今最具侵略性、强度与爆发力的作品。整张专辑延续了她根植于drone、具象音乐与内在脏器般质地的创作路线，声音设计呈现出大地裂开的血管意象——拉丁美洲被攫取的资源化作岩浆暗流，最终喷涌而出。专辑既是向乌拉圭作家Eduardo Galeano文学成就的致敬，也是来自墨西哥Lacandon丛林的呐喊，与萨帕塔运动、瓜拉尼人抵抗及拉美原住民声音形成共振。在创作概念上，它延续了16世纪Nahuatl文本《Visión de los vencidos》那种由被征服者书写的历史视角，揭示殖民与掠夺在新形式下的延续，拒绝接受官方叙事。专辑录制于柏林、海牙与墨西哥三地，由Rafael Anton Irisarri在纽约Black Knoll Studio完成母带处理。

items.body:
In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to marvel at one of the finest examples of loop-based electronic music typical of the early noughties.

Taking what reads like a pretty austere set of ingredients, Jelinek's technique revolves around a trio of elements which consist of second long cuts of 1960's-70's jazz recordings, the loop-finding modulation wheel (do your homework!) and the Moiré effect; albeit rendered in the acoustic as opposed to the image and spectral domains.

If all this sounds a bit academic, be assured that on record it is anything but; as crumbling edifices of mealy rhythms slowly pulse into life and swirl around your head like snow storms clashing with a dust devil. Taking sediments of fathom deep static then skimming the best stuff from the top, Jelinek opens through the dampened echoes of 'Moiré (piano & organ)' wherein a slow-motion thrum of spiraling clicks, rustles and analogue tones conspire to give the impression of recondite perspectives that extend well beyond the constituent elements.

Elsewhere, 'Rocky in the Video Age' instills a gratuitously optimistic blush to the aquatic micro-sound ebb, 'Moiré (Strings)' is a perfect companion to Basinski's disintegrating tape archive, whilst 'Them, Their' represents an aural crease so sleight you can only catch its distinctive gleam from the corner of your eye.
items._cn_summary: Jan Jelinek 的这张专辑以极简手法处理六十至七十年代爵士唱片片段，将一秒钟长度的素材反复循环调制，借助听觉领域的莫尔效应使多个相似频率互相干涉叠加，构建出绵密的颗粒感声场。评论指出成品远非学究式的枯燥实验，而是呈现出雪暴裹挟沙尘般的有机听觉体验：钢琴与管风琴片段在缓慢脉动中浮现，《Rocky in the Video Age》注入明亮的水下微声律动，《Moiré (Strings)》与 Basinski 缓慢瓦解的磁带档案遥相呼应，《Them, Their》则以近乎隐形的方式将褶皱藏入混音边缘。整张作品擅长从深厚静默中提取表层精华，把碎片化的爵士沉积物转化为抽象的微观声响雕塑，让极简素材获得远超其本身的纵深感与神秘感。

items.body:
Long considered a diggers holy grail, 'African Skies' is a harp-led weightless jazz masterpiece from early Arkestra member and Chicago legend Kelan Phil Cohran - crucial, life affirming gear that’s compulsory listening for disciples of Sun Ra, Alice Coltrane, Dorothy Ashby, Chicago Underground.

In 1993, decades after his work with Sun Ra and long after he'd carved out a revered solo niche for himself with 'On the Beach' and 'Spanish Suite', Cohran was tapped by Chicago's Adler Planetarium to score a program they called African Skies - designed to reach out to the city's Black neighbourhoods and present the next generation with inspiration and education. Cohran was an obvious choice; he’d been working with young Chicago talent for years, opening the short-lived Afro-Arts Theatre in 1967 and running various educational initiatives for his community, teaching Black history and mentoring fresh talent.

The project aimed to present footage collected from observatories in Africa with music, tasking Cohran with recording suitably cosmic material for the score. Gathering collaborators Oscar Brown III (on string bass, piccolo bass and flute), Aquilla Sadalla (on bass clarinet, guitar, flute and vocals), Josefe Marie Verna (on harp, trombone and flute) and his son Malik Cohran (on guitar, string bass and flute), he set out to put together a kaleidoscopic soundtrack inspired by decades of research into devotional music, African history and archeo-astronomy.  The result is undoubtedly Cohran’s most ethereal suite, lifted to the heavens by his virtuosic performances on harp, trumpet, congas, violin uke, guitar, flute and his "space harp" the frankinphone -  an amplified lamellophone that Cohran designed after studying African instruments like the kalimba. 

Opening with the incendiary harp-led 'Theme', Cohran immediately hits the album's most-loved cue, the 10-minute devotional tour de fource 'White Nile'. Leading with harp, Cohran picks out stars from the wide, open skyline with notes that seem to ricochet off brown's basslines, while Sadalla's voice soars like a comet, heralding brass and woodwind flourishes in the track's jubilant second half. The record's flipside might be even more uplifting. On 'Sahara', each musician follows Cohran's jerky frankinphone phrasing as the band draw tight spirals that Cohran responds to with pitchy fiddle vamps. On 'Kalahari', each member of the quintet plays flute instinctively, coaxing out animalistic resonances, while 'Kilimanjaro' sends us off on a mutable rhythmic showpiece that's guided by the space harp's rhythmelodic clangs and clacks, forming a sturdy backbone for Sadalla's wordless scats.

A stunning set - finally available again for high definition consumption.
items._genre: spiritual jazz / cosmic jazz / harp-led / Afro-futurist / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥传奇竖琴手兼作曲家Kelan Phil Cohran于1993年为Adler天文馆项目录制了这张配乐专辑，将非洲天文影像与宇宙冥想音乐结合。他自创的"frankinphone"（受非洲kalimba启发的放大lamellophone）与竖琴、小号、康加鼓、提琴尤克里里交织，形成漂浮而灵性的音景。五重奏成员在'White Nile''Sahara''Kalahari''Kilimanjaro'等曲目中以竖琴与frankinphone引导，发展出盘旋式的器乐即兴，融合非洲传统节奏、灵性音乐遗绪与天文意象。Sadalla的人声如彗星般飞升，铜管与木管在欢腾的后半段绽放。这张长期被视为挖掘者圣杯的作品以高解析度格式重发，是Sun Ra、Alice Coltrane、芝加哥地下场景追随者的重要文献。

items.body:
Picked up by Ninja Tune after a highly acclaimed release on Smalltown Supersound in 2002, this excellent outfit featured members from the Norwegian jazz, improv and electronics scene to make up what was akin to a Charles Mingus big band for the 23rd century.

"Early this year remarkable reviews began to appear in the British music press for the latest sensations to come out of Scandinavia. There was a difference to many of the other acts earning Norway its reputation at the time, though. Jaga Jazzist is what can only be described as a supergroup. The ten members of the band are also active participants in, Kim Hiorthoy's group, Bobby Hughes Experience, Bugges Wesseltoft, Motorpsycho, Big Bang, Euroboys, Jazzkammer, Biosphere, Supersilent, Alog and Lasse Marhaug, covering every type of music from electronica, nu-jazz and rock. Jaga Jazzist are well known in Norway for contributing to almost every quality Norwegian record released in recent times.

The comparisons reached for by the press were as broad as they get - from Talk Talk, Soft Machine, Eric Satie, John Coltrane and Don Cherry to acts like Aphex Twin, Stereolab, Squarepusher, Isotope 217 and Tortoise. This range sums up the breadth and originality of the group's sound. Jaga Jazzist are indeed a musical one off who’s arsenal includes trumpets, trombone, electric guitar, bass, tuba, two bass clarinets, Fender Rhodes and vibraphone, and it is the mixture of these instruments with a sometimes harsh electronic edge that really makes the music stand out. It is melodic, delicate and subtle but a million miles from wallpaper music. It is music that demands and rewards attention, further proof that you don't have to shout to avoid being lazy chill-out-by-numbers.

The group came to the attention of Ninja Tune who will be releasing their work outside of Norway from now on and while "A Livingroom Hush" garnered critical acclaim , its distribution was patchy. Hence, this re-release, complete with the very odd but very wonderful Monty-Python-on-safari promo video from "Animal Chin".

It's a journey into sounds and moods that manages to sound both classic and contemporary and is an oasis to anyone interested in music which combines iconoclasm with beauty, melody with avant gardism and, in general, a complete lack of interest in anything other than good music."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由十人组成的挪威超级乐团打造，成员横跨爵士、即兴与电子等多个领域。编制罕见而丰富，包含小号、长号、吉他、贝斯、大号、两支低音单簧管、芬达 Rhodes 电钢琴与颤音琴，与电子音色交融，形成既经典又当代的声响。评论将之比作23世纪的Charles Mingus大乐队，跨越从Talk Talk、Eric Satie到Aphex Twin、Tortoise的广泛谱系。音乐旋律细腻敏感，却远离背景音乐的温吞，以安静的方式展现力量。原始版本由小厂牌发行后获得高度评价，但传播渠道有限，此次由Ninja Tune重新发行，使更多听众得以接触这张融合avant-garde美学与精致旋律的作品。

items.body: These releases are not merely containers for music. They are thoughtfully conceived artistic objects that extend, deepen, and enrich the listening experience. They are works meant to be lived with, revisited, displayed, and cherished. Josh Mason‘s Kicking A Dark Horse, the third installment in the label’s FOLIO format, may be the clearest realization yet of that philosophy. A single artistic statement expressed through multiple mediums Kicking A Dark Horse by Josh Mason   One of the enduring questions facing experimental music today is deceptively simple: why release music in physical form at all? In an era where nearly every recording is instantly accessible, what purpose can a tangible object still serve beyond nostalgia? With its FOLIO series, greyfade has been steadily constructing a compelling answer. These releases are not merely containers for music. They are thoughtfully conceived artistic objects that extend, deepen, and enrich the listening experience. They are works meant to be lived with, revisited, displayed, and cherished. Josh Mason‘s Kicking A Dark Horse, the third installment in the label’s FOLIO format, may be the clearest realization yet of that philosophy. At first glance, the project presents itself as two parallel works: a nine-track electronic album and a hardcover book of experimental writing subtitled a nonlinear travelogue of the states of Florida. Yet the more time one spends with the release, the more apparent it becomes that separating the two is impossible. Mason and greyfade are explicit about this. Kicking A Dark Horse is not an album accompanied by a book, nor a book inspired by an album. It is a single artistic statement expressed through multiple mediums. That ambitious premise succeeds because Mason‘s creative approach remains remarkably consistent across both forms. His music and writing are governed by similar principles: discontinuity, recursion, instability, and association. Both resist straightforward narratives. Both reward patience and curiosity. Musically, Kicking A Dark Horse is among the most fascinating electronic releases I have encountered this year. Fragments reappear altered and transformed :: Mason, a Florida-based musician and sound artist whose work spans more than a decade of experimentation with modular synthesis, guitar, and electronics, has built these compositions around a custom modular framework operating on streams of binary data. Rather than pursuing total control over the system, he intentionally embraces its resistance. Sequences drift apart. Rhythms fall out of alignment. Fragments reappear altered and transformed. The distinction Mason draws between randomness and chaos is essential to understanding the album’s achievement. These pieces never feel arbitrary. There is always a hidden logic at work beneath the surface. The music evolves organically, generating structures that seem to emerge naturally rather than being imposed from above. The opening “Unincorporated Community Fight Song” immediately establishes this unique language. Softly bubbling textures, weathered tones, and subtle rhythmic instabilities create an atmosphere that feels unmistakably tied to place. Unlike much contemporary ambient music, which often favors generalized moods and placeless serenity, Mason‘s work is rooted in specific geography. These sounds feel lived-in. They carry traces of highways, motel signs, humid evenings, forgotten parking lots, and stretches of coastline. Florida itself becomes a character throughout the work :: Yet this is not a romanticized portrait. Mason captures something more complex and compelling. His Florida is beautiful, strange, fragile, and occasionally unsettling. The album’s textures often feel weathered by heat and time. Dusty clicks, degraded signals, phase-shifting artifacts, and low-resolution fragments drift through the mix like half-remembered memories. What makes the record so rewarding is the balance between experimentation and emotional resonance. It would be easy for a project built around technical systems and conceptual frameworks to become academic. Instead, Kicking A Dark Horse remains deeply human. Tracks such as “Would Go” and “Repair 22,000,000” reveal a remarkable sensitivity to pacing and atmosphere. Sounds emerge slowly, hover briefly, then dissolve before fully resolving. Harmonic fragments appear like distant landmarks glimpsed through fog. Nothing is overstated. Nothing feels forced. Mason‘s live performance approach contributes significantly to this sense of vitality. Rather than assembling pieces through meticulous post-production alone, he conducts the system in real time, manually shifting divisions, guiding sequences, and responding to emergent behaviors as they occur. The resulting music feels alive. One can hear the delicate balancing act taking place, as though numerous independent systems are simultaneously threatening to drift apart while somehow remaining connected. The companion text extends these ideas beautifully. Reading while listening creates an experience unlike any traditional album or book. Timelines collapse. Memories blur. Documentary details coexist with apparent invention. Meaning emerges through accumulation rather than explanation. The effect is profoundly immersive :: Equally impressive is the care with which greyfade has realized the physical object itself. The FOLIO format continues to demonstrate why the label has become one of the most exciting homes for contemporary experimental music. The linen hardcover presentation, thoughtful design, and integration of text and sound transform the release into something far more substantial than a conventional album package. In many ways, greyfade is quietly redefining what a record label can be. Their releases feel less like products and more like complete artistic ecosystems. Every aspect, from mastering and design to sequencing and physical presentation, contributes to a unified vision. These are objects intended not simply to be consumed but to be kept. Kicking A Dark Horse stands among the strongest examples of that philosophy. It is intellectually ambitious without becoming inaccessible. It is experimental without sacrificing emotional depth. It rewards close listening while remaining inviting and endlessly replayable. Josh Mason has created something rare: a work that feels simultaneously personal and expansive, carefully structured yet constantly surprising. Together with greyfade‘s extraordinary presentation, the result is more than an album and more than a book. It is an experience. Kicking A Dark Horse is available on greyfade. items.body:
Over the course of the last decade, the group أحمد [Ahmed] has carved out a distinctive approach to the jazz canon through their tireless exploration of the music of Ahmed Abdul-Malik. Mining Abdul-Malik’s compositions and his incorporation of non-Western microtonality into the jazz vocabulary, pianist Pat Thomas, alto saxophone player Seymour Wright, bassist Joel Grip, and drummer Antonin Gerbal have done more than reinterpretation. They have used the music as a foundation for both immersion and subversion of the way that the standard jazz quartet functions within post-bop structures. For last year’s Sama'a (Audition), they went into the studio for an expansive refraction of Abdul-Malik’s Jazz Sahara. During that same session, the four took a slight detour to record Play Monk, a dive into deconstructions of six pieces by Thelonious Monk, all but one of which he recorded in the late 1950s when Abdul-Malik was part of his group. أحمد [Ahmed] has incorporated Monk tunes into their live sets but this is the first time they have focused on his tunes on a recording.

While Thomas, Wright, Grip, and Gerbal have not altered their strategies in the switch of source material, there is one significant shift in the way one listens to this music. A quick search returns no other versions of Abdul-Malik’s pieces other than those recorded by the composer or أحمد [Ahmed] whereas Monk’s “Epistrophy” or “’Round Midnight” have hundreds. Even a less well-known piece like “Oska T” has dozens. Because the pieces covered are so well known, their teasing apart and restructuring of the underlying thematic kernels are more readily evident. Over two CDs, the quartet digs in, with improvisations that range between 20 and 30 minutes with the exception of a seven-minute extrapolation of “Epistrophy.” These extended explorations allow the group to excavate the forms with a focused patience, zeroing in on and elucidating microscopic details, extricating them into the fundamental elements of penetrating improvisations.

The first phrases of the opening “Bye-ya / Epistrophy” provide a glimpse of what is to come. Bass and piano circle around the theme and Gerbal’s lithe drumming circles up to drive momentum. Wright’s stabbing alto picks apart the melody and the four launch off on a circuitous inquiry, dismantling Monk’s tune into its constituent fragments and then reassembling them with constructivist abstraction. Each of the four seize on elements of the underlying piece, playing them off of each other with unwavering resolve, an approach the group continues to advance in their sweeping live sets. There is an insistent intensity as Wright’s notes pick and prod at Thomas’ skewed clusters, Grip’s free walking lines, and Gerbal’s churning free rhythms. Shards of “Epistrophy” are introduced into the mix by Grip and Thomas, slowly accruing with multifaceted erudition.

The group continues to subvert expectations with “Friday the Thirteenth” as Thomas insistently repeats the first phrase of the tune against Grip’s growling arco inversions. Wright’s keypad pops and Gerbal’s open percussion build momentum and Wright unleashes spattered honks that open into a collective four-part splintering of the theme, picking it apart and recasting it with angular exactitude, building density and intensity over the course of the sweeping 26-minute improvisation. “’Round Midnight” gets a relatively straightforward introduction with Wright intoning the theme over sinuous bass and cymbal splashes. Thomas’ spare chords enter as the quartet dynamically transposes the constituent parts of the piece with imperturbable resolution resolving with the riveting cycling hushed snare abrasions that brings the piece to a close.

A seven-minute scorching, stuttering run through “Epistrophy” serves as an interlude to an abstracted, cascading reading of “Evidence” which takes Monk’s stop-start theme and explodes it with relentless, spiraled piano phrases and the hurtling momentum of bass and drums driving Wright’s coruscating alto which prods and jabs with spiky dexterity. The 30-minute improvisation is an engulfing exemplification of unflagging invention. Monk’s “Oska T.,” structured around an obsessively cyclical riff, is a fitting conclusion to the release. The quartet slows things down to a free shuffle with bass and alto arcing over the mutable pulse of piano and drums. The four players adroitly weave their lines in and out of the collective undercurrent with indefatigable ingenuity. While others have dedicated themselves to the reinterpretation of the music of Thelonious Monk, أحمد [Ahmed]’s Play Monk is distinctive in its mastery, fully absorbing his music into the collective rigor and artistry of this singular ensemble.

items._cn_summary: 这支由钢琴Pat Thomas、高音萨克斯Seymour Wright、贝斯Joel Grip和鼓Antonin Gerbal组成的四人乐团，长期深耕低音提琴手Ahmed Abdul-Malik的音乐遗产，将其作品中非西方微分音元素融入爵士语汇。他们不仅重新诠释，更以此为基础对后波普标准四重奏范式进行沉浸与颠覆。这张专辑将焦点从Abdul-Malik转向Thelonious Monk，拆解其六首作品，其中五首录制于Abdul-Malik参与其乐队的1950年代末。由于Monk曲目有大量参照版本，乐团对这些旋律内核的拆解与重构显得格外清晰。两张CD中，多数即兴段落长达20至30分钟，以耐心与专注挖掘作品结构，将碎片以构成主义抽象手法重新拼贴。Wright尖锐的高音萨克斯挑拨Thomas扭曲的音簇，Grip自由行走的低音线与Gerbal翻腾的自由节拍持续碰撞，Monk主题在解构中逐渐浮现。

items.body: Machinefabriek is no stranger to the compilation format. One of the earliest such efforts, 2007’s two-disc Weleer, collected the best tracks from over 30 CD3″s. At the time, it was considered to be a perfect entry point into the work of a relatively new artist. Two decades later, Rutger Zuydervelt continues to be prolific ~ multiple releases have already appeared in the wake of Samen ~ while distinguishing himself as the rare artist whose productivity does not result in a dulling of quality. Samen contains stray tracks from the past decade, originally available on lathe cut, business card, cassette, 7″, digital, split release and other compilations. Again, this is a fine introduction to the world of Machinefabriek, but not a complete one, as the composer’s field has expanded greatly in the course of his career, touching upon nearly every genre we cover and most recently concentrating on productions for theatre and dance. The album also has a great sense of flow, as Machinefabriek sequences these pieces in a way that makes sense rather than presenting them in release order. The stomping “Sidder,” offset by kind flute, leads off the set, but other tracks from this release appear in the five, nine and twelve spots. The combination of aggression and tenderness is a staple for Zuydervelt, whose sonic curiosity results in instinctive juxtapositions. One of the most recent cuts, last year’s “Verpulver,” blends ambience, drone and crunchy, non-club beats. “Sound and Stone (Part 7)” is built on the sound stones of Hannes and Klaus Fessmann; the track fits just as well here as it did among the other eight parts, all by different artists. “As Much As It Is Worth,” composed for a dance performance by Marta + Kim, is a window into Zuydervelt’s recent activities. An electronic pulse provides the invitation to move, albeit slowly and thoughtfully, an alternative to the club. With a decade worth of tracks to choose from, even outliers such as “Melodrama 1 and 2” seem right at home on Samen, as if composed intentionally for this set. Nestled snugly in the electronic section of the compilation, “Studying Space” topples first into density, then into filament, setting up the third Zinder track, whose timbre explains its separation from “Sidder.” Assertive beats meet placid, wordless vocals, while the flute vanishes. Longtime readers may recall Angry Ambient Artists on the Forwind imprint, which we reviewed a decade ago. “Graniet” still sounds new, although we still insist that angry ambience (even when it contains chimes) is no longer ambience, but drone or noise. The chimes of “Graniet” are tonally connected to the organ of “Merg;” we can imagine how much fun it must have been to put this 17-piece puzzle together. Zuydervelt grows reflective on “Waqur,” from To Yemen With Love, setting up the sprawling, 16:27 “Verlat,” wisely placed at the end, a long, centering denouement. No compilation is sufficient to convey all of the sides of Machinefabriek ~ one notable omission here, albeit understandable for tonal purposes, is his playful, club-friendly side, heard on releases such as Hinkelstap. We’d love to hear a second compilation of this type, and even ~ dare we ask? ~ a greatest hits album. The challenge would be in the compiling, as the artist has already provided so many transcendent moments over the years that it would be nearly impossible to narrow them down. Keep them coming, we say; we’ll be listening to every one. (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: Machinefabriek（机器工厂）的主创Rutger Zuydervelt精选了过去十年间散布于各处的零散作品，重新编排成这张合辑。这些曲目最初以多种极小规模的实体形式发行——黑胶切割、卡片碟、磁带、七寸、数字等——跨度从2007年的早期两碟合辑至今，横跨二十年。Zuydervelt以高产出著称，却少有质量滑坡，专辑以'Sidder'开篇，侵略性的节奏与柔和长笛形成对比，随后穿插安排各时期作品，营造出内在逻辑而非按发行时序的聆听体验。专辑涵盖氛围、嗡鸣、噪音颗粒、电子脉冲、非俱乐部节拍等多种手法，横跨舞蹈配乐、声音石采样等合作项目，展现了作曲家长达二十年的田野扩展，从极简声响雕刻到剧场与舞蹈制作均有涉足。

items.body: Imaginary not real In a world that has fallen from grace And in the park, the rush begins to make its way down Down, down he goes After more than a decade as DRIFT., Nathalia Bruno has pushed the project into a new, harder shape. The solitary synth work of earlier releases has given way to a full-band attack, with Max Oscarnold on guitar, Finn Kidd on drums, and Lucy Lucifer on keys joining Bruno for Violence For Your Furs, out September 16 via God Unknown Records. The shift suits her: the music still carries her familiar chill, but now it comes dressed in glam-goth sleaze, rock n roll cabaret menace, and the charged feeling of a London night already halfway off the rails. Rough Rider is the record’s streetlamp confession, a nasty little ride through Kingsland Road where romance has been mugged and left arguing with itself. Bruno sings as if she has spent the afternoon listening through walls, picking up curses, sirens, and the burden of the Ten of Wands card. “There’s a world outside your door” hits as a dare from someone who has seen what waits there and still reaches for the handle. The band plays with the cruel economy of people who know excess works best with a switchblade tucked under the coat. Oscarnold’s guitar scratches at the corners, Kidd’s drums shove the song forward with alley-cat impatience, and Lucifer’s keys give the scene a cabaret stink, part cheap perfume, part electrical burn. Bruno sits above it all with a delivery that calls up Alan Vega, Anne Clark, Fad Gadget, hanging out at an after-hours where somebody has put Suicide on repeat and locked the exits. Those names are coordinates, useful because they sketch the room: black leather humour, broken drum-machine discipline, art-school dread, and the blessed naïveté of rock still thinking salvation might be hidden in volume. The song’s lyrics are chock full of bodies, cops, masks, vomit, bikes, glass, meat, overdose; lovely stuff, because pop music has spent too many years selling self-help lotion to people who need a brick hurled through their window. DRIFT. gives us “cold country” and “hope country” as two names for the same cracked pavement, and the trick is that both feel true. Every generation gets told it lives with promise, then spends the night finding out that promise has a boot on its throat. The video, with Bruno performing behind wet glass, pushes the song deeper into that aquarium panic, as though we are watching a nightclub priestess from the wrong side of the tank. She appears trapped, blurred, touchable and unreachable at once, making theatre out of distance while keeping pain clear of boutique gloom. The images smear, the song stalks, and the quartet sounds thrilled by its own bad news. You can almost smell beer, rainwater, burnt cable, and an extinguished clove cigarette. Watch the video for Rough Rider below: Rough Rider belongs to the tradition of songs that know the city can crack jokes while bleeding and pass for hard while begging somebody, anybody, to notice the damage. DRIFT. has found a new body for Bruno’s private apocalypse. Listen to Rough Rider below and pre-order Violence For Your Furs here. Violence For Your Furs by DRIFT. items._cn_summary: DRIFT. 经历十余年单人合成器项目后，转型为四人乐队编制，发行专辑《Violence For Your Furs》。吉他、鼓、键盘的加入让早期冰冷的合成器声响扩展为更具攻击性的乐队整体表达，融合华丽哥特、摇滚卡巴莱与合成朋克的语汇。单曲《Rough Rider》以伦敦Kingsland Road街景为底色，歌词堆砌身体、警察、面具、呕吐、玻璃等粗粝意象，挑战流行乐长久以来的自愈式抒情。Bruno的演唱令人联想到Alan Vega、Anne Clarke与Suicide的余绪，冷峻而带有距离感。MV中她隔着湿玻璃表演，制造出水族馆式的隔绝与窥视氛围，强化了歌曲中城市既是冷酷笑话又是求救信号的二元张力。专辑由独立厂牌God Unknown Records发行，保留了地下场景特有的粗粝质感。

items.body:
Ocean Cage is a live recording of Tianzhuo Chen and Siko Setyanto’s performance Moyang & Seaman – a stage work that evolved from the immersive theatre performance project Ocean Cage, sharing the same title.

"Directed by Tianzhuo Chen, aka Asiandopeboys, the immersive performance Ocean Cage merges scenography, installation, choreography, and live music into a unified whole. Inspired by the complex whaling traditions in Lamalera, an Indonesian village that preservers ritualised whaling practices and ancestral beliefs, the work unfolds through interconnected trinities – Moyang (ancestor), Lera Wulan (god), and Seaman – all incarnated by Siko Setyanto. It tells a porous story of unlocking the cage of the ocean: receiving ancestral blessing while becoming entangled with misjudgement, misunderstanding, ecological grief, and temporal displacement, until the sacrifice and life cycles move toward equilibrium.

Evolving from this larger narration, Moyang 先祖 & Seaman 漁 師 shifts into a frontal, meditative dialogues between ancestor and seaman. Inspired by Japanese Noh theatre and deeply rooted in Nusantara traditions, the performance integrates music, dance, and stage art into a mutable and fluid process, continuing to explore ancestral presences, cyclical time, and spiritual transformation.

The album features music by KADAPAT and Nova Ruth, interwoven with Siko Setyanto’s narrations and monologues. KADAPAT’s electronic-gamelan practice moves through interlocking rhythm and cyclical time structures, extending asymmetrical Balinese ancestral yet modern sonic with digital signal. Bamboo and metal, folk and sacred, horizontal and vertical forces collide and co-exist, forming layered pulses that shift and reform in motion.

As Siko beautifully summarises the creative synergy in Ocean Cage/Moyang & Seaman: “Being on stage is like sailing together into the unknown – embracing every mystery that comes our way.” The album of Ocean Cage also records the reciprocal, communal, improvisational, polymetric, and relational collaborations among Nova Ruth, Siko Setyanto, KADAPAT and Tianzhuo Chen. No role is fixed; no expression remains confined to its original context. In this sense, Ocean Cage becomes an assembled living being."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自陈天灼与Siko Setyanto的沉浸式剧场演出《Ocean Cage》及由此衍生的舞台作品《Moyang & Seaman》，是对现场表演的录音呈现。音乐部分由KADAPT与Nova Ruth合作完成，将电子加美兰的实践与Siko的念白独白交织在一起。KADAPT的作品运用互锁节奏与循环时间结构，以数字信号延伸巴厘岛传统声响，竹制与金属器乐、世俗与神圣、水平与垂直的力在其中碰撞共存，形成层叠脉动并在运动中不断重构变形。专辑受印尼Lamalera村庄捕鲸传统与日本能剧启发，融合Nusantara传统音乐、舞蹈与舞台艺术，探讨祖灵在场、循环时间与精神转化等主题。整体呈现一种跨媒介、跨文化的协作式创作，没有固定角色与单一表达边界，是一次关于活态传统与当代声音交融的探索。

items.body:
‘ИМА (Ima)’ is a work by KiMiMi, the solo project of a musician Shin-ya Ohno, which captures the layers of time and the presence of people inhabiting ‘Arimasuton Building’―a self-built structure created over 20 years by architect Keisuke Oka, located in Mita, Tokyo, and reconstructs them into music.

"A multi-instrumentalist who masterfully handles a diverse range of instruments, with the gaida (an ancestor of the bagpipes) – which he studied in Bulgaria – at the core of his sound, KiMiMi has previously brought traces of daily life and folk melodies recorded during his travels back to the scale of home recording, weaving fantastical folk soundscapes through cassette tape works and stage music.

Alongside his musical activities, he has participated in the construction work for ‘Arimasuton Building’, recording the sounds of hammers and steel beams echoing on site, lunchtime chatter, the melodies of instruments played by others, and the sound of cars passing by. From the end of 2022, a zine titled ‘Monthly Arimasuton Building Urimasu’, based on this construction project, was launched. KiMiMi incorporates these recordings into the musical works he contributes to each issue, layering sounds from live instruments―including the gaida, accordion, guitar, flute, ukulele, piano, foot-pump organ, melodica and xylophone―alongside a few synthesiser tones, to shape a soundscape imbued with the humidity and breath of the site.

KiMiMi’s creative process is characterised not by planned construction, but by an attitude of entrusting the work to chance, intuition and the passage of time. Fragmented recordings are layered, set aside for a time, and then unearthed again. Through this repetition, the music naturally takes shape. This resonates perfectly with the process of ‘Arimasuton Building’, which was built up improvisationally, layer by layer, without any pre-prepared blueprints.

‘ИМА (Ima)’ marks the current stage of KiMiMi’s sonic journey and represents an attempt to gracefully transcend the boundaries between architecture and music, documentation and creation, and the individual and the community. The clamour of the city, the tranquillity of manual labour, laughter, and every sound resonating at the Arimasuton Building site blend with KiMiMi’s music, reflecting the very passage of time in which people live."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以建筑师冈启介在东京三田耗时二十年亲手建造的「Arimasuton大楼」为核心素材来源。音乐人KiMiMi（大野真也）长期参与该建筑的施工过程，将工地的锤击声、钢梁回响、午休闲谈、过往车辆声与其他乐手的演奏一并收录，再与盖达（保加利亚风笛祖先）、手风琴、吉他、长笛、钢琴、脚踏风琴、口风琴、木琴等原声乐器及少量合成器音色层层叠加，形成带有湿度与呼吸感的音景。创作不依赖预设蓝图，而是将碎片化的录音反复搁置、再挖掘，让时间与直觉自然塑形。这种将建筑、劳动、社区声响转化为音乐的方法，模糊了档案记录与艺术创作之间的边界。

items.body:
Hanoi-based artist Trần Uy Đức, who's been spotted alongside Vietnamese avant-garde collective Rắn Cạp Đuôi, arrives on Lolina's Relaxin imprint with 'ByyShh', a set of warped pop experiments, casual electro abstractions and glitched-out sketches that'll make perfect sense if yr into Voice Actor, LA Timpa or even Tujiko Noriko.

There's no real sense of continuity to 'ByyShh', and that's why it's so refreshing. Đức has been releasing material since 2018, working as a video artist and a designer as well as putting together wonky deployments like 2021's noise-caked 'Came' and 2024's curiously poppy 'It Whims'. 'ByyShh' is his most high profile release yet and straddles the length and breadth of his output, bounding from idea to idea with a relentless level of engagement. Specific songs aren't overworked, they're dubbed sketchily - for posterity, more than anything - before Đức moves onto the next. Opener 'Dessert', for example, is a jerky set of guitar riffs and ring modulated belches that Đức arranges into a jaunty march, while 'Play With Me (Deep Down It’s So Hard)' is sci-fi R&B that sounds as if Timbaland was making a DIY melt movie soundtrack in 1982.

From moment to moment, Đức sounds as if he's flushing out his brain of ideas that have been marinating for decades. The surprisingly catchy 'Do It' lands somewhere between Enya's 'Orinoco Flow' and Daniel Johnson if someone had gifted him a voice modulator, and upfront single 'Like a Star' is a dembow banger attacked by an electric razor and a tape speed dial, slowing up and speeding up seemingly randomly while an incessant buzz takes the place of a lead synth. It's relentlessly outlandish, erratic material - perfectly at home on Relaxin, then.
items._cn_summary: 河内艺术家Trần Uy Đức在Lolina旗下的Relaxin厂牌发表专辑，将扭曲的流行构想、电子抽象片段与故障化的声音速写并置一炉。整张专辑缺乏统一的连续性，反而成为其新鲜之处——作品如同一本不被反复打磨的速写簿，每首歌都在想法成形之初便匆匆封存，迅速转向下一个。开场曲以断断续续的吉他riff与环形调制构成怪诞进行曲，另有作品将Timbaland的R&B置于1982年DIY磁带拼贴的语境之中重构；部分曲目在Enya式旋律与人声调制器的扭曲之间游走，另一些则以电剃刀般的嘶响替代合成器主旋律，速度在快慢之间随机跳脱。这种不断闪烁的、难以归类的创作状态，将多年积压的碎片式灵感倾泻而出，呈现出高度自由且持续外延的声响实验面貌。

If you'd only heard 'Sommer Im Pfirsichhain' and 'Aprilnacht', the first two parts of Christian Schoppik and Katie Rich's seasonal quadrilogy, 'Geträumt hab ich vom Martinszug' (I dreamed about the St. Martin's Day procession
items.body:
Originally released in 2016, German "dark folk" duo Brannten Schnüre's third album is even more atmospheric than its predecessors, a vision of the Bavarian winter that follows the St. Martin's Day procession - something like Bonfire Night muddled with Halloween, basically.

If you'd only heard 'Sommer Im Pfirsichhain' and 'Aprilnacht', the first two parts of Christian Schoppik and Katie Rich's seasonal quadrilogy, 'Geträumt hab ich vom Martinszug' (I dreamed about the St. Martin's Day procession) might come as a surprise. Here, Schoppik works into his samples and instrumental takes even more, sometimes leaving just faint traces of music in a sea of drones, glitches and ghost traces. It's like listening to sequence of inversions at first, with backmasked vocals and incomprehensible instrumentation: head over to the Caretaker-like 'Da Unten Leuchten Wir', or the noise-caked freeform lullaby 'Unser Zug Führt Durch Die Stadt'. If it's music that's supposed to represent a dream of St. Martin's Day, rather than the even itself, it makes perfect sense.

To an outsider, it's a strange event. There's a parade of children with homemade paper lanterns that usually begins at a local church and is sometimes led by a person dressed in Roman gear, then there's a bonfire and a festive meal that doesn't look that different from a Thanksgiving spread. Schoppik and Rich's eccentric songs - like the organ-led 'Damit Die Zähne Wieder Glänzen' - are peppered between haunted, scene-setting hypnagogic moments, like the woozed 'Lösche Aus Dein Licht' or the genius 'Rote, Gelbe, Grüne, Blaue', five-and-a-half-minutes of downsampled gurgles, decelerated accordion gusts and distant footsteps. Properly good stuff - if you enjoyed Schoppik and Rich's 2022 Freundliche Kreisel album, or Schoppik's solo material as Läuten der Seele, this'll be essential listening.
items._genre: dark folk / experimental / drone / glitch / ambient
items._cn_summary: 德国二人组Brannten Schnüre的第三张专辑延续四季四部曲主题，以圣马丁节游行日为背景，将巴伐利亚冬日氛围转化为极度实验化的声响景观。Schoppik在采样与器乐编制中大幅留白，音乐常隐没于无人机、失真残响与幽灵般的声音痕迹之间，背向掩声与不可辨识的器乐编排营造出梦境般的倒置感。作品中游走于催眠式的场景描绘与怪异的歌曲形态之间，如降采样咕噜声、减速手风风声、远处脚步声的拼贴，以及风琴主导的仪式感段落。评论将其与Caretaker的破碎美学相提并论，对喜爱其前作与Schoppik个人项目的听众而言是不可错过的关键作品。

items.body:
DAF legend & EBM pioneer Robert Görl tightens his bonds with OG Dorian Gray DJ, Sylvie Marks, on a sinuous debut duo LP referencing their illustrious history of Teutonic meat motors.

‘Dark Silver Moon Light’ binds the German club mavericks’ respective ideas on EBM, post-punk, industrial, and techno, thru 10 taut synth + sequencer workouts largely defined by motorik momentum and melancholic air which guides them to brooding arp hymns and side quests into slower kraut sleaze. Some six years in the works, it effectively picks up where Robert & Sylvie left off with their completion and release of DAF’s final album, ‘Nur Noch Einer’ (2021), following the passing of his bandmate Gabi Delgado (1958-2020), with Sylvie ideally helping to fill Gabi’s role as spiritual spur to her pal.

Sylvie’s sharp DJ and club instincts, honed since her days as the first and only female DJ at Frankfurt’s resoundingly influential Dorian Gray club since the ‘90s, surely help keep Robert’s iconic sequences and steel-tipped drums on course for bodies in motion. It’s all maybe not as fierce as early DAF, but is still athletically toned and smacks below the belt on the fanged aces ‘Falscher Ton’ and ‘Wir brechen aus’, but the best bits more clearly project an air of restless gloom. From the shark-eyed swagger of ‘So wie Du bist’, thru a classy mid-section spanning the tortured troubadour turn of ‘Don’t Stay at Home’, a razor-riding title tune, and standout of Gerald Donald-esque finesse on ‘Der Fluss’, to the kerb-crawl cruise of ‘Es int die zu spät’, DAF’s legacy is in safe hands here.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国电子音乐传奇人物Robert Görl与资深DJ Sylvie Marks的首张合作全长专辑，融合了EBM、后朋克、工业与电子的多重脉络。制作历时六年，承接二人此前合作完成DAF遗作《Nur Noch Einer》的线索，Sylvie填补了已故搭档Gabi Delgado所留下的精神推动者角色。整张作品以紧凑的合成器与音序器编排为核心，motorik节奏驱动贯穿始终，旋律线条带着沉思与阴郁的气质。曲目中既有如《Falscher Ton》与《Wir brechen aus》般尖锐锋利的俱乐部冲击，也有《Der Fluss》这类带有Gerald Donald式精致触感的暗流作品，以及《Es int die zu spät》般的缓慢推进段落。DAF的遗产在这张专辑中得到了沉稳而具延续性的继承，节奏与情绪的掌控展现出对舞池本能的深刻理解。

items.body:
Indonesian instrument-builder and folk mutator Johanes “Mo’ong” Santoso Pribadi meets wildman Shigeru Ishihara (aka Scotch Rolex) on a 2nd Takkak Takkak screwball for Nyege Nyege Tapes, tipped FFO Gabber Modus Operandi, Hulubalang, Raja Kirik, Lord Spikeheart.

One up to the duo’s eponymous debut of 2024, the possessed tempest of ‘Abu’ opens wormhole portals to fantasy dimensions triangulated with frightening vibrancy. The 40 minute trip goes hard into sweltering zones where ancient folk rituals encounter modern technology and psyches, replete with shifting atmospheric conditions and febrile oneiric logic. The results are a hyperrealistic projection of heck, taking listeners by the scruff of the neck and plunging them into an anomalous sort of fantasy island or parallel world teeming with phosphorescent life, from the animalcule level to the metaphysical. 

The ceremonial atmosphere of opening track 'Hai no uta' mixes Javanese gong with flute blasts  interspersed with unsettling electronic vibrations, while the title track takes shape through hoarse chants and a cocktail of rhythms: tuned, gamelan-like resonances through ordered electro-plated taiko structures, evolving into fractured free improv and syrupy drone metal. The album keeps shifting through these tense ceremonial sounds and hard dance textures, inviting heavy electronic kicks into the mannered mass of flutes and metallophone, matching acoustic instrumentation with carnivalesque synths and hardstyle rhythms.

Get your imaginary jabs in: it’s wild out there.
items._genre: experimental / world music / electronic / folk fusion
items._cn_summary: 印尼乐器制造者与即兴音乐人合作的第二张专辑，将爪哇传统民间仪式声响与现代电子技术深度融合。开场曲将爪哇铜锣与笛声交织，辅以不安的电子振动；同名曲在沙哑吟唱中展开，经过加美兰调律的共振结构，演变为碎裂的自由即兴与黏稠的 drone metal。全长四十分钟的氛围不断在仪式感声响与硬核舞曲质感之间切换，笛声与金属打击乐器与 carnival 合成器、硬派电子节拍相互碰撞。整体构建了一个充满磷光生命的异次元幻境，将古老民俗仪式的精神性注入当代实验电子语境，呈现出独特的跨文化声音想象。

items.body:
Really feeling this trippy acid treat by a one-of-a-kind Lolina; her 10th solo album since the last Hype Williams drop with Dean Blunt in the early 2010s, and typically riddled with low-key mischievous slants on mutant dance-pop, as heard in her regular midweek club night at ace London venue, Spanners.

Chasing up her trip-hop tinted LP ‘Unrecognisable’ (2024), and a mix CD as Balmainjeans repping her club night ‘Distressed’, Lolina plays to an ideally unpredictable form with a shift into acid pop on ‘Monopoly of Mistakes’; featuring eleven concentrated formulations of dry drum machines x tweakiest 303 gunk gilded with those vocals that keep us coming back. The combo of silver box x slanted vox finds the DIY prism-pusher bending timelines thru lo-fi indie-pop with sound system steppas, basement noise, cold wave and free party acid tekno, but never quite settling into any one style.

Maintaining her mutable range of variations within a theme, Monopoly of Mistakes really catches our breath with the way Lolina turns a paucity of ingredients into a dead satisfying thing. Whether commanding the 303 to the beat-less abstraction ‘Border Beach’ or alloying with wooziest keys and steppas fizz on ‘The Mercenaries’, or going deep into the lushest wormhole on the titular, 7 minute standout, her min-to-max sense of economy is key to this LP’s appeal. It’s there in the piquant synth-pop of ‘Menace’ and ‘Everlasting’ - think Wee Papa Girl Rappers via Dave Ball at John T. Gast’s - and calling to mind a lost SOPHIE x EVOL gem in ’Stand Off’. But it’s also finely measured with an utterly gorgeous new age miniature harking to classic Hype Williams on ‘Welcome to the Drift of Whats Already Begun’, and of course the zinging closer ‘Penalty’, where zippiest ‘80s french cold wave meets AFXian harmony and a sort of Dopplereffektish science-lab engineering in a chef’s kiss demo of the extended melodic wooo that sets all her work apart.

Best believe it’s fully distinctive, addictive gear.
items._genre: acid / experimental electronic / mutant pop / cold wave / lo-fi indie-pop
items._cn_summary: Lolina第十张个人专辑转向酸涩流行路线，以十一种浓缩配方展开：干涩鼓机与极端303酸线交织，辅以人声穿透其中。专辑在lo-fi独立流行、声音系统节奏、地下室噪音、冷浪潮与自由派对酸 techno之间自由游走，从不固定于任何单一风格。她以极少素材构建丰富层次的能力贯穿始终——无论是无节拍抽象小品、七分钟迷幻深潜，还是合成器流行短曲，均展现从极简到极繁的经济感。部分作品呼应新世纪冥想气质，末曲则以八十年代法国冷浪潮碰撞AFX式和声与实验合成器工程，收束于一段悠长迷醉旋律。整体延续其可变且难以归类的创作脉络，独立厂牌发行，具有高度辨识度。

items.body:
Essential listening FFO Time Is Away, Jon Collin or the 'Bagpuss' soundtrack, Rory Salter, aka Malvern Brume, confronts cutesy British folk nostalgia on 'For Red Riverbank', using 'The Wind in the Willows' references, sobering newsreel snippets and straight-to-tape acoustic jams to develop a faded image of labour inequality.

Nostalgia is supposed to be digestible - a cultural banana that gives the mind all familiarity without friction. But munch on the same gear for too long and it starts to cause irritation; it's hard not to notice, for example, that the prim Ghost Box-style Gen Z hauntology has reached its logical conclusion. Whatever it was saying about the UK's welfare-era lost futures has not only been photocopied half to death, but it's also been added to the slop machine, spat out as empty "content" that's almost hypnotically nauseating - especially when you consider the state of welfare in 2026. Thankfully, we're not the only people to have noticed; Salter takes aim at the romance of British folk culture on his proper The Sprigs debut, using a framework we'll all be familiar with - Kenneth Grahame's Edwardian children's classic 'The Wind in the Willows'. It's important to note that the book was already steeped in nostalgia when it was first published back in 1908, a reflection on nature in the face of mass industrialization, as the affordable Ford Model T was beginning to appear on roads for the first time. So it's a more complex reference than you might initially figure, and Salter uses this backdrop to root his investigation of British labour history and the very meaning of tradition.

We've all heard remnants of folk music vibrate through the collective consciousness over the years, not least in the wake of the New Weird America movement of the early '00s. And Salter's awareness of these sounds and the perpetual churn that followed is crucial; he doesn't subvert them as such, but repurposes them, hitting on themes and sequences that connect us to the country's soil and textures that help to rub away some of nostalgia's entrancing sparkle. The 12-minute opener 'come along, back home' sounds at first like an old protestant hymn being bellowed through broken pipes and Salter keeps scraping away at history, collaging textured environmental loops with simplistic, almost naive folk songs, peculiar resonances and, occasionally, what sounds like an old recorder. And it's the back-and-forth between gravelly noise and nostalgic naivety that makes 'For Red Riverbank' so inviting. The short, sharp 'Ratty & the moles get to work' is just as jolly as its title, sounding as brittle and evocative as Sandra Kerr and John Faulkner's fluttered folk songs that lifted Oliver Postgate's 'Bagpuss'.

And Salter doesn't just look back through rose-tinted spectacles, he juxtaposes these evocative sounds with sobering recordings of newsreaders, politicians and union leaders, who complete a quite genuine picture of the recent past. Like George Eliot's Middlemarch, that imagined a fictional Midlands town four decades prior to its writing, the inviting idealized setting was a Trojan horse for Eliot's real theme: the 1832 Reform Act that upended the electoral system. Salter employs the same sleight of hand, introducing us to a world we know and love before drip, drip, dripping the politics we so desperately need.
items._genre: experimental folk / hauntology / sound collage / lo-fi acoustic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以肯尼斯·格雷厄姆的《柳林风声》为框架，通过磁带直录原声民谣、环境音循环与新闻录音片段的拼贴，构建出一幅关于英国劳动历史的褪色图景。作者并非简单怀旧，而是借助早已承载怀旧情绪的文本，质疑英国民间文化中浪漫化的传统叙事。专辑将破碎的赞美诗质感、粗糙的噪音层叠与天真质朴的民谣旋律并置，并以政客、工会领袖和播音员的真实录音片段形成对照，在怀旧的糖衣下撕开劳工不平等的裂痕。整体手法介于田野录音与磁带音乐之间，文本层次丰富，声音考古式的挖掘赋予其超越常规民谣的厚度。

items.body:
Real heart-stopping, life-affirming, almost indescribably beautiful posthumous album featuring (for the first time) vocal works by beloved, dearly departed, Ethiopian nun and now-legendary pianist/composer Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru, room recorded straight to tape between 1977-1985, sounds of life just about audible in the background. Almost had an out of body experience listening to it the other night - just a perfect, 10/10 album.

’Souvenirs’ is an intimate self-portrait written, recorded and compiled by the late Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru; a classically-trained pianist turned nun, whose singular style of jazz and blues-inflected composition and performance became globally renowned in her latter years via reissues and compilations reaching as far back as the 1960s, namely the ‘Éthiopiques 21: Piano Solo’ CD and a much-prized eponymous set in 2016. At the age of 99, Emahoy passed away in Jerusalem last year, whilst planning towards this first ever showcase of her vocals - which have never appeared on her purely piano-based recordings until now, making for a truly life-affirming experience from its opening bars. 

The posthumous release, realised in collaboration with Emahoy’s family and Mississippi Records - is a stone cold stunner. It grants unprecedented access to her discrete craft and inner world in Addis Ababa, against a backdrop of the Ethiopian Red Terror and Civil War, prior to her subsequent exile in a Jerusalem convent. Whilst all no doubt defined by her signature, intricate and lilting type of classical meets jazz-blues phrasing, the eight songs are all far more concise than her usual instrumental works, made even more spellbinding by the revelation of her softly contoured and captivating vocals that beautifully trace and overlie the cadence of her keys. It’s just pure, unbridled expression that’s only heightened by the seemingly off-the-cuff nature of the recordings, as if she just sung the songs to herself, impromptu, never intended for public consumption.

Replete with incidental creaks of the piano stool, birds outside the window, and Emahoy’s finger on the record button, the songs depict themes of loss, mourning and soon-to-be exile, sung into a basic boombox. They place us in the room with her, closer than ever, privy to a vocal version of the closing number to her eponymous compilation, now unveiled as a dedication her niece, the titular Tenkou, with lyrics to guide her adulthood “Don’t cry / Childhood won’t come back / Let it go with love”, alongside the beatific, open-window paean ‘Clouds Moving on the Sky’, and melancholic hiraeth of ‘Ethiopia My Homeland’ or ‘Don’t Forget Your Country’, and ineffable, humbling elegance of idea and execution to ‘Is It Sunny or Cloudy in the Land You Live?’ and ‘Where is the Highway of Thought?’.

Unmissable.
items._genre: world music / jazz-blues / classical piano / Ethiopian
items._cn_summary: 这张遗作收录了埃塞俄比亚修女钢琴家兼作曲家Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru于1977至1985年间用磁带直接录制的八首歌曲，首次呈现她此前从未公开的人声演唱。作品以基本录音设备捕捉，保留了琴凳吱呀声、窗外鸟鸣以及按下录音键的瞬间，将听众直接带入她在亚的斯亚贝巴的私人空间。她的钢琴演奏延续了一贯的古典与爵士蓝调交织风格，而柔和的人声在琴键上方蜿蜒铺展，与器乐作品相比更加凝练。歌词涉及失落、哀悼与即将到来的流亡，背景正值埃塞俄比亚红色恐怖与内战时期。专辑由其家属与密西西比唱片合作完成，呈现出一种近乎即兴的私密表达，歌曲仿佛是唱给自己的，从未打算公之于众。

items.body:
Lauded Canadian no wave noise rockers Earthball live by their improvised wits on convention-scything recordings made at Cave 12, Geneva, and Le Guess Who? Festival, The Netherlands.

"Side A captures a thumping performance at Cave12 in Geneva. Frazzled from a white-knuckle alpine descent, the group settles into a hypnotic sprawl, stretching time and form across a colossal 53-minute set (with the first 22 minutes presented on the LP; the full performance appears on the CD edition). The Cave12 recording is a study in tension and release; ruminative, volatile, and barely contained. Drums stumble and surge, saxophone howls cut through the air, and Ford and Van Wyke’s voices briefly pull together the circle twice, before the tumult lapses into a spinning maelstrom.

Side B meanwhile presents a scorched excerpt from EarthBall’s crushing performance at Le Guess Who? Festival. As Van Wyke reflects: “Having the most excellent Dwarfs of East Agouza play before us only heightened our intention to bring the noise. Listening back, the thing that strikes me most is how we truly were operating in the ever-elusive but always sought-after ‘group mind’. Ninety-degree changes are super tight. Izzy and I are finishing each other’s sentences. Liam’s horn is cradling our outer and inner space. Kellan’s talk box rains down like the voice of a reawakened spirit, and all this havoc is safely stowed in the rumbling ox-cart of John’s solid drumming”.

EarthBall are an avant/noise/rock wrecking ball of a band from Nanaimo, Canada. Rooted in total improvisation, free expression, and a deeply psychedelic sensibility, EarthBall operate on pure instinct. They hurtle onwards in a combustion of spontaneous composition, shooting from the hip, as they fall out of the sky ablaze. The group encompass Isabel Ford (vocals, bass), John Brennan (drums, percussion), Jeremy Van Wyke (vocals, guitar, trumpet), Kellan Maclaughlin (guitar, talkbox), and Liam Murphy (saxophone). Each member brings a rich and varied musical history, with past and present projects including Shearing Pinx, Plan Your Future, Kamikaze Nurse, Eschatons, and Psychedelic Dirt. Collectively and individually, they have collaborated with artists such as Deerhoof, Raven Chacon, Chris Corsano, and William Hooker, deepening the band’s exploratory reach and collective language.

Actual Earth Music - Volume 3 & 4 marks another ascent in EarthBall’s ever-expanding, totemic discography, an ecstatic storm of raw immediacy and unfiltered expression. EarthBall came, conjured and opened the portal! Blink and it’s gone. What was that? Actual Earth Music!"
items._genre: no wave / noise rock / free improvisation / avant-garde / psychedelic
items._cn_summary: EarthBall 来自加拿大纳奈莫，是一支以完全即兴为核心的实验乐队。《Actual Earth Music - Volume 3 & 4》收录了两段现场录音：A 面是乐队在日内瓦 Cave12 完成的五十三分钟演出，展现了高度紧张的集体即兴，鼓声跌宕起伏，萨克斯尖啸撕裂空气，人声偶尔汇聚又散入混乱漩涡；B 面则截取自荷兰 Le Guess Who? 音乐节，乐队成员在描述中提及了'集体意识'的默契状态，乐器之间紧密咬合。专辑横跨噪音摇滚、自由即兴与迷幻摇滚的边界，乐队成员各自拥有丰富的地下音乐履历，曾与 Deerhoof、Raven Chacon 等合作。整张作品强调原始冲动与未经雕琢的能量爆发，是地下即兴音乐场景中典型的现场录音文献。

items.body:
Dutch techno duo Artefakt invite KMRU to assist on their third 'Collaborations' volume, improvising with the Kenyan sound artist in the studio to capture the immediacy of their exchange.

'Collaborations III' follows last year's short, sharp EP with Mayaan Nidam and its predecessor, a record of deep techno variations made alongside Sardinian producer Claudio PRC. This one's the series' most generous set so far and started life in 2023 when the trio found themselves at Pulse, a wooden cabin-cum-studio in the Brandeburg forest. This is where most of the improvisations were initially formulated and in the second session, at Artefakt's Berlin studio, they dubbed the two solo piano tracks and finished the arrangements. It's charming material, as you might imagine, that deviates from Artefakt's prior material and KMRU's noisy recent gear. Made mostly of pillowy, synth-led drones and subtle environmental sounds, it's prime gear for sinking into your surroundings to.
items._genre: ambient techno / drone / experimental electronic / improvisation
items._cn_summary: Artefakt与肯尼亚声音艺术家KMRU合作的第三辑《Collaborations》系列延续了即兴创作的核心方式。三人在勃兰登堡森林的木屋工作室中完成大部分即兴录制，随后在柏林工作室补充了两首独奏钢琴作品并完成编曲。专辑呈现出柔软的合成器主导的drone音色与微妙的环境声响，明显偏离了Artefakt以往的技术路线以及KMRU近期的噪音倾向。作为该系列迄今最丰满的一张作品，它更像一种沉浸式的氛围体验，适合在特定空间中反复聆听。整体气质偏向环境电子与即兴创作的融合，保留了Artefakt的极简底色，同时融入了KMRU对空间感与细节的敏锐处理。

items.body:
Their first project as a duo, 'Midmeste' is Aussie composer-performers and long time collaborators Judith Hamann and James Rushford's latest slow-mo meditation on musical history, psychoacoustic phenomena and minimalism, performed on cello and various pipe organs.

Hamann and Rushford have been working together for years, most visibly alongside Sam Dunscombe as Golden Fur, a chamber ensemble the friends established back in 2008. Each artist has moved decisively in the time since: Berlin-based Hamann outdid herself on last year's intimate and deeply personal 'Aunes', while Rushford brought his various experiments to a focal point on 'Turzets', balancing his tongue-in-cheek electroacoustic experiments with bold medieval deconstructions. Working as a duo, the pair isolate the similarities in their respective musical signatures; the title is a Middle English word meaning "the middlemost point" and signals the album's creation, where they searched out creative overlaps: xenharmonic tunings, organology, psychoacoustics and unintentional sounds, just for starters. And knowing each other so well is also a boon. Where so much minimal avant-garde gear can sound stuffy to the point of being exclusionary, 'Midmeste' sounds inviting even at its most uncompromising.

They use English early music composer John Dunstaple's 'O rosa bella' to anchor their experiments, returning to its core themes every time the album starts to veer too far off course. And there's a refreshing calmness to this technique; in the beginning, Hamann's piercing harmonics provide the edge, while Rushford's rounded organ chords welcome in a more familiar structure that Hamann respects with elegant cello tones. Interestingly, the duo were given the opportunity to record the world's oldest playable organ, a 15th century instrument at Basilica St Valere in Switzerland. Since they were both on residency at La Becque in Lake Geneva, it made perfect sense to document the organ's unique character and add it to their composition - contextually, it's right on point. Mid-way through the first side, we can hear its creaking, crackling wooden frame and whistling resonances, the puffing bellows and the sound of hands and feet on the instrument.

It's these impeccably captured peripheral sounds that give us a sense of place, bolstering the duo's engagement with history with a tangible historical object that still tells us its age. Tones warble, wobble and boom through the centuries-old pipes and Hamann follows the course with her patient, literate responses that add romance, mystery and humanity to what, on its own, might be dry. So we end up with forty minutes of some of the most unashamedly beautiful music either artist has put their name to yet - 'Midmeste' is a duet that whisks you through time, physical space and tonality itself. Remarkable stuff.
items._cn_summary: Judith Hamann与James Rushford的首张二重奏专辑，以大提琴与管风琴为载体展开对音乐历史与心理声学的慢速冥想。两人长期合作的默契使专辑虽根植于极简先锋传统，却具备罕见的亲和力。作品以中世纪英国作曲家Dunstaple的《O rosa bella》为核心母题反复回归，在实验偏离时重新锚定方向。Hamann尖锐的泛音与Rushford圆润的管风琴和弦形成互补，而瑞士巴塞尔圣瓦莱尔大教堂15世纪古老管风琴的物理声响——吱嘎作响的木质框架、气阀的呼吸声、演奏者的手脚动作——被完整纳入作品，构成可触摸的历史在场感。专辑探讨微分调律、乐器学与非意图声响等议题，在四十分钟内穿越时间、空间与音色本身。

items.body:
A digestibly pared-down version of Félicia Atkinson's 90-minute score to Georges Franju's controversial French horror film 'Les yeux sans visage' ('Eyes Without A Face'), 'SANS VISAGE' is her most sinister material to date, made on piano and keyboards and improvised to the film. 

Atkinson was just a teenager when she first saw Franju's 1960 film and it moved her enough that when she was approached by Belgian cultural institute VIERNULVIER to work on a new score, she knew exactly how to approach it. She remembered how impactful the film's themes had been and how resonant they were even decades later, where violence against women is still nauseatingly commonplace. In the film, an adaptation of an even more disturbing novel by Jean Redon, a plastic surgeon stalks and kills women who look like his disfigured daughter, removing their faces in an attempt to create a new one for her. Atkinson dedicates her slow-motion, menacing soundtrack to Gisèle Pelicot, remarking how patriarchal violence cycles again and again through history, creating cages within cages for women. But there's hope; Atkinson doesn't languish in darkness and terror, she knows that in there somewhere, liberation might be on the horizon. 

Underneath the grim, gloomy electric piano notes and agonising pauses, Atkinson seems to relish in a sense that escape might be possible. And if you've seen the film then you'll realise that she's acknowledging the fact that Dr. Génessier, the antagonistic surgeon, meets a fittingly grisly end. While he's let off the hook by police, his daughter Christiane is horrified by his crimes, freeing the dogs he was experimenting on and letting them take their revenge. It's a horror film, after all. But Aktinson swerves all the usual tropes; she improvises an impressionistic dream of wailing tones and aborted phrases that centre the resolution, not the torture itself. Re-scores are often a creative dead end, but thankfully this one adds texture, color and new context to the source material - it makes us want to watch the film all over again.
items._genre: experimental / contemporary classical / dark ambient / avant-garde / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Félicia Atkinson为乔治·弗朗朱1960年法国恐怖片《无脸之眼》创作的90分钟配乐的精简版本。Atkinson以钢琴和键盘即兴录制，在凝重的电钢琴音符和漫长的停顿之间构建氛围。她没有停留在恐惧与黑暗的表面，而是将重心放在影片的终局——被囚禁者的解放与逃离。这种印象派式的处理方式以哀鸣的音调和未完成的乐句为载体，既尊重了原片的阴郁气质，又为影像注入了新的层次。专辑将恐怖配乐转化为关于循环暴力与女性困境的沉思，在暗色音景中保留了微弱的希望之光。

items.body:
Chicago cohorts Natural Information Society and Bitchin' Bajas present their two collaborative albums as a single 2CD package.

Released 10 years before 'Totality', 'Autoimaginary' introduced Bitchin Bajas and Natural Information Society's ongoing collaboration with a cosmic wave of drone and spiritual jazz energy.  While not quite as time-disintegrating as it follow-up, it provides a tantalizing first taste of their collaboration. It's the first side, the 20-minute 'On No Fade' where 'Automaginary' really blossoms. Without getting bogged down in jazz and funk logic, working on a wide-open canvas with billowing drones that swirl around the frame, smudging into washy percussion that never properly materializes, the group of players sound as if they're having a blast, almost lifting themselves into the heavens before the track fades to silence.

And although the flip, that's split into four shorter segments, is still enjoyable, anchored by motorik grooves ('Anemometer'), Dorothy Ashby-style devotional harp runs ('Tricks Me Mind') and furious rhythms from Abrams and drummers Frank Rosaly and Mikel Avery, it takes until the title track for the band to regain their sense of awe. 

Splitting their sophomore collab into disorientated side-long contemplations of "space" and "time", they  puzzle out the divine symmetry between spiritual jazz and polychromatic new age gear. They've refined their cooperation here, choosing to separate their dronier, more new age compositions on the first ("space") side, and the deliberate, transcendent free jazz jams on the flip ("time", natch). 

The extended title track is up first, and it's flawlessly blurry, losing Abrahams' signature guimbri plucks in crystalline synth and woodwind gesticulations that freeze and liquify until Mikel Patrick Avery's soft focus rhythms draw all the sounds together in the final act. And although 'Nothing Does Not Show' is comparatively brief, it offers a more structured counterpart, scratching at the same theme but fading Abrahams' lithe double bass and Lisa Alvarado's harmonium quivers into the foreground alongside Crain's tremolo organ and Rob Frye's swirling flutes.

And although the balance is markedly different on Side B's 'Always 9 Seconds Away', it's equally as crushing. Dilating the tempo to a crawling, Bohren-like 40bpm, Avery just glances the drum heads, opening up time (and space, tbh) for Frye and bass clarinetist Jason Stein to haunt the emptiness with a permed woodwind duet. The sound's topped off with eerily ornate organ and synth vamps, and the result is like a half-speed Don Cherry, dazed from stretched tape and temporal disintegration. It's so good that the jammy, full-throttle finale 'Clock no Clock' kinda pales in comparison, but that's a minor grievance; if you're gonna study time, it should probably go both ways, right?
items._genre: spiritual jazz / drone / new age / experimental / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥的 Natural Information Society 与 Bitchin' Bajas 以 2CD 套装形式合集发行两张合作专辑。《Automaginary》以二十余分钟的《On No Fade》开场，在宽广的音画中铺展嗡鸣与流动打击乐，摆脱爵士与放克逻辑束缚，呈现近乎升入天际的自由感；后段则融入摩托克节奏、竖琴式竖琴拨奏与激烈鼓击。《Totality》将合作细化为「空间」与「时间」两侧，标题曲以水晶般的合成器与木管模糊化吉他布里琴的拨弦，最终由柔焦节奏收束；《Nothing Does Not Show》将低音提琴与印度风琴置于前景，与颤音管风琴与长笛交织；《Always 9 Seconds Away》将速度拉至四十拍，营造类似半速唐·切里的失重感与管乐幽灵般的空旷对话，末曲《Clock no Clock》则以全速即兴收尾。整体上两张专辑呈现精神爵士、新世纪氛围与嗡鸣美学的融合，在即兴与冥想之间反复切换。

items.album: Where Light Pauses in the Silence of the Sun
items.excerpt:

"Functioning as both recording studio and performance venue, the space has no stage, with the audience gathered around the performers. Working within an open framework, the duo reshaped the music each evening while recording the performances live to multitrack. Rotary speakers, modular syn
items.body:
In spring 2025, Abul Mogard and Rafael Anton Irisarri created the source material for their second album, Where Light Pauses in the Silence of the Sun, during a three-day residency at Morphine Raum in Berlin.

"Functioning as both recording studio and performance venue, the space has no stage, with the audience gathered around the performers. Working within an open framework, the duo reshaped the music each evening while recording the performances live to multitrack. Rotary speakers, modular synthesizers and bowed guitar formed the core of their sonic language, captured through a 1970s mixing console and microphones placed around the room.

Back in Mogard’s studio in Rome, the material was further crafted as motifs were stretched, fragments isolated, and tempos dissolved. Irisarri recorded additional guitar textures and treatments in New York, while passages recorded by Martina Bertoni and Andrea Burelli in Berlin reinforced the harmonic centres and brought breath, refinement and a new sensibility to their compositions. The process continued as Mogard’s layering and subtraction reassembled everyone’s parts into the final arrangement.

The album opens with “In the Eastern Wild,” building from a sparse outline into a monumental formation of low-frequency weight, its internal motion shaped by the rotating Leslie speaker. “Over the Domes” widens into a broader acoustic field, where sustained modular tones meet waves of softly plucked guitar. The music then turns inward with “A Blue Descent,” centred on Bertoni’s cello, whose growling timbre introduces a melancholic depth.

At the album’s centre, “In a Quiet Radiance” unfolds around a slow guitar ostinato, its luminous stillness opening into a more expansive and reflective state. Across its ten-minute span, Burelli’s violin lines and Bertoni’s lower cello phrases gradually surface, weaving through the harmonic field. Mogard brings Burelli’s processed voice to the fore, its emotive, operatic presence becoming one of the record’s pivotal moments. “Of Blessed Ages” suspends the sonic flow, shifting between parallel major and minor chords as lingering, slowly decaying melodies shape the music’s internal drift. The closing “Among Shadows” settles into a darker resonance as layered textures recede.

Mogard and Irisarri’s shared language balances restraint and maximalism. UK magazine Crack describes the music as “a tidal wave held in suspension,” while Dutch newspaper de Volkskrant writes, “What a colossal sound, and how this music strikes at the emotions.” Reflecting on the residency sessions, Irisarri recalls: “At moments I genuinely couldn’t tell if a sound was coming from me or from Abul. It stopped feeling like two people making decisions and began to feel like we were inside a system moving on its own."

Marja de Sanctis’ cover artwork revisits the vessel sculpture from the duo’s first album, Impossibly Distant, Impossibly Close. There it appeared as raw, unfired clay. Here it has been fired in the kiln and finished with a glaze. Light gathers on its polished surface and spills into the surrounding space. As she explains, “I wanted to convey the idea of continuity within the duo, and the vessel became a kind of container for that idea. However, their music felt different this time, and with the collaboration of Martina and Andrea, I felt it should have a sleeker, softer, more glamorous look, very distant from the first raw appearance.” The transformation of the vessel from raw clay to fired form suggests a passage from immediacy toward permanence, mirroring the music’s gradual expansion."
items._genre: ambient / drone / experimental electronic / modern composition
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Abul Mogard与Rafael Anton Irisarri的第二张合作作品，源于2025年春季在柏林Morphine Raum为期三天的驻留创作。两人围绕旋转音箱、模块化合成器与弓弦吉他展开即兴录音，在无舞台的亲密空间中进行现场多轨录制，回罗马后进一步雕琢：拉伸动机、抽离碎片、溶解节拍，并融入纽约与柏林乐手的大提琴、小提琴与人声处理。整体呈现出低频厚重而内部流动缓慢的声响景观，旋律在大调和弦与暗淡小调之间悬浮游移。从稀疏的音形逐渐铺展为庞大低频构造，弓弦乐器的人声化质感成为情感支点，专辑在沉静的辉光与暗影间寻找平衡。

items.body:
Pensive to strangely sublime electroacoustic abstraction and frisson from cellist-composer/sound designer Martina Bertoni & TAL’s bossman and To Rococo Rot / Mapstation legend) Stefan Schneider, quietly undergoing each other in their intuitive process.

‘Holding on and letting go’ manifests the duo’s mutual fascination for musical economy in restricted electronic palettes that unfold as a pair of time-slipping works defined by incremental metamorphosis. They land in the label’s 10th year of operations after that ace Garth Erasmus LP to continue an ever-roving, dot-joining agenda at its most oblique yet subtly absorbing.

In ‘Holding On’ they almost subliminally transition from folk drone wheeze to iridescent ambient noise with a spellbinding semi-organic quality, where the smallest gestures become amplified in butterfly effect chain reaction of microcosmic clinamen, producing low key entrancing results. 

On ‘Letting Go’ Bertoni’s cello is more discernible, yet likewise melts into air with alluring nuance, fraying and congealing into a sort of plasmic jazz x ambient noise abstract, calling to mind the queasy air movements of Joachim Nordwall pieces or CMvH’s paranormal studies gone more exotic, humid.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是大提琴家兼作曲家Martina Bertoni与电子音乐人Stefan Schneider（To Rococo Rot成员）的合作成果，以极度克制的电子音色为底，通过缓慢的渐进式变化展开两个长篇作品。第一首从民谣式的嗡鸣音色几乎难以察觉地过渡到微光闪烁的氛围噪音，最细微的声响动作在蝴蝶效应般的连锁反应中被逐级放大，产生低调而迷人的效果。第二首中大提琴声部更为可辨，却同样以微妙的渐变融入空气，碎裂又凝结为一种可塑性的爵士感抽象氛围噪音。整张专辑体现了两位音乐人对极简电子配色的共同迷恋，将有机乐器与电子纹理以直觉性的方式相互交融，强调时间感错位与微观层面的声音嬗变，而非传统曲式结构，是当代实验音乐中精致内敛的典范之作。

"Reeling In The Weeks—which felt like Years — after my first Current 93 album, I
items.body:
C93’s second album, following ‘Nature Unveiled’ (1984) in the same year, continued to break new ground in the post-industrial arena with problematic visionary David Tibet leading a phalanx of co-conspirators - Steven Stapleton, Diana Rigerson, Steve Ignorant (Crass), among them - into fractious, psychoacoustic heck starkly contrasting his later neofolk works. Required listening FFO Gen P-O/TG/Psychic TV, NWW, Coil.

"Reeling In The Weeks—which felt like Years — after my first Current 93 album, I had started on the difficult second C93 album, DOGS BLOOD RISING.Having been asked to appear on both Top Of The Pops AND The Old Grey Whistle Test 93 times in the same week after the release of NATURE UNVEILED, I realised that God was telling me that I had hit on a winning formula of Christian eschatology and Apocalyptic Christian texts over a SoundScape As Cool As Flies, but that I was missing the vital ingredient of a Simon & Garfunkel song. DOGS BLOOD RISING — which I described to myself in a VISION as an album which hoped, wished, and made bad trips sound like good trips — was essentially the Mirror Night of NATURE UNVEILED, although only half of it was recorded at Roundhouse Studios. Squats were calling, and 8-track studios were all I was able to afford. DOGS BLOOD RISING didn’t chart, except in my NightSweats. Listening to it now, it makes me as restless as I was then, staring beyond the windows there, watching and praying for something, someone, anything, anyone.

- David Tibet, Hastings, 11 March 2026."
items._cn_summary: 这是Current 93在1984年发行的第二张专辑，紧随《Nature Unveiled》之后，是后工业领域的开拓性作品。David Tibet与Steven Stapleton、Diana Rigerson、Crass的Steve Ignorant等合作者共同打造了一张在声学上极具攻击性的专辑，刻意区别于他后来转向的neofolk风格。专辑融合了基督教末世论文本与心理声学实验，自称试图让糟糕的迷幻体验听起来像好的迷幻体验。录音条件简陋，仅有一半在Roundhouse Studios完成，另一半依赖8轨设备与廉价空间。David Tibet后来撰写的回忆文字为这张充满不安与宗教狂热的作品增添了私密注脚，专辑从未上榜，但在他个人的噩梦中始终留有位置。与Throbbing Gristle、Psychic TV、Coil等先驱一脉相承，是工业与实验音乐场景中不可绕过的文献。
