items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家兼作曲家Omar Sosa在意大利Fazioli钢琴厂的音乐厅中进行了一场两小时的独奏即兴演奏，录音后经后期混入人声采样、打击乐、循环音轨、田野录音和环境声响，构成专辑《Sendas》。Sosa自Thelonious Monk处汲取灵感，坚持每次演奏皆不重复，作品横跨爵士、拉丁、古典与世界音乐，打破风格界限。他在采访中谈到创作时追求无意识的自由状态，认为'少即是多'，强调声音应与低脉轮产生共鸣，呼应人类精神层面的连结。专辑对音乐工业将艺术家归类于市场标签的做法持批判态度，坚持独立、自由、跨界融合的艺术立场。

items.body: The Visit by cris derksen The Visit isn�t an album built on compromises. The fourth release from Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father�s side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions, where it�s the opening, full-throated improvisation of �White Gladis 1� (with singer Jennifer Kreisberg) or the encompassing haunting mood that grows up around �Lyre Birds.� She�s primarily a cellist, one who works across genres; one of the great joys here is it�s impossible to attach any kind of handle to the music. Just as you think you have it nailed down, the next track is something different, as with the the cello and programming of �aabaakwad� which becomes the wordless singing of �New Heya.� The Visit by cris derksen There�s a raw, unfettered beauty to the album, music made with passion and no restraints. There are a couple of songs here, but nothing that conforms to expectations, altering gears and direction, as when the strings and brass that arrive from nowhere to take over �Buffalo Girls.� The Visit by cris derksen But the emotional centrepiece here is �Lyre Birds,� with Derksen�s cello weaving sparely around the shards of spoken words, leading into the fluttering piano arpeggios of �Nice And Clean.� This is an album of surprises, leading down strange lanes and around brilliant corners that offer startling new views. As both composer and musician, Cris Derksen is more than a singular talent; she�s a person with a vision for her music, and she keeps true to it here. The Visit is not an easy listen, but it is eminently satisfying. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Cris Derksen作为大提琴手与作曲家的第四张专辑，跨越多种类型边界，拒绝任何简化的归类。专辑以充满即兴色彩的开篇作品展开，与歌手Jennifer Kreisberg合作呈现出饱满声线，随后在'Lyre Birds'中构建出弥漫而幽暗的氛围，大提琴与碎片化的语言交织。曲目之间频繁转向：编程节奏与器乐对话、突然涌入的铜管与弦乐、无歌词的人声段落交替出现，展现出丰富的创作想象力。德克森拥有加拿大北部TallCree原住民（父系）与门诺派（母系）的双重血脉，这种文化背景在她对声音空间的处理方式中有所体现。整张专辑不迎合既定预期，制作充满热情且不设限制，在艰涩与满足之间取得了平衡。

items.body: The songs flow right into each other and are only composed of what seems to be a few layers each, but there is a fond fuzziness to them, that glistens like the light reflected off the water. There is a slight melancholy tinge to the music, but it’s not overpowering. Everything else going on in the world disappears for a time Dreams of a Sunflower River by Black Brunswicker   Ambient folk artist Black Brunswicker paints a pastoral drift down a slow river, a winding lullaby that floats down the meandering Sunflower River, a tributary to the Yazoo River with guitar, field recordings, and light electronics. The Yazoo in turn flows into the veins of Americas dividing artery, the Mississippi, before emptying itself into the Gulf of Mexico (yes, of Mexico). The Sunflower River itself sits inside a channel that Mississippi carved out in long ago years. The brackish muddy water moves between farms, neighborhoods, wetlands, and the abandoned shacks where sharecroppers lived out their years. The river starts just below the border of Tennessee before it snakes its one hundred mile way into the Yazoo. Along the way, at Clarksdale, the county seat of Coahoma County, they hold the annual Sunflower River Blues & Gospel Festival. There is no Gospel music here unless you call it the gospel of drone, the gospel of sweet ambiance. The Delta Blues, however, can be heard on this record, but slowed down and refracted through a gaussian lens. This is a perfect addition to Nettwerk’s growing catalog of “shoe gauze” music as heard in the solo music of label mate Hollie Kenniff. Sometimes you have to leave a place too, in order to recreate that place in your art. Such is the case with Black Brunswicker, the ambient folk project of Etta Helfrich. She makes her home now in Manchester, UK, but comes from Bloomington, Indiana. The rivers of the Midwest have much in common with those further south. They are all flowing towards the Mississippi and they are often muddy waters. More muddy than rippling and clear, but no less inviting on a hot summer day. In the music there is a similar cloudiness. There is a slight melancholy tinge to the music :: No drums, no voices, just warbling instrumentals recalling the first highways of America that can only be navigated by boat. The fingerpicking here is placid, impressionistic, with lingering pastel synth pads adding to the shimmer. The songs flow right into each other and are only composed of what seems to be a few layers each, but there is a fond fuzziness to them, that glistens like the light reflected off the water. There is a slight melancholy tinge to the music, but it’s not overpowering. This music is akin to floating down such a river in a black rubber tube. Soft field recordings chirp and buzz, the hum of insects and birds along languid drifts as gentle picking brings the mind and heart into a relaxed center. Everything else going on in the world disappears for a time. Problems go away. Time is blurred until there is only the sun and the sound of the water as it hits a shallow place bubbling over rocks, as it moves back into a deeper channel before stopping for a time on a sandbar where a fire can be made to heat up whatever lunch was brought along (hot dogs on sticks were what my dad and I ate on our canoe trips in eastern Indiana). Somewhere along the way there will be a rope swing and time to swim. This is music of full summer and the grains of distortion on the guitar strings are like sheens of haze on a humid afternoon. Dreams of a Sunflower River is available on Nettwerk. [Bandcamp] Dreams of a Sunflower River by Black Brunswicker
items._genre: ambient folk / drone / field recording / ambient guitar
items._cn_summary: Black Brunswicker 是 Etta Helfrich 的环境民谣项目，现居英国曼彻斯特，源自印第安纳州布卢明顿。专辑以向日葵河（密西西比河支流）为意象，用吉他指弹、轻柔合成器垫音与田野录音（虫鸣鸟叫）构建出一条缓慢漂流的声音河流。没有鼓点与人声，只有层叠的原声吉他与朦胧嗡鸣，呈现出南方河域泥泞、慵懒又略带忧郁的氛围。评论将之与 Hollie Kenniff 的"鞋纱"风格并置，指出三角洲布鲁斯在此被慢速化、通过高斯透镜折射成无人声的冥想音景。整体结构松散连贯，歌曲如水般彼此衔接，音色温暖而有颗粒感，适合作为忘却周遭烦扰的听觉容器。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — In my opinion the best Myrath album is Desert Call. The band's second album and their first with vocalist Zaher Zorgati, it saw them find a fine line between the chaotic prog metal of their first album, but adding in catchy hooks, heavy riffs, melodic but complex instrumentation and epic orchestration and focus on Arabic melodies. While I can see their want to go into a more mainstream sound, I think this album is the perfect mix of the 2 worlds. Zaher Zorgati's vocals are a perfect fit in the band, filling the tracks with great emotion and very impressive technical and diverse ability. It would be great to see them return to this sound one day, which they did show promise of on their most recent album. The track I'd recommend is Empty World.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是突尼斯前卫金属乐队Myrath的第二张作品，也是主唱Zaher Zorgati的首张录音，乐队在混乱前卫金属基底上加入了抓人的旋律钩子、厚重的吉他律动以及复杂的器乐编排，同时大量融入阿拉伯旋律元素与史诗管弦乐编配，实现了两极风格之间的平衡。Zorgati的人声情感充沛，技术能力多样且极具表现力，与乐队的器乐走向契合。该作试图在主流可听性与前卫复杂性之间寻找融合点，作为北非地区将阿拉伯传统音阶与金属框架结合的较早尝试，在跨文化融合层面具有代表性，被认为为后来的中东金属场景提供了方向性参考。

items.body: You tie the red shoes to rhythms you do not choose You dance, you dance to rhythms you do not choose Athens synth-punk outfit Dramachine takes Hans Christian Andersen’s The Red Shoes, drags it through a series of back rooms full of busted strobes and analogue machines, and come back with Choros tou Thanatou, a dance of death sung in Greek, with a mesmerizing video. Directed by Antoinette Tat, with Eleni Kosmopoulou behind the camera and Myrsini Lyra as the doomed dancer, the clip turns compulsion into choreography, then lets the body pay the bill. Speed can become more disturbing when someone sings over it, as they have already accepted the crash. Choros tou Thanatou moves like a cheap car with the brakes cut: frenetic, kinetic, hi-octane, all hard angles and bad nerves. The beat has that wonderful low-budget death-machine insistence, snapping forward while the synths jab and glare. Yet the vocals come in strangely plodding, deliberate, almost numb in their delivery, giving the track an unnerving imbalance. You are, with no doubt, being commanded. The video interprets the old fairy tale without embalming it in literary respect. The Red Shoes has always been a nasty little moral engine: a girl wants beauty, the world punishes appetite, and the body becomes a prison with music playing inside it. Here, that punishment becomes feverish and theatrical, with the dancer condemned to motion until motion itself begins to look like possession. The band members appear as the diabolical Charmer and the helpless Angel, two sides of the same rotten bargain, temptation and pity staring at each other across the frame. Tat leans into a Lynchian unease without turning the piece into mere quotation. The retro eighties visual effects, abrupt edits, and unreal colour treatments give the video the texture of a cursed television broadcast picked up on a dead channel in some Athens apartment at 3 a.m. Lyra’s performance supplies the ache beneath the velocity: every gesture feels pulled from her by invisible strings, every turn another small surrender. Watch the video for Choros tou Thanatou below: As the title track from Dramachine’s March 2026 album, Choros tou Thanatou works as both a warning and an invitation. Desire enters smiling, compulsion takes over the room, and by the end the dance has become less an escape than a sentence. items._cn_summary: 希腊雅典合成器朋克乐队 Dramachine 释出专辑《ΧΟΡΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΘΑΝΑΤΟΥ》同名曲音乐视频，将安徒生童话《红舞鞋》改编为一场以希腊语演唱的死亡之舞。评论指出音乐以低保真的机械化节奏推进，合成器尖锐刺目，鼓机如失灵刹车般狂飙，但人声却迟缓、近乎麻木地铺陈其上，形成速度与情绪之间的失衡张力。MV 由 Antoinette Tat 执导，借助复古八十年代视觉特效、不规则剪辑与超现实色彩处理，呈现出林奇式的焦虑氛围。舞者 Myrsini Lyra 的肢体被不可见丝线牵引，每一次旋转都如献祭，乐队成员则分别化身诱惑者与悲悯者两极。整件作品将欲望与强迫的主题转化为剧场化的视觉寓言，希腊文化语境为这则古老道德寓言注入了新的地域色彩。

items.body: Euro Kiosk comes out of Aarau sounding as if Switzerland finally got sick of being treated as a pretty postcard and decided to answer back with bass, groove, and a sly little grin. The project fits into the Swiss wave and post-punk scene, yet with its debut EP’s title track, Temptations, it exudes a relaxed, effortless vibe—like a laid-back 90s attitude, knowing the club is open, and the Kirchwasser is flowing. The rhythm section locks into Motorik patience, the steady forward shove of a train you cannot quite afford to miss. Over it, the bass runs in hot pursuit, clipped and wiry, while the guitars bring in the jangly UK aftertaste without turning into a museum of record-collector references. Joy Division hangs in the architecture, Grauzone in the steel, Kleenex in the nerve endings, and Le Tigre or Sneaks in the dry, funky snap of the attitude. Beaks hover nearby too, with post-punk pulled through a colder, more contemporary room. Euro Kiosk sidesteps the usual gray-coat solemnity by actually letting the body into the room. The groove slouches, stretches, and smirks, carrying a devil-may-care looseness that feels faintly stoned but never sloppy. The funk element never begs for attention. It leans against the wall, insolent and spare, moving the hips while the song stares out at a continent broken into payment plans, border controls, military budgets, ad feeds, and panic sold back to the people as lifestyle. That name starts to bite harder the longer the music plays. A kiosk sells the small consumable comforts of a collapsing age: coffee, tobacco, magazines, lottery tickets, chewing gum, and some bright wrapper to hold while the institutions rot. Euro Kiosk turns that little commercial booth into a psychic checkpoint, a place where anxiety and consumerism meet under fluorescent light and call themselves civilization. Temptations carries a little shoegaze haze at the edges, enough darkwave frost in the air, and a post-punk frame built for motion. It slides into the groove without making a speech about it. items._cn_summary: Euro Kiosk 来自瑞士阿劳，首张EP以单曲《Temptations》切入后朋克场景。乐评指出其节奏段呈现Motorik式的持续推进，贝斯线条紧促而锋利，吉他层带来英式后朋克的明亮回响，同时融入funk的松散律动。整体编曲摆脱了瑞士后朋克常见的灰暗肃穆，以一种懒散、略带迷幻的姿态让身体性回归音乐。作品被置于Joy Division、Grauzone、Kleenex、Le Tigre等乐队的影响谱系中，并带有当代暗潮的冷感与少量shoegaze的边缘朦胧感。乐评延伸至对'Euro Kiosk'这一名称的社会隐喻解读，将其比作消费主义衰败时代的心理检查站，在荧光灯下审视焦虑与商品的合谋。

items.body: ARMOURS BODY self-released ARMOURS draw on the grand synth music traditions of their home in Sweden in more ways the one on their debut EP. On the one hand, they’re definitely steeped in synthpop, as the five tracks on the BODY EP all display a strong sense of melody and general songcraft. On the other hand, they’ve got their stomping boots on, and draw from classic and modern EBM, without going all in on the sounds aggression and muscle. A helpful point of comparison is American act Sleek Teeth, although ARMOURS’ approach is unique; on “Allegiance” the trip go for a gentle synth ballad, but back it with some busy, hard hitting percussion, including metallic sounds, giving the whole track a nice feeling of grit in contrast with its sweet melody. The title track on the other hand builds itself around a wiry synthline and a mid-tempo rhythm track, with the addition of some chiming sounds and stabs that give the song an urgency fit for it’s foreboding tone. With a few additional nods towards various electronic genres in the same orbit across the remaining tracks (there’s some new beat in the Easterb melodies that float through “Push”, and “Confront” invokes the slow and emotional electropop of their countrymen Kite), it’s an EP of remarkable breadth considering its length, and a very pleasingly developed sound for a debut. BODY EP by ARMOURS Run Level Zero The Star Of Naked Truth self-released The incredibly productive recent run from Swedish electro-experimentalists Run Level Zero have been on has continued, with a whopping four archival EPs dropping in as many months. Hans Åkerman and Oskar Lygner are also putting out new material at a quick rate, too, with the brooding, downtempo unease of preceding release Pneuma continued on The Star Of Naked Truth. If anything, these four cuts continue the project’s drift further away from its trad electro-industrial roots and into impressionistic synth composition for its own cosmic sake. “The Traveller” feels like a more wistful and wounded yet musically light sequel to the preceding release’s “The Ship”, while the moody arpeggios of “Heavy Stones” feel of a piece with any number of faded pastel synthwave soundtracks (though its lyrics tackle themes of aging and unmet ambition with stark sincerity). While clocking in at under twenty minutes there’s still a fair bit of variety on display, with a sharp contrast to be found between “You Are Made For Something” (part early Mute Records, part “Nightclubbing”) and the sprained, yet still mournful minimal synths of closer “In Your Embrace”. Much more so than sub-genre or even general style, RLZ are pursuing specific moods with each piece on each new record, and holding to whatever chilly but soulful sound suits. The Star of Naked Truth by Run Level Zero The post Observer: ARMOURS and Run Level Zero appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 本期乐评聚焦两支瑞典电子乐队的最新发行。ARMOURS的首张EP《BODY》展现了合成器流行与EBM的折衷路线，五首曲目在甜美旋律与硬朗打击乐之间取得平衡，标题曲以金属感节奏与阴郁氛围支撑怀旧合成器线条，而《Push》中浮现的新律动元素和《Confront》对同胞Kite式忧郁电气流行的致敬进一步拓宽了作品的纵深。Run Level Zero的《The Star of Naked Truth》延续了项目从传统电气工业向印象主义合成器写作的漂移，四首曲目围绕忧郁、低沉的情感展开，泛音与简约合成器编排营造出冷峻却真挚的宇宙感，歌词直面衰老与未竟抱负等主题，与褪色粉彩合成波配乐形成张力。两者皆为独立发行，在瑞典电子音乐谱系中各自延伸出鲜明的个人表达。

items.body:
R&B outsider Zsela joins forces with inc. no world's Daniel Aged and film composer Taul Katz on '4 Dreams', a billowing ambient-neoclassical hallucination that'll tickle fans of Mary Lattimore, Malibu, Nala Sinephro, Gigi Masin.

If you only know Zsela thanks to her dramatic 2024 debut album 'Big For You', the mostly beatless, fully reflective '4 Dreams' might come as a surprise. But look a little further back in her catalogue and things will fall into place; remember 'Angels Pharmacy' and Remembrance' from Actress's 'Karma & Desire'? That was Zsela on vocals, so she's got priors. '4 Dreams' started life as the soundtrack to 'Seven Heavenly Senses', an art exhibition from last year at Paris's Hôtel de la Marine, but has since taken on a life of its own. Zsela's breaths are stretched and sculpted into warm, washing biomechanical pads on the opening dream, left to weather tinny arpeggiated FM synths and muggy bass drones. So far, so predictable. But Zsela muddles proceedings with her confident delivery, layering her voice into jazzy, R&B inflected key changes that keep you guessing. Imagine an astral plane answer to Dawn Richard's ambient-inflected pop and you'll have some idea of where this is headed.

Then 'Dream 2' takes an unexpected diversion, the vocals replaced by swirling harp flourishes and the kind of floating synth stabs that draw a core logic from classic Ambient - Harold Budd, Laraaji et al - then adding extra colors just where necessary. And on 'Dream 3', faint, almost folk-y strings enter the frame, calling out from beyond the horizon, almost blotted out by a synth part that's in the thrall of Gigi Masin's legendary 'Clouds' - the track that ended up being repurposed by Björk on 'It's In Our Hands'. Zsela, Katz and Aged keep that momentum for the final track, too, letting cinematic strings echo around subtle synths and vanishing rhythms, hitting those hypnagogic, tranquil notes that so much contemporary ambient music seems to avoid. 'Cause at its heart, '4 Dreams' is deeper than that, a record that's entrenched in jazz, soul and classical minimalism rather than throwaway numbing music, of the contemporary varierty.
items._cn_summary: Zsela与制作人Daniel Aged及电影配乐作曲家Taul Katz合作的《4 Dreams》，源于巴黎Hôtel de la Marine艺术展的配乐，后独立发展为完整专辑。作品以无节拍、呼吸感强烈的人声为基底，将声音拉伸塑造成温暖洗练的生物机械式音垫，叠加细碎FM合成器琶音与黏稠低音嗡鸣。人声线在爵士化和声与R&B转调中游走，第二首以竖琴与飘浮合成刺音替代人声，向Harold Budd、Laraaji的经典Ambient脉络致敬；第三首引入近乎民谣质感的弦乐，呼应Gigi Masin《Clouds》的合成器语汇；终曲以电影感弦乐环绕微弱节奏与消退中的合成器，收束于沉静氛围。整张作品扎根于爵士、灵魂乐与极简古典传统，拒绝当代Ambient常见的麻痹式轻飘，呈现出更具深度的冥想质地。

items.body:
London/Helsinki label Cold Blow map the subliminal links of early ‘90s electro, techno and its backroom, downbeat offshoots thru a plethora of tunes recorded ’92-’99 by the likes of Stasis, 2000 And One, CiM, all displaying how they translated Detroit techno intricacies and new age ambient soul for UK & EU bodies in motion, or those eaten by sofas.

“Across eight carefully selected slices of starry-eyed machine soul, Cold Blow presents an exquisite tour through backroom techno and downtempo electro. With a focus on thematic flow and an immersive listening experience, the London-based label explores works from leading lights of the 1990s and previously unreleased cuts that celebrate the human heart that can be discovered in synthetic sound practices.

The development of techno in the 1990s saw the music evolve in different directions across the world. From the expressive blueprint laid out by the Detroit pioneers, a wide range of tempos and energies emerged. Techno's evocative synthesis and intricate drum machine programming was especially potent for deeper explorations away from the dancefloor.

Documents Of Different Reality casts back to when technology was steering quantum leaps in communication and creativity and the future was shot through with naive optimism. It was also a time when the media and industry hadn't caught up with the music to box it into distinct categories. As such, there's a sense of creative freedom that informs the older tracks on the album, from 2000 And One and Sandy Huner's (originally as Pure) sparkling example of early Dutch techno to London-based LA Synthesis' detailed take on braindance and the majestic night sky vision of cult legend Stasis.

There's also space for rare, late 90s machine funk from Icelandic outlier Thor alongside Connective Zone's charmingly fractured bleep dream and a more contemporary offering from Barcelona-based duo Permutation. Meanwhile Mind Control and CiM both capture the spirit of stylistic fusion with twitchier rhythms that take influence from hardcore and jungle as much as techno.

With an atmospheric through-line of melancholic pads and harmonious leads, this small but perfectly formed collection naturally follows on from previous, equally thought-out compilations on Cold Blow, and adds a distinct perspective on the history and continuing legacy of pioneering early ambient techno.”
items._cn_summary: Cold Blow 厂牌以八首精心挑选的曲目回溯上世纪九十年代电子音乐的发展脉络，聚焦于底特律技术派衍生出的深沉派别与慢拍律动。这些录音完成于1992至1999年间，Stasis、2000 And One、CiM 等艺术家展示了机器灵魂如何承载情感温度，而非仅服务于舞池。整张专辑贯穿忧郁的合成器铺垫与和谐旋律线，营造出沉浸式的聆听氛围。曲目横跨荷兰早期技术派、伦敦的 Braindance 演绎、冰岛稀有作品及巴塞罗那当代创作，呈现了那个媒体尚未将电子音乐强行分类的自由创作时代。整体编排注重主题流动与情绪连贯，是一份对早期氛围技术音乐历史及其延续影响的精致考察。

items.body:
Airbrushed, subtropical, new age ambient-jazz from Jesse Peterson’s Maui-based project, given its highest profile platform to date on Amsterdam’s Music From Memory, and warmly advised to admirers of his regular spars, Carlos Niño, Laraaji, Mia Doi Todd...

"Originally formed in New York in the late 2000s, Turn On The Sunlight has evolved into a fluid, location-spanning practice rooted in collaboration, intuition and process. Now based on Maui, Peterson’s work draws together a wide network of musicians and environments, with recordings taking shape across Los Angeles, Tokyo, London, San Miguel de Allende and Haʻikū.

Loosely situated within a framework of organic, ambient-leaning jazz, 'Iseo' unfolds as a series of open, exploratory pieces, with electronics sitting subtly beneath acoustic and environmental elements. Built from layered instrumentation including synthesizers, guitar, zither, flutes, voice and field recordings, Peterson moves between grounded, tactile detail and more expansive, immersive states. A sense of warmth and permeability runs throughout: organic percussion, environmental textures and drifting rhythmic elements lend the record a gently saturated humidity, reflecting Peterson’s base in Hawaii, where the presence of nature is felt as much as it is heard.

Underlying the project is a way of working rooted in gathering, listening and tending. Instruments, ensemble sessions, field recordings and everyday environments are approached with attentiveness, shaped through collecting, refining and allowing things to settle. Relationships, landscape and lived experience shape the sound, giving 'Iseo' a tactile, almost hand-made quality.

Rather than fixed arrangements, the album feels as if it has been organically and lovingly assembled through a process of listening and response, each element finding its place within a wider, evolving whole. This approach reaches a natural centre point in the 15-minute piece 'Medianoche En La Calle Aurora', which unfolds patiently, bending through shifting environments as motifs and textures emerge and dissolve with quiet continuity.

Peterson’s role as both instigator and facilitator is central to the project. Bringing together a diverse group of collaborators including Carlos Niño, Mia Doi Todd, Laraaji, Ko Ishikawa, Luis Pérez Ixoneztli and Miles Spilsbury, he creates space for individual voices to emerge within a shared language. The result is a music defined by openness and generosity.

'Iseo' takes its title from Peterson’s son’s middle name, a word that can be understood to mean ‘one-world life’. The piece itself takes the form of a gentle lullaby, its melody loosely shaped around the syllables of his name and sung to Peterson’s son by Luis Pérez Ixoneztli, a close collaborator whose presence across the record reflects a long-standing relationship that extends beyond the music itself.

Sleeve art and design by Michael Willis."
items._genre: ambient jazz / new age / experimental fusion
items._cn_summary: Jesse Peterson在夏威夷Maui创建的Iseo项目推出的专辑《Turn On The Sunlight》，由阿姆斯特丹独立厂牌Music From Memory发行。作品以有机、ambient倾向的爵士为框架，将电子元素悄然置于原声乐器与环境声之下。录制跨越洛杉矶、东京、伦敦、San Miguel de Allende与Haʻikū等多个地点，合成器、吉他、齐特琴、长笛、人声与田野录音层叠交织，呈现出一种温润而通透的热带湿润质感。专辑以集体的协作、倾听与沉淀为工作方式，Peterson召集了Carlos Niño、Laraaji、Mia Doi Todd、Ko Ishikawa、Luis Pérez Ixoneztli等多元合作者，使每件乐器在共享的语言中保有独立的表达空间。15分钟长曲《Medianoche En La Calle Aurora》是全作的自然重心，动机与音色在变换的环境中浮现又消融。标题曲《Iseo》取自Peterson之子中间名，意为'一个世界的生命'，由Ixoneztli以摇篮曲形式演绎人声旋律，整体散发着一种手工拼贴般的亲密质感与跨文化、跨地理的声音叙事。

items.body:
Slamming, sci-fi skooled Detroit jit from the sound’s contemporary standard bearer, bolstered by a lethal Arpanet remix from Gerald Donald, whose early Dopplereffekt classics are ghettotech/jit canon.

On four brisk originals Shawscape Renegade weaves extramusical inspiration from classic sci-fi themes - existential dread; the costs of technological evolution; the dead ends of overspecialisation - into tightly coiled club motors. 

His acidic electrofunked ’78 Light Years From Earth’ pings like a Stingray zinger, and ‘Mechanise 9’ locks into a proper pneumatic 4/4 pump galvanised with gunky synths, and ‘Ignition One’ pares it all back to fluid bass hydrodynamic punctuated by the type of snares that knock your fillings out - as deployed in the Black to Techno documentary soundtrack. 

His ‘Terraformers Warning’ is a standout of inimitable 313 machine funk, but let’s be fair, Arpanet’s Quanta Remodel of the same components is just on a whole nexx level: riddled with breathless detailing, discordant synth voices and cyber-dubbed aerodynamic sleekness that will sound utterly sick on a decent rig. 

DJs beware - “the vinyl versions of A1 & B1 are five BPM slower than the digital, moving the music to between 128BPM and 151BPM on a standard Technics turntable and opening it up for play in a greater range of club environs.
items._cn_summary: Exoframe的这张EP以底特律jit风格为核心，四首原创作品从经典科幻主题汲取灵感，将技术演化的代价、过度专业化的死胡同等存在主义命题编织进紧凑的俱乐部节奏中。'78 Light Years From Earth'呈现酸性电funk质感，'Mechanise 9'以气动式四四拍泵动节奏推进，'Ignition One'则回归流体低音线与极具冲击力的军鼓音色。'Terraformers Warning'展现出难以模仿的313机器funk特质，而Arpanet（Gerald Donald）的Quanta Remodel remix将同源素材重新解构，注入呼吸感密集的细节、不和谐合成器人声与赛博dub式的空气动力学光泽，在高级音响系统上效果尤为突出。值得关注的是黑胶版本比数字版慢5BPM，使曲目适应更广泛的俱乐部播放环境。整体制作精准地延续了底特律电声传统的科幻叙事基因。

‘Aftersun’ composer Coates furnishes a score of heart-in-mouth classical strings, keys and choral arrangements to gay romance flick ‘Pillion’, aka an opportunity to ogle Alexander Skarsgård, replete with biker leathers, in a sub-dom relationship

By now one of the preeminent composers in his field - up there with Mica Levi, 0PN, Bobby Krlic et al - Coates continues to expand and hone his distinctly classic yet fresh palette and chops to purpose on this particularly lush set of orchestrations and sweeping sound design, including his take on a Satie evergreen. Gently gelled to the film’s narrative, revolving a shy yung queer lad seduced into a BDSM relationship with a dashing local biker, Coates’ score is ravishingly sensual and heady, full of oneiric allusions to classical, ambient, lavish ballads and twinkling electronica, all sure to hit pleasure centres of anyone who fancies Romance, Jonny Greenwood’s ‘Phantom Thread’ OST, Enya’s crushed velvet wafters, or event schmaltziest ends of Leyland Kirby.
items._genre: contemporary classical / ambient / electronica / orchestral / choral
items._cn_summary: Oliver Coates 为同性题材电影《Pillion》创作配乐，将古典弦乐、键盘与合唱编排融合到电影叙事之中。乐评描述其编制饱满而层次丰富，兼具萨蒂式古典底蕴与梦幻氛围，还涉及精致电子音效，呈现出感性、迷离的听觉质感。整张配乐在浪漫旋律与抽象声响之间游走，既有传统管弦乐的抒情线条，也有现代电子质感的空间感。评论将其与Jonny Greenwood《Phantom Thread》原声、Enya的朦胧氛围及Leyland Kirby作品并列，暗示其风格偏向精致化、氛围化的当代古典。作为Aftersun配乐作者的新作，Coates展现了在电影配乐领域扩展个人声音美学的能力，将古典架构与电子肌理有机结合，适合偏好当代古典与氛围跨界融合的听众。

items.body:
Electronic Corporation "1998–2006", a compilation bringing together rare and long unavailable recordings by the German electronic projects heimelektronik and MAS 2008.

"Active around the turn of the millennium, both projects share the involvement of producer Ive Müller while developing distinct collaborations and approaches to electronic music. H.E.I.M. Elektronik was founded in 1996 by Holger Erlenwein and Ive Müller (after the two artists split in 1999, Müller continued using the name), while MAS 2008 is the project of Ive Müller together with René Kirchner. Though separate entities, the two projects explored a similar sonic territory: stripped-down electro, minimal electronics and machine-driven body music shaped by analog hardware and a raw DIY production ethos.

The roots of Müller’s work go back to the final years of the DDR. As a teenager he worked as a licensed DJ — officially known as a “Schallplattenunterhalter” — operating a travelling disco across Saxony. With limited access to official Western releases, music circulated through cassette recordings taped from West German radio stations such as RIAS Berlin, NDR2 and Bayern3. Together with friends he travelled between youth clubs and discos around Leipzig with a “rolling discotheque”: a Russian Wolga pulling a trailer loaded with Electro-Voice sound systems sourced through the black market.

At the turn of the 2000s this background in underground electronic culture resurfaced in a series of recordings rooted in electro, EBM and minimal machine music. The tracks collected on Electronic Corporation 2000–2002 capture this moment: cold sequences, driving rhythms and stark synthetic textures produced with a direct and uncompromising approach.

Compiled and remastered by Rude 66 from the original sources, Electronic Corporation 2000–2002 documents a small but fascinating chapter of German underground electronics from the early digital era."
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了德国电子项目heimelektronik与MAS 2008在1998至2006年间罕见的录音作品，两个项目均由制作人Ive Müller参与，以模拟硬件和DIY制作精神为核心，探索精简电子乐、极简电子与机器驱动的身体音乐。专辑记录了Müller从东德末期地下文化到千禧年初的创作轨迹：少年时期作为持证DJ在萨克森地区运营流动迪斯科，通过西德广播电台的磁带录音接触电子音乐，最终在2000年前后将这些经历转化为冷峻序列、机械节奏与粗粝合成器质感的作品。由荷兰制作人Rude 66从原始音源编译并重新母带处理，呈现了德国早期数字时代地下电子音乐中一个虽小但引人入胜的篇章。

items.body:
44 years after its original release, the 7” by German group DEUTSCHE SCHÄFERHUNDE (engl. German shepherds) - remastered and reissued for the first time on Anna Logue Records.

"Recorded in the winter of 1981/82 between rehearsal space, provincial disco and bar nights, and a humble four-track setup, these tracks capture the raw spirit of a generation that simply started creating—no formal training, but plenty of attitude. Minimalist, uncompromising, and inspired by krautrock, punk, new wave, electronic music and dub, the songs move between raw electronics, percussive noise, new wave experimentation, and sharp social commentary. „Rosa Brille“ (rose coloured glasses) in particular feels as urgent today as it did back then—a track that has lost none of its relevance, „Gasmasken“ tells of gas masks dancing in the woods to the sound of sirens, and a timeless Holger Czukay/Jah Wobble inspired „Mein Herz“ (my heart).

Originally pressed in a small run of just 500 copies and later becoming a sought-after collector’s item now worth 200€, the record now returns in a carefully crafted edition featuring a laser-printed reverse side and additional materials such as original lyric sheets and articles, postcard and poster. DEUTSCHE SCHÄFERHUNDE thrived on paradox—a provocative name paired with a clear stance, and lyrics that still resonate today. Shaped by Cold War tension, political unease, and youthful rebellion, their sound refused to fit into any neat category. Only few other bands, such as Der Musikant, Im Namen des Volkes, Thorax Wach, Klinisch Sauber oder Stephan Eicher spielt Noise Boys come to mind."
items._genre: post-punk / new wave / experimental electronic / krautrock-influenced
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国乐队Deutsche Schäferhunde于1981/82年冬季在排练室与酒吧之间用简陋四轨设备录制的7寸单曲，44年后由Anna Logue Records首次重新母带处理再版发行。作品融合了极简电子、打击噪音、新浪潮实验与尖锐的社会评论，受Krautrock、朋克、电子音乐与Dub多重影响。歌曲在粗糙电子声景与节奏化噪音之间游走，歌词涉及冷战张力、政治不安与青年反叛，诸如《Rosa Brille》关于粉红色滤镜的隐喻至今仍具现实意义，《Gasmasken》描绘防毒面具在森林中随警笛起舞的画面，《Mein Herz》则带有Holger Czukay与Jah Wobble式的贝斯质感。原版仅压制500张，曾是收藏市场追捧的稀有品，再版附加原始歌词页、文章、明信片与海报等丰富材料。

items.body:
Modular bod M. Geddes Gengras gets the band back together on 'Guestlist', roping in an estimable team of collaborators (including Christina Carter, WANDA GROUP, Greg Fox, Ben Chasny and Meg Duffy, among others) to recapture the lightning in a bottle energy of Chicago's early post-rock era, when sounds would criss-cross over each other relatively freely.

Despite technology being accessible, commonplace even, it's still relatively difficult to find the sweet spot between live instrumentation and electronics. Modular synthesis, that thrives on its self-contained, often unpredictable moments of serendipity, adds an even more problematic element. You can make it work, sure, but so much of what we like about modular music is that it doesn't feel as if it's been looped into structures that file down its sharp edges. Gengras sets himself a challenge here, working like a synthesist but also drawing on his experience playing in bands - he sees both sides, which gives him a head-start. And he's also got the good sense to think back to an era where the possibilities felt endless: the "early Pro Tools" era as James Toth writes in the accompanying notes, when bands like Tortoise and The Sea and Cake were looking at artists like Autechre and AFX and wondering what techniques they could integrate.

And 'Guest List' is undoubtedly Gengras' most ambitious record to date. There's more to it than personnel, too - proper songs, a far cry from the hazy new age-tinted synth jams that we heard on 'Expressed, I Noticed Silence' or the post-kosmische "ROMpler worship" of 'QUIK-MELT', appear in the dense tangle of instruments and expressions. While the 11-minute 'The List is Millions Long' initially seems to not-so-subtly reference Tortoise's 'Millions Now Living...' with its chiming guitars and motorik beat (supplied by Portland-based sound artist Colin Blanton, no less), it gets more complicated when Will Epstein's saxophone enters the frame. And that harmonic complexity remains when the track melts into 'Laplace/Montagne' and Gengras' synth belches are augmented by Chasny's golden shreds. Hell, there are even vocals on 'Seven Dials' provided by Austin's Cory Plump, who shouts listlessly over Gengras' sunny arpeggios, Fox's drums and Duffy's riffs.

Prepare yourself, 'Guest List' is not the M. Geddes Gengras you're likely to be expecting. There's even a spoken word intro to the album's brilliant finale '"The Weather"' from cult social media star and sometime genius WANDA GROUP. Proper good.
items._genre: experimental electronic / post-rock / synth / motorik / krautrock-influenced
items._cn_summary: 模块合成玩家M. Geddes Gengras在这张专辑中召集了Christina Carter、Greg Fox、Ben Chasny、Meg Duffy等横跨实验与独立场景的音乐人，试图重现芝加哥早期后摇滚时代那种不同声响自由交织的能量。他将模块合成的不确定性与乐队化编制结合：motorik律动、敲击吉他、萨克斯与合成器相互穿插，十一分钟的长曲在段落之间缓慢变形。WANDA GROUP的口白引入专辑终曲，Cory Plump的人声则覆盖于明亮的琶音之上。整体走向从以往偏氛围化的合成独奏转向更复杂的器乐织体，是Gengras迄今最具野心的项目。

items.body:
Danish composer Astrid Sonne opens up her heart on 'Great Doubt', singing candidly for the first time over powdery beats and jerky instrumentation (assisted by none other than Slauson Malone, Ben Vince, Levitation Orchestra's Emma Barnaby and Alvilda Reiter Jakobsen), and even referencing Mariah Carey. It's a revelation - and funny in places too - properly in line with Tirzah, ML Buch and HTRK.

We almost didn't recognize Sonne when we first spun 'Great Doubt'. Her voice - not her viola or rack of synths - takes the spotlight on 'Do you wanna', murmuring gently over brittle, tightly reverberating drums that Sonne plays herself. It's a far cry from the pitchy, jazz-inflected psychedelia of 2021's 'outside of your lifetime' or its vaporous predecessor 'Human Lines'. "Do you wanna have a baby?" she asks ruefully, leaving the question unanswered at first, room for strings, piano and subtle synths to reply. She strips herself naked, wondering what it might mean to bring a child into the world; it scrapes against Tirzah's 'Colourgrade' not just sonically but thematically. On that album, Tirzah contemplated motherhood and family - here, Sonne weighs up her choices, using the track's emptiness to suggest emotional malnutrition. "I don't know," she finally relents.

'Give my all' follows with boxy, disney strings and orchestral phrases that bring an uncanny drama to Sonne's blunt words. She sounds confident and forthright as she paraphrases Maria Carey: "I'd give my all to have / just one more night with you." The plasticity of the backdrop only makes the words resonate further, and it's this push and pull between artificiality and raw sensitivity that makes 'Great Doubt' so captivating. There's an unmistakable trip-hop impetus to 'Boost', that features Sonne on drums again, playing slowly alongside sampled woodwinds and fictile synths. There are no vocals on this one, so the instrumentation stands in, winding in and out of tune to poke out towards the boundaries. It's at this moment when Sonne sounds closest to her sometime collaborator ML Buch, bridging the gap between traditional songwriting and a simulated new age. But Sonne doesn't sound as if she's trying to approximate pop, just bare her soul more frankly.

And there are traces of her earlier material on the stand-out 'Staying here', when she coos more animatedly over organ-like arpeggios and digitized stabs. We can hear outlines of classic Enya or Kate Bush on this one, and while it's beatless, it sounds as if it's rushing towards a drop that never comes - all tension, no release. "Everything is unreal," she cries. "But I'm not going anywhere." Then we're led out with the folk-y 'Overture', that features Ben Vince on sax, and dubby closer 'Say you love me', the biggest indicator that she's now based in London. It's the most revealing, heart-puncturing material we've heard from Sonne to date, a hyper-literate wirework of influences and skills that's put together with care and no small amount of restraint. We're sold.
items._genre: experimental pop / art pop / electronic / contemporary composition
items._cn_summary: 丹麦作曲家Astrid Sonne在新专辑中首次以人声为主角，融合了脆弱的演唱、粉末化的电子节拍与锯齿状的器乐编排，合作者包括Slauson Malone、Ben Vince等。专辑探讨了生育选择、情感裸露等私密主题，以留白与回响制造情感张力。配器在迪士尼式管弦弦乐与失谐合成器之间游走，模糊了民谣写作与模拟新时代音乐之间的边界。部分曲目向Tirzah《Colourgrade》致敬，亦有trip-hop质感的器乐段落，整体呈现出人工感与原始敏感性的持续拉扯。

items._cn_summary: 这是Swans乐队2023-24年美欧巡演的现场录音合集，横跨布鲁克林与海牙两地的演出，时长接近三小时。专辑记录了乐队现场演出的原始面貌，这些素材也为乐队2025年5月发布的录音室专辑《Birthing》奠定了基础。音乐呈现出催眠式的旋律逐渐演变为密集音墙的过程，Gira标志性的嗓音贯穿始终，乐手使用滑棒吉他、贝斯、Mellotron和动态打击乐器构建层次。Gira本人形容这些作品是以灵魂撕裂般的投入和对声音真理的不懈追求锻造而成。整体延续了Swans一贯的极简重复与渐进累积手法，将现场能量以高音量直接传递给听众。

items.body:
Simon Shreeve (Mønic, CUB) sifts and tweaks nine personal highlights of his cult transition from D&B to dubstep circa the late ‘00s/early 2010s, all acutely advised to acolytes of Youngsta, SP:MC, Icicle, Raime, The Bug x Ghost Dubs, Mick Harris...

By the time Kryptic Minds switched from darkest D&B to dubstep in 2009, they were arguably late to the game, but heavily made their presence felt with a five year string of classics for Loefah’s Swamp81, Tectonic, and their own label, Osiris Music UK, now considered canon to the sound. ‘The Things They Left Behind’ now dusts off and refines nine crucial examples of how they brought D&B production values to the heel of its rogue sibling, dubstep, firmly living up to El-B’s original dream of fusing late ‘90s tech-step and darker UKG, but also augmented with careful measures of atmospheric trip hop sensuality that place it in the long shadow of UK gloom shrouding Burial and Pinch bits.

Basically it’s a director’s cut of 2011 album ‘Can’t Sleep’, all “reimagined, refined and 2026 remastered” to best tell his tale of that pivotal era. In passage from the pensive title tune to cinematic closer ‘1000 Lost Cities’, he tightens the screws and checks the brakes on a definitive redux, edging the rictus halfstep tension of ‘No More No Less’, and a spidery 2-step dissection ‘Alone’, along with the relatively sublime levity of ‘Fade to Nothing’, and what sounds like ‘Mezzanine’-era Massive Attack gone halfstep on ‘Myth’, thru to the digitally shivered delays of ‘Depth of Field’ and slicker retread of ‘A Glimpse of Hope’.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张对Kryptic Minds从D&B转向dubstep时期作品的重新整理与再混音专辑，由核心成员Simon Shreeve亲自操刀，将2011年专辑《Can't Sleep》中的九首曲目进行再构、精细化处理并以2026年标准重新母带。从沉思的标题曲到电影感十足的终曲《1000 Lost Cities》，专辑呈现出明显的情感递进：半步回响的紧张感、蜘蛛般细碎的2-step分解、以及带有Massive Attack式氛围的段落交织其中。制作上融合了90年代末tech-step与暗潮UKG的基因，承袭了Burial与Pinch所定义的英国忧郁美学，并注入trip hop的感官质感。低频设计沉稳，空间感与回声延迟处理细腻，整体在dubstep的沉重骨架上构建出适合深夜聆听的声音场景。

items.body:
UK born, Shanghai-based producer SHALT presents Votive via Infinite Machine.

"SHALT lands on Infinite Machine for a full-length. The album is entitled Votive, functioning as an exploration of memory and how, "over time, recollections of words and meanings become hazy and decayed, in turn taking on new forms and purposes

Votive comes from a sense of an offering in 'devotion to a memory'. The offering that Votive makes is an overt one, where very little is held back. In this spirit, the album wears emotion on its sleeve: the grooves, the chords, the melodies are big and immediate, especially at the front end of the album. As it progresses and over the second half it draws in on itself, becoming more reflexive but no less sentimental, and a poignant melody or atmosphere is never far at hand.

Mangled vocals appear and then recede throughout the proceedings. You’d be mistaken, however, if you thought this provides immediate humanity: the processing and the unintelligible words keep the warmth at arms’ length, as if dealing with ghosts. According to SHALT himself, “words are removed from their original context, given different meaning by recasting the voice into new elements, rather than relying on the original language itself”. Indeed, often, a voice can only barely be made out as such, morphed beyond recognition into a lead synth or an alien texture.

Overall, Votive is more cinematic and expansive than any of SHALT’s previous releases, as if the familiar traits and gestures (big square-wave basslines, 3-D IMAX leads) were given free rein and were finally allowed to stretch out to their full potential, freed from the constraints of the dancefloor."
items._cn_summary: SHALT 这张全长专辑以记忆的衰变与重构为核心概念，将人声采样经过深度处理后转化为合成器音色或陌生质感，使原本的语义被剥离并赋予新的意义。专辑前半部分律动饱满、和弦与旋律外放直白，后半段逐渐内敛转向沉思，情绪始终浓郁。人声被扭曲至几乎无法辨识，在温暖与疏离之间维持张力，仿佛与幽灵对话。整体编曲比以往更为电影化与宏放，粗犷的方波低音与立体声主奏旋律被释放出舞池的限制，获得充分展开。Infinite Machine 作为以实验电子与俱乐部语境著称的独立厂牌，与这张专辑的气质高度契合。

items.body:
Jackson Bailey & Luke Blair’s Cav Empt tape as Rezzett is a definitive dose of their signature crud, and now finally available to download on its tod. Fugged-out bass for the hardest-to-please lugs

Rezzett’s 3rd album ‘Into the Boiling Darks’ is now presented as 21 individual tracks, scraping their bin juice-soaked barrel for grittiest morsels of mutant dance music, now primed for DJ use, and also as a proper 72 minute dunk in their bilgy sound. You probably know what to expect from their 13 years of crooked productions, both in duo and solo as Tapes & Lukid, and it doesn’t disappoint for levels of thee scuzziest, sawn-off dance noise blatz.

They’ve clearly reserved some of the dankest in the dungeon for this album, laying it down thick and fuming in a mix of mildewed ambient vignettes, blown-out beatdown, Actress-alike deep bleep trodders, hobbled proto-house and fizzy clangerz that know no chill. If pushed to play faves, the Skaters-esque horn of ‘Bliss Up’ is one, as is the faded, romantic jungle tekno lustre of ‘Kissing Twelve’ and ‘Bongo Tax’, thru the manic rush of ‘In The Loneleyz’ and ‘Nirvana’, or the teeth-chatter gnash of ‘Kopli’, but it’s simply all gravy.
items._genre: experimental electronic / IDM / mutant dance / ambient
items._cn_summary: Rezzett 第三张专辑《Into the Boiling Darks》由 Cav Empt 厂牌发行，以21首独立曲目重新呈现，总时长72分钟。两位制作人 Jackson Bailey 与 Luke Blair 延续过去十三年在 Tapes 与 Lukid 名下的扭曲制作路线，将发霉的ambient小品、失真的节拍打击、Actress风格的深邃电子律动、跛行的proto-house以及尖锐的碎裂声响融合在一起。整体音色浑浊、潮湿、低保真，bass线条被故意做得模糊与脱节，鼓机在工业噪音与丛林律动之间摇摆。乐评特别提到了几首亮点曲目：小号采样的'Bliss Up'、带有浪漫丛林光泽的'Kissing Twelve'与'Bongo Tax'、躁动的'In The Loneleyz'与'Nirvana'，以及锋利粗粝的'Kopli'。这是一张定位明确、风格统一的地下电子实验作品，适合在俱乐部深夜时段或耳机独处时聆听。

items.body:
Planted and watered by Horn of Plenty's Deutsche operative Nein Rodere (aka David Roeder) and Providence-based PPM-affiliated Nowhere Flower (aka Lila Jarzombek), Nein Flower roots itself in wyrd folk and outsider musick history, sucking up nutrients from Christina Carter, Sun City Girls, The Shadow Ring and Jandek in the process.

We can't be sure whether Roeder and Jarzombek were in the same room together when these ramshackle tracks were made, but 'Nein Flower' sounds spontaneous in a way that feels unconnected to modern wireless technology. They're both visual artists as well as musicians, and found a deep connection, despite growing up on different continents. And although both locations clearly feed into the music - Berlin's restless, punkish isolation and Providence's basement-dwelling, lo-fidelity introspection - the session sounds like it was recorded from beginning to end in a third space, directly to tape. 

It's as if Graham Lambkin and Darren Harris (circa 'City Lights') were tasked with recording an early Charalambides side - blown out, dissonant and poetic - but strangely tuned in with folk history, too. Both Roeder and Jarzombek seem to share all duties, with Jarzombek's smudgy coos wisping and whirling around Roeder's surreal Lou Reed-inspired narrations and instrumentation, appearing and falling away unceremoniously. 

Nein Flower is about capturing the moment; an impromptu back-and-forth that’s fully mesmerising. In the accompanying press release, the duo talk about naïve art and no-frills performance; composition, they explain, is landscape painting and their details are fully revealed when you look a little closer, finding elements that are less obviously premeditated. And honestly, it's a technique that works for them - not only does the album feel completely honest in a way that's genuinely charming, but it places them in an unusual artistic plane that's teetering between nostalgia and innovation. It's tangible, messy and alluring stuff, intimate, often grotesque, always compelling.
items._genre: experimental folk / outsider music / lo-fi / drone folk / psychedelic
items._cn_summary: 这是两位视觉艺术家出身的音乐人跨越柏林与普罗维登斯的远程合作专辑，根植于奇异民谣与局外人音乐传统，汲取Christina Carter、Jandek和Sun City Girls的营养。整张专辑以即时即兴的方式直接录制到磁带，摒弃现代无线技术的精致感，呈现出粗粝、失谐而诗意的声响质地。Jarzombek模糊的人声吟唱与Roeder受Lou Reed启发的超现实叙事及器乐演奏交织缠绕，彼此呼应又随意消散。乐评将其比作Graham Lambkin与Charalambides早期作品的结合，捕捉了naïve art式的无修饰表演美学。专辑在怀旧与创新之间找到了独特的平衡位置，私密、凌乱却极具吸引力，每一处细节都值得近距离倾听。

items.body:
5 Gate Temple’s Danish binds yield another crooked gem with sound artist Victoria Mingot’s enchantingly casual, even barely-there, lower case strums and murmurs, like diaries of broken sleep FFO Joane Robertson, Loren Connors, Graham Lambkin.

5GT’s Danish affiliations now reach to Victoria Mingot and ‘God Spill’, which takes CPH’s lonely solo songwriter thing to its quietest, most ruminative depths. Her dozen pieces are mostly instrumental, defined by plaintive melodic structuring for acoustic guitar on what sounds like dictaphone recordings that imbue everything with a eerie intimacy. However, there are vocals, and they’re pretty special when they do appear, like a flickering filament in the aether of ‘i saw the sign’, recalling Mary Maddox off Mike Ratledge’s ‘Riddles of the Sphinx’, floating, Virginia Astley-like, on the frayed Lambkin-esque strum of ‘in plentitude of the harvest’, or more textural in the mournful raga meditation ‘om dhyana’.

This exquisitely discreet balance of unshowy yet transfixing instrumental economy makes other works such as ‘before you fly’ stand out even more for its shimmering blend of Joanne Robertson and Loren Connors-like substance, and the whole record fully reveals itself with repeat listens.
items._genre: experimental folk / lowercase / ambient acoustic / lo-fi
items._cn_summary: Victoria Mingot的专辑《God Spill》由哥本哈根5 Gate Temple厂牌发行，以十二首极简吉他短曲为主轴，大量采用录音笔式低保真录音质地，营造出失眠日记般的私密氛围。大部分为器乐作品，吉他弹奏带有冥想式的忧郁旋律线，偶尔出现的人声如细丝般漂浮在音景之中，与Joane Robertson、Loren Connors、Graham Lambkin等低保真独奏传统形成呼应。专辑在'om dhyana'中融入印度拉格冥想元素，展现跨文化融合倾向。整体制作刻意保持低调内敛，摒弃修饰，依靠重复聆听逐步展开其微妙层次。独立小厂牌发行，契合地下实验民谣与极简声响美学的交汇地带。

items.body:
Deaf Center member Otto A Totland’s 2014 debut LP, an intricate work for solo piano.

"Otto A Totland's modern compositional elements are most widely recognized as half of the Norwegian duo Deaf Center, where his melancholic, intricate piano work provides haunting relief to the beds of noise and deep strings from Erik K Skodvin. Pinô is the first full-length release by Totland, though his solo work has been released once, as the 5-minute A-side of Sonic Pieces 7inch Harmony From the Past. Otto's previously brief vignettes are now expanded into a fully personal realization of his own style.

Initial track Open fills itself with heavy, knowing pauses that quickly become overwhelmed with the desire to understand what's to come. Each silence leads into quick flutters of keys, preparing the listener for a vast terrain of giddy beauty, bleak depths, and true contentedness. Pinô quickly recalls deep winter; in front of a fireplace for days on end, you lose how far along you've ventured into the 18 tracks without any idea how far is left to go. The experience feels inevitable, with no other option but to curl up somewhere cozy and appreciate the sense of timelessness that Totland has created. His album is a haunting modern compositional treasure, expressed through instrumentals completely unique to Totland and captured masterfully by Nils Frahm at Durton Studios.

With Pinô, Otto A Totland appears out of the Norwegian landscape, sharing an achievement that will provide a relief during the brooding winter darkness. Though a highly personal endeavor, the recognizable continuation of Totland’s compositions will attract fans of Deaf Center, and the cinematic and classical components of his solo work will hold sway for those familiar with Harold Budd or Dustin O’Halloran."
items._genre: contemporary classical / modern composition / solo piano / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这是挪威作曲家Otto A Totland的首张全长独奏钢琴专辑，由Nils Frahm在Durton Studios录制完成。Totland此前作为Deaf Center成员广为人知，其作品中忧郁而精细的钢琴音色与深沉弦乐交织。本专辑将他过去的简短片段扩展为完整的个人风格表达，十八首曲目构建出广阔的情感地形——既有欢愉的美感，也有荒凉的深渊。作品具有强烈的电影感和古典美学底蕴，与Harold Budd、Dustin O'Halloran的意境相呼应。专辑营造出深冬壁炉前的沉浸氛围，沉默与音符交替推进，呈现出一种超越时间流动的聆听体验，是当代器乐创作中兼具个人化表达与北欧忧郁气质的作品。

items.body:
Vibrant reminders of the Éthiopiques series’ peerless ‘60s/‘70s brilliance, collated by Francis Falcetto, the man who brought the sounds back into circulation via Buda Musique in the late ‘90s.

First introduced to us by Shackleton, and maybe best known to many for heavy rotation on Jim Jarmusch’s ‘Broken Flowers’ (2005), the Éthiopiques series showcases a relatively short-lived but incredible explosion of jazz, funk and Afrobeat-adjacent grooves that emerged from Addis Ababa in the ‘60s, mostly issued on the labels Amha, Kaifa, and Philips-Ethiopia, but sadly all curtailed by political revolution by the late ‘70s. 

For the uninitiated or keen admirers ‘Heavenly Ethiopiques: The Best Of The Ethiopiques Series’ yields a best-of cornucopia of infectious tunes by the sound’s founding fathers - Mulatu Astatke, Mahmoud Ahmed and Tilahun Gessesse - and their crackshot players, such as Wallias Band, sequencing a range of blazing to cool, and always sophisticated, vocal tunes and taut, breakbeat-led instrumentals bound to ignite love for this sound or rekindle old passions.
items._genre: Ethiopian jazz / funk / Afrobeat / world music
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Francis Falcetto策划，精选自Bud Musique在1990年代末重新发行的Éthiopiques系列。内容聚焦于1960至1970年代阿迪斯阿贝巴音乐场景的黄金时期，汇集了Mulatu Astatke、Mahmoud Ahmed、Tilahun Gessesse等开创性人物及其伴奏乐队如Wallias Band的作品。乐评指出该系列展现了爵士、放克与Afrobeat邻近律动的短暂而璀璨的融合，曲目从炽热到冷静皆有，器乐部分以紧凑的碎拍节奏为骨架，人声曲目则始终保持精致格调。音乐发行曾因政治变革而中断，这套合辑为新听众提供了了解这段被遗忘历史的入口，也为熟悉者重新点燃对该声音的热爱。乐评来源为Boomkat，文字质量充分但偏向介绍性质。

items.body:
Italian club shapeshifter Piezo pulls from a native history of cosmic disco, trance and electronica on a diverse handful of aces nodding to Beppe Loda, Marco Passarani and Donato Dozzy.

Named for the Tibetan funerary rite, ‘Sky Burial’ follows in a guess-again run of dub, hard drum, and breaks-driven works of the past decade to portray Piezo at full dancefloor wingspan. They’re all fine-tuned for effortless motion, from a sleek title tune that spotlights how synth-pop paved the way for trance - think Chris & Cosey-meets-Pet Shop Boys - thru the urgently uptempo yet elegant electronica of ‘Their Amnesiac Colours’ harking late ‘90s Pssarani via Orbital, and the D’Arcangelo-type braindance of ‘Vimelodica’, next to something like Beppe Loda meets Black Merlin on ‘Bardo Climax’, and echoes of Donato Dozzy’s take on modern Roman trance in ‘Trunks’.
items._cn_summary: 意大利制作人Piezo在这张专辑中回溯本土电子乐传统，从宇宙迪斯科到迷幻trance再到硬核鼓击与碎拍，每首作品都指向意大利电子史上的关键坐标。标题曲以合成器流行为桥接，串联起八九十年代trance的脉络；其他曲目则分别向Marco Passarani九十年代末的electronica、Donato Dozzy的罗马trance、Beppe Loda的迷幻舞曲等前辈致敬。整张专辑围绕舞池展开，强调律动的流动感与精致编排，作品虽以跳舞为核心目的，却在风格谱系上呈现出清晰的脉络意识与跨年代拼贴手法。专辑名取自西藏天葬仪式，但这一文化指涉更多停留在概念层面而非声音本身，乐评集中讨论的仍是欧洲地下电子舞曲谱系内部的对话。

items.body:
A six-part song cycle, Aliya Ultan's first solo album for Kou Records a celebration of the cello that stretches its range, letting it inhabit multiple registers at once.

Ultan came up with 'Looks Far Woman' when she felt burned out, expended utterly after years of arduous touring, teaching and constantly collaborating. But she still couldn't rest; her sessions became a way for Ultan to reconnect with the cello, using the hypnagogic state she was in to isolate its wooziest, most unusual textures. And its six songs examine each way the cello can be approached: on 'Road Song', it represents an open landscape as Ultan strums the strings and plays elongated drones; 'Wind Song' is gusty and dissonant; 'Mountain Song' is imposing and seismic; on 'Sky Song', Ultan lets weightlessness elevate her fictile notes; she reduces the sound to dusty granules on 'Seed Song'; and lets romance crack through the darkness on the moody finale, 'Heart Song'.
items._cn_summary: 这是一部由大提琴家 Aliya Ultan 创作并演奏的六乐章声乐套曲，也是她在 Kou Records 厂牌的首张个人专辑。在长期巡演、教学与合作的消耗之后，她在半梦半醒的状态下重新接近这件乐器，试图挖掘大提琴最隐秘、最不寻常的纹理。六首曲目分别从不同角度探索大提琴的可能性：《Road Song》以拨弦与持续低音营造开阔风景；《Wind Song》呈现气流般的不协和感；《Mountain Song》厚重而具有地震般的压迫力；《Sky Song》释放失重感；《Seed Song》将声音压缩为粉尘般的颗粒；终曲《Heart Song》则在暗色情绪中透出一丝浪漫裂缝。整体上，专辑以一件传统乐器为媒介，却跨越了当代作曲、声音艺术与氛围音乐的边界。

items.body:
Gorgeous DIY, private press, lounge jazz and Latin boogie stardust from 1984, framing keyboard maestro Ronald Langestraat in his living room, laying down pure vibes to 4-track - huge tip FFO Lewis, Gil Scott Heron, James Mason, Starship Commander Woooo Wooooo.

"Searching was self-recorded in Ronald’s living room on a 4-Track Tape Recorder in 1984. The recordings symbolise his engagement to cross-over everything that was known to him musically at that time. Most importantly, all recordings reflect his personal way of searching; searching for his own characteristic sound. Rhythmical patterns meet well balanced distortion, shaping the music into a mirror of his character. He was part of several Dutch Latin and Jazz bands, including Cascada and Ritmo Natural. With the latter he performed at Holland’s North Sea Jazz Festival. At this point Ronald is 78 years old, playing music every day.

Instruments: Acoustic Piano, Fender Rhodes Piano, Farfisa Organ, String Ensemble, Tenor Sax, Alt Sax, Soprano Sax, Clarinet, Alt Clarinet, Organ Bass, Micro Moog, Drums, Longa & Voices.”
items._genre: lounge jazz / Latin boogie / private press DIY
items._cn_summary: 这张1984年的私人出版专辑由荷兰键盘演奏家Ronald Langestraat在自家客厅用四轨磁带录音机完成录制，展现了他在爵士与拉丁波萨之间的跨界探索。录音中运用了电钢琴、Farfisa风琴、弦乐合成器、萨克斯家族、合成器贝斯及鼓机等丰富乐器，构建出节奏感强烈且带有微妙失真质感的融合音色。整体风格在lounge jazz的松弛氛围中融入拉丁律动与早期合成器音色，既保留了现场即兴的温度，也透露出家庭录音特有的粗粝感。Langestraat曾参与Cascada和Ritmo Natural等荷兰拉丁爵士乐队，并在北海爵士节演出，如今已78岁仍坚持每日演奏。这张专辑作为DIY私人出版的稀有录音，呈现了一位音乐人在有限条件下对个人声音的真诚追寻。

items.body:
As O.G. Jigg, Will “Memotone” Yates adapts his broad palette to the 16mm documentary and folk horror short imagery of Graham Vasey’s film project, The Black Tor, with an unmistakably vintage tone FFO Oskar Sala, Delia Derbyshire, Gruppo.

Named for the granite outcrop of Dartmoor, not too far from the musician’s native Bristol, ‘Black Tor Tracks’ depicts Yates in actual soundtrack mode, as opposed to imaginary. It gathers six instrumental accompaniments written between 2022-2026 that match the oneiric anachronisms of County Durham based Graham Vasey’s films with masterful blends of analog electronics and acoustic kit rendered in widescreen and dusted with a tone that reflects the filmmaker’s use of a 1950s Bolex and a 1930s Ensign Auto-Kinecam. 

If we weren’t informed otherwise, the music could easily pass for ‘50s or ’60 orchestral scores in a classic vein of British folk horror, or even Bernard Herrmann’s work for Hitchcock psychological thrillers - and by extension, even Oskar Sala in its electronic nuance - such is the timeless quality of Yates’ touch as O.G. Jigg. Severed from intended imagery the music remains potently synaesthetic, from the gloomy brood of ‘The Black Tor’, thru the celluloid dream sequence evocation of ‘The Sunken Kirk’, fine-wrought early electronic timbres of ‘Woodwose’ and ‘The Stones of Obb’, and hallucinatory tension of ‘Plough Stots’.

Good stuff.
items._genre: experimental electronic / analog soundtrack / folk horror score / vintage electroacoustic
items._cn_summary: 音乐人O.G. Jigg（Will "Memotone" Yates）为Graham Vasey的16mm纪录片与民间恐怖短片项目The Black Tor创作了六首器乐配乐，写作跨度从2022至2026年。作品以模拟电子与原声乐器为核心媒介，刻意营造出五十至六十年代英国民间恐怖片配乐的时代质感，同时融入Oskar Sala式的电子音色细微处理与Bernard Herrmann式的心理悬疑张力。Yates的配乐具有强烈的通感特质，即便脱离影像单独聆听，依然能唤起胶片梦境般的画面联想——从阴郁压抑的氛围铺陈，到早期电子音色的精细雕琢，再到幻觉式紧张感的层层递进。模拟合成器与原声乐器的宽广声场混融，赋予音乐一种超越时代的永恒质感。

items.body:
Mexico’s 1OO1O twists the dembow beat in deep house, halfstep D&B, footwork-jungle and tekno permutations on Florentino’s hugely distinctive label. RIYL Nick León, Arca, DJ Python

Running quicksilver on the heels of his ‘Tribalista’ EP for Tra Tra Trax, and Club Romantico’s Safety Trance LP, the Mexico City resident exerts a deftly sharp, Latinate spin on well worn ideas. We’re particularly partial to the neuro D&B mutation of ‘Lo Que Quiero’, voiced by a sultry Rico Rica, and the brisk jungle-footwork flight ‘Amargo’, but it’s all dead solid clubaction; from the slow/fast doble paso percolation and Eski flute motifs of ‘Tres de Espadas’, thru the pendulous pressure of ‘Candelita’, and peak time gait of ‘Báilalo Rico’, again with Rico Rica.
items._cn_summary: 墨西哥制作人1OO1O在Florentino厂牌发行专辑《Tres De Espadas》，将dembow节拍解构后融入deep house、半速鼓打贝斯、footwork-jungle及tekno等多种俱乐部舞曲变体。这张专辑延续了他此前在Tra Tra Trax的'Tribalista'EP以及Club Romantico合辑《Safety Trance》中的拉丁俱乐部路线，以锐利的制作手法对既有舞曲范式进行重新诠释。作品《Lo Que Quiero》展现了神经质鼓打贝斯的变体形态，Rico Rica献声演绎；《Amargo》则是快节奏jungle-footwork的飞行段落；同名曲《Tres De Espadas》融合慢/快双步节奏与Eski笛子旋律动机；《Candelita》呈现钟摆式的下沉压力；《Báilalo Rico》以Rico Rica的声线打造峰时段律动。整体围绕俱乐部场景的功能性展开，在拉丁节奏基因与欧洲俱乐部美学之间建立对话。

items.body:
Part 2 of a 12" series featuring Beatrice M.’s 'Sinking', the rudely aerodynamic debut LP where Tectonic's franco-british hope flexes a signature balance of ruff & smooth, building on a solid reputation earned via 12”s with her label, Bait, plus Tempa and Darwin’s SPE:C.

Dubstep is not necessarily an album genre: beyond scant examples from the likes of Burial, Shackleton, or 2562, 12”s and DJ sets serve the sound in best context. However, Beatrice M.’s grasp of subtle sensuality and propulsive traction patently ends itself well to the format on ’Sinking’, with rolling, stepping and skanking permutations that deftly dance in the space between dubstep, proper, and its close-related cousins - UKG, broken beat, dub techno - with a finely measured proprioception of space, weight and pressure. 

Along with 2562’s recently dispensed ‘Lost Dubs 2006-09’, ’Sinking’ is arguably the best thing on Tectonic in recent memory, with a sound that revels in more ambiguous club suss. It’s the type of release primed for cans/buds as much as big cones, proving she’s equally adept at sublime tension, as in the weightless love note ‘Dear Dubstep’, and thru the 2562-like fluid hydrodynamics of ‘Juice.’.
items._genre: dubstep / UKG / broken beat / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Beatrice M.的首张全长LP，延续了她在Tectonic、Bait、Tempa等厂牌发行12寸单曲时建立的声誉。评论指出dubstep通常更适合12寸单曲和DJ set而非专辑形式，但Beatrice M.对微妙感性氛围与推进力的把握，使她能够驾驭这一长篇格式。作品在dubstep与UKG、broken beat、dub techno之间游走，对空间、重量与压力有精确感知。专辑中既有'般轻盈的情书'Dear Dubstep展现的张力之美，也有像Juice这样充满流动液压感的作品。评论将其与2562近期作品并列为Tectonic近年的最佳发行之一，乐迷既能在耳机中细品，也能在大型音响系统中感受其冲击力。

items.body:
Echospace Detroit’s Stephen Hitchell is at his most romantic, club-friendly and elemental on these effortless dub house glyders, newly remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion

Originally issued on 12” in 2015 and hard-to-find ever since, ‘Lost Sequence’ is classic, archetypal Echospace tackle. The OG goes for 14 mins of strutting deep house groove swaddled in velvet-coated textures dubbed to the rafters and happy to hold its lane for the duration, adding extra layers of conga and crackling atmosphere as it proceeds. Hitchell’s Intrusion dub pitches the same elements in a spring weather system, drenching everything in fine mist of elemental FX and loosening the bass drum to a satisfyingly soggy slosh for 16 minutes of hypnotic bliss out.
items._genre: dub house / dub techno / ambient house
items._cn_summary: 这张作品由底特律Echospace的Stephen Hitchell创作，是其浪漫化、俱乐部友好且回归元素本源的dub house系列。原始曲目以14分钟的深层house律动为核心，铺陈天鹅绒质感的声音纹理，混响深重，节奏平稳贯穿全程，过程中逐步叠加康加鼓与细碎氛围层。Hitchell的Intrusion混音版将相同元素置于春雨般的气候系统中，用元素化的FX细雾浸润一切，放松底鼓使之变得松软潮湿，在16分钟内构建出催眠般的迷幻漂浮感。整张作品经过Pole重新母带处理，追求最佳沉浸感。原版2015年以12寸发行后长期绝版，此次重制版令这张经典的Echospace式dub house得以再度被聆听。

items._cn_summary: 这是Lance Austin Olsen与Jamie Drouin暌违六年的首张音乐合作专辑。两人此前主要从事视觉艺术和漫画书项目，并经历了漫长的新冠疫情期。专辑延续了他们以往的声音探索路线，使用多种声学与电子乐器及物件，包括洋琴、大提琴、钢琴、儿童吉他与训练吉他、各种物件，以及无线电、笔记本电脑、放大器等非乐器音源。两位音乐家在跨界合作中融合了原声乐器的物理质感与电子媒介的抽象处理，呈现出介于即兴与构图之间的实验声响。作为Free Jazz Blog报道的对象，专辑展现了独立实验音乐场景中跨媒介艺术家的典型创作路径。

items._cn_summary: 贝丝·奥顿时隔四年推出的新作，是其三十周年纪念节点上的重要作品。延续前作自我制作的方式，与汤姆·斯金纳、尼克·哈基姆等爵士与电子领域的音乐人合作，将爵士即兴元素和环境音乐质感编织进原本的民谣底色之中。专辑整体呈现冥想式的氛围，旋律在简约框架内展开，随时间推移逐渐显露作为词曲创作者的成熟质地。编曲兼顾亲密的温度与开阔的规模感，使声场层次在克制的表达中不断向外延展。文中提及卡罗尔·金式的怀旧侧面，暗示作品并未完全脱离传统旋律的滋养，而是在此基础上追求更深远的精神空间。

items.body: [PLAYLIST] Ron Wilson kam aus Kalifornien, blieb wegen des Militärs in der Region Lüttich/Maastricht – und komponierte dort das Repertoire einer Band, die er mit Jacques Pelzer, dessen Tochter Micheline und Cousin Steve Houben aus Jam-Sessions in Lüttich formte. Open Sky Unit, 1974 live im Jazzland Club aufgenommen, klingt nicht nach Fusion-Spektakel. Man hört Jazz, Soul, Funk und freie Improvisation – aber nichts davon drängt nach vorne. Ein Stück heißt »Passion and Compassion«: Leidenschaft und Mitgefühl, das trifft die Haltung. Die Musik verhält sich zu Fusion-Jazz wie Antifolk zu Folk: selbes Material, weniger Hochglanz, mehr Direktheit. Ab dem 31. Juli gibt es Open Sky Unit in Zusammenarbeit mit Sdban Records bei HHV exklusiv in einer auf 300 Stück limitierten Orange-Vinyl-Edition. Im HHV Shop kaufenOpen Sky UnitOpen Sky Unit HHV Summer Of Jazz Exclusive Orange Vinyl Editionab 30.99€ Passion and Compassion Die Band tourte bis etwa 1975/76, ehe Steve Houben nach Boston ans Berklee College of Music ging. Aus der Hommage an Dave Liebmans 1973er Album Open Sky wurde so eine eigene europäische Form von Jazz-Funk – eine, die nicht groß auftreten musste, um großartig zu sein. Ron Wilson zog später nach Deutschland und nahm 1985 mit Bill »Zuckerpuppe aus der Bauchtanz-Gruppe« Ramsey ein Swingalbum auf.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1974年在比利时列日Jazzland俱乐部录制的现场专辑，由美国加利福尼亚乐手Ron Wilson与比利时萨克斯手Jacques Pelzer、其女Micheline及堂亲Steve Houben组成的Open Sky Unit共同呈现。乐评将其风格定位为爵士、放克、灵魂乐与自由即兴的交汇，整体气质不追求融合爵士的华丽铺陈，而是以朴素直接的方式呈现素材本身。标题曲《Passion and Compassion》点明了乐队的创作姿态——热情与共情兼具。乐评将该专辑比作Antifolk之于Folk的关系：同样的原材料，更少的高光修饰，更直接的触感。专辑向Dave Liebman 1973年作品《Open Sky》致敬，并在此基础上发展出独特的欧洲爵士放克语言。这张唱片由Sdban Records与HHV合作发行300张限量橙色黑胶版本，在主流爵士市场上具有较高的收藏稀缺性。

items.body: Beside your oldness Beyond words and measure I marvel at your strength I marvel at your dignity SNEERS. treat the body as a suspect instrument: a vessel for appetite, prayer, revulsion, and endurance. On Mothers & Others, from the duo’s latest record, (Don’t Quit Before) The Miracle—released on vinyl and in digital format via Manchester-based label God Unknown Records—that body grows old before our ears. M. Greta Blaankart sings as though the voice has become a brittle room, her performance taking on the wheezing death rattle of a dying matriarch. It carries the tremor of an elderly woman, the dry lift of someone summoning strength from a chair, a kitchen table, a bed, a doorway. The song turns aging away from abstraction and toward domestic detail. Its subject is care, but care rendered without decorative softness. The lyrics gather around the ordinary miracles of answering the phone, remaining available, staying home, and offering love without judgment. These gestures, on paper, could seem plain. Blaankart gives them the gravity of survival. Her phrasing bends around each line as though time itself has made the throat uneven, and that unevenness becomes the point: affection here depends on bodies that falter, memories that blur, and days that must be repeated because repetition is how the living are kept alive. Leon’s video extends that idea with severe tenderness. An aged maternal figure performs small tasks, again and again, until routine begins to resemble fate. The actions appear almost emptied of purpose, then gradually regain meaning through duration. A hand moves, a body rises, a chore continues. The clip finds sacrifice in the plain machinery of daily life, especially the kind undertaken by women whose labor is usually absorbed into walls, meals, washed fabric, and silence. The maternal presence becomes animal, sacred, exhausted, and persistent, closer to birth than biography. Watch the video for Mothers & Others below: SNEERS. is a woman-led music project spearheaded by Italian singer and guitarist M. Greta Blaankart with drummer Leonardo O. Stefenelli. Initially formed in Berlin and later moving to Rome, the duo crafts a sinister, hallucinatory expedition into human despair, driven by the raw emotional power of Blaankart’s lyrics. Their work, characterized by blood-soaked poetry and luminous melancholia, pays tribute to spirituality and guilt. SNEERS.’s exploration of heaven and hell is documented in their 2018 studio album *Heaven Will Rescue Us, We’re the Scum, We’re in the Sun*, which features Kristof Hahn of Swans on lap-steel guitar. They also collaborated with Freddie Lee of Father Murphy on *Tales for Violent Days* in 2022. After four years of silence, SNEERS. returned with renewed intensity on (Don’t Quit Before) The Miracle, produced by Jamie Stewart of Xiu Xiu. The album was preceded by To My Serpent, You, which was released on March 6, 2026. Its first single was a haunting, cinematic track that featured eerie vocals, sparse percussion, and built up to a powerful crescendo. Leon, who has managed the project’s visual style from the start, also created a minimalist video for it. Speaking about the record, SNEERS. explains: “(Don’t Quit Before) The Miracle presents itself, starting from its very title, as a metaphor for human existence, centered on the anticipation of an epic turning point capable of giving meaning to life. One becomes lost in a belief that gradually weakens, almost fading away, leaving room for resignation. Yet it is precisely at this moment that one must not retreat: it becomes necessary to rediscover the spirit of younger days, with a mother’s strength, to shed one’s skin like snakes, and to follow a current of hope. Even when the only hope left is that of a miracle.” Listen to Mothers & Others below and order (Don’t Quit Before) The Miracle here. (Don’t Quit Before) The Miracle by SNEERS. items.body: Pulling out my sutures Pulling out Let the blood let For the last time get out now Sleep Of Mirrors’ Not My Skin comes slithering out of the Chicago cable-laced gutter with its teeth filed down and its nerves exposed, a bass-driven slab of dark electronic body panic featuring Ronnie Canizaro (Born of Osiris) in a role that may surprise anyone expecting the usual metalworld detonation. Here he sounds less like a frontman trying to split the ceiling and more like a man transmitting from inside the walls, whispering through drywall, steel, dodgy wiring, and whatever awful private chamber keeps producing the self you wake up inside. The track, from Sleep Of Mirrors’ debut album Crown, out now via Negative Gain Productions, plants Canizaro in a colder habitat: darkwave, electro, dark techno, industrial pressure, and the bruised mechanical glide one might file somewhere between Nine Inch Nails, Front Line Assembly, later Gary Numan, and Ministry at their most bad-tempered. The bassline does the stalking. The electronics scrape and tighten around it. Every element seems greased with hospital antiseptic and club-floor dread, the kind of music that understands the body as equipment, accident, prison, disguise, and evidence. Not My Skin is about identity as an emergency. The lyrics keep returning to secrecy, blood, sutures, alien flesh, and sightless guilt, as if confession has become a surgical procedure performed without anesthesia. “Don’t tell” becomes less a warning than a reflex, the old instruction of someone trained to bury pain until the burial site starts breathing. When the refrain circles back to “Not my skin” and “Eyeless sin,” the song enters that grim zone where the self feels assigned, assembled, and possibly counterfeit. The ending it imagines is no clean liberation. It feels closer to rupture, panic, and a last exit from a world whose rules have suddenly become unbearable. Directed and produced by Christopher Lee, with cinematography by Cornelius Kite and Tom Birch, the video pairs band footage filmed at Bourbon on Division with visions of a humanoid body under construction. A synthetic form is pieced together, animated, and left to confront the hideous metaphysical joke of receiving a body before receiving any clear consent to inhabit it. Christopher Lee’s video wall visuals, editing, and post effects push the performance footage into a slickly diseased theater of wires, limbs, screens, and staged resurrection. Watch the video for Not My Skin below: Not My Skin lands hard in the sick overlap between the nightclub, the lab, the operating room, and the mirror. Sleep Of Mirrors takes the familiar industrial question of man versus machine and drags it inward, toward the private horror of man versus flesh. By the end, the song feels less performed than extracted. Listen to Not My Skin below and order the single, out now through Negative Gain Productions, here. Crown by Sleep Of Mirrors Sleep Of Mirrors spoke with Post-Punk.com about the new single and gave us a little insight into its creation: Ronnie is known for Born of Osiris. How did he end up on a Sleep Of Mirrors track? Chris: The answer is that we’re just really good friends. Danny: Yea, the real story is that we’re homies and it’s organic. Ronnie: We do music Thursdays. We write music together and we have fun. We’re not trying to be someone we’re not. We like doing what we’re doing. So this was not a traditional “feature” situation? Jay: On the surface it might look like we just got Ronnie as a feature, but no, that would be misleading. Danny: Nothing was planned. It just sort of happened. Chris. Yea, Ronnie was over, because he’s with us all the time when we’re making songs in the studio. Ronnie: Yea, I was there and I said, “Let me try a vocal on it.” What was the first spark for “Not My Skin”? Danny: It came out as a bass riff first, then I added synthesizers and drums and brought it to Chris. Chris: Right, similar to most of our songs, Danny comes up with some cool beats, synthesizers, and guitars as the bones, and then we bring them into the studio and rework them into songs that we all want to listen to. Ronnie, what pulled you into this darker electronic world? Ronnie: I wouldn’t even know about darkwave without Danny. The more I’m around Danny, Jay, and Chris, the more I have become a fan. Everything Danny shows me, I’m like, “Oh, this is cool. Let’s do something like that.” People who know your voice from Born of Osiris may expect something more aggressive. What do you want them to know? Chris: I think if people stumble across it and they know Ron and his music, it’s a completely different side of him. It’s less aggressive and more singing. The lyrical content is still intense, but the vocals are definitely not screaming. Ronnie: It’s whispery and vibey. Chris: For the vocal style, we were kinda trying to pull inspiration from Billie Eilish a bit. You can kinda hear that in the verses. Then Ron did a really cool chorus, so we just ran with it. Jay, what does “Not My Skin” mean lyrically? Jay: I had written a note about abjection, the ambiguity between a subject and an object. Where does the border of a person end? Is my skin the border of who I am, or is it something that I do in the world? That was the original theme, and then Ronnie took some of the lyric lines and created that punch in the chorus. Ronnie: I was thinking about not feeling like you’re in or have control of your own body as if you’re being manipulated by the chaos around the world. I feel like I’m surrounded by sin and I’m not in my body. That’s how I was interpreting it. How did that idea become the video concept? Chris: Based on the lyrics, we kicked around a handful of concepts. Then there was this idea of, what if Not My Skin is actually a bot that is being built? We originally tried to make a build-a-Ron where he’s the bot at the end. But the AI kept giving him boobs, so we scrapped that and just did a more solid concept. It evolved into this idea of something synthetic coming to life and realizing that this is its skin and it doesn’t know how to feel. Jay: When Chris was creating the music video, the idea of the bot being synthetic and coming to life just seemed to match organically with the song. From beginning to end, all of it felt like it was in the same world. Ronnie: I think it’s sick.§ Follow Sleep of Mirrors: Website Bandcamp Instagram The post Chicago Dark Electronic Act Sleep of Mirrors Animate the Body in Video for “Not My Skin” — Featuring Ronnie Canizaro (Born of Osiris) appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
