items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 974Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. This is undoubtedly Steven Wilson's most successful and projected musical project of all, as evidenced by the band's popularity. Porcupine Tree consists of a mixture of progressive rock, psychedelic rock, avant-garde experimentalism and heavy metal. It's defined by many fans of the progressive rock community and by the band's members themselves as an art rock music style. The official debut studio album of the band "On the Sunday of Life..." was released in 1992. Porcupine Tree initially remained a Wilson's one-man project. So, the line up on "On the Sunday of Life..." was only made of Steve with some other musicians as guests. The same happened with their second work "Up The Downstair".So, "Up The Downstair" is the second studio album of Porcupine Tree that was released in 1993. The line up on "Up The Downstair" is composed by Steven Wilson (vocals, guitar, bass guitar, keyboards and drum programming). "Up The Downstair" also has the participation of some other musicians. So we also have here the presence of Suzanne Barbieri (vocals), Richard Barbieri (electronics), Colin Edwin (bass guitar) and Gavin Harrison (drums), as guests.Although "Up The Downstair" was preceded by "On The Sunday Of Life...", Wilson sees "Up The Downstair" as Porcupine Tree's actual debut album by Porcupine Tree. After all, in the booklet of the most recent edition of this album he says that he cannot consider "On The Sunday Of Life?" as the real debut of the band, because that album consists of old previously recorded material from the period between 1988 and 1991. "Up The Downstair" contains ten songs on which Wilson tries to achieve a daring and well-thought-out synthesis between quite diverse music genres such as ambient, dance, electronic, krautrock, prog rock, psych rock and space rock. The album almost constantly moves back and forth between the youthful open-mindedness on the one hand and the mature ingenuity on the other. "Up The Downstair" incorporates some new components that are a herald of the more streamlined sound on their later works."What You Are Listening To..." is a short intro that fulfills the role of showing what to expect from the album and where someone presents what will be its music. Its synthesizers allow it to blend subtly with the next track. "Synesthesia" has a catchy beat, an exciting rhythm guitar and sensational solos performed by Wilson. This song comes with a somewhat simplistic rhythm, but the noticeable combination of pop and Floyd extractions, especially the beautiful Floydish guitar steered by the inclusion of electronic elements, makes up for it. "Monuments Burn Into Moments" with just 22-seconds, can be called as a kind of a "preparation track" for the next one. "Always Never" is a strong song with clear Pink Floyd reminiscences. This is a spacey and a fantasy song, with the acoustic guitars and climatic synths paving the way until heavy riffs invade the soundscapes in a sweeping explosion accompanied by prominent powerful drums. The title track is a 10-minute instrumental track that begins with ambient sounds. Then, an electronically generated choir intones a sombre melody that runs through the rest of this title. After a while, a rather simple rhythm sets in, but numerous electronic effects and a choir that keeps appearing give the piece an extremely dense, fascinating atmosphere. "Not Beautiful Anymore" reverts to the spoken verse at the beginning, until energizing drums open up a more exciting rock section, with the bass line and slightly distorted guitar riffs providing a great moment. "Siren" is a short ambient piece, a strange but concise intro to the next track, as happened with "Monuments Burn Into Moments". "Small Fish" has a Floyd atmosphere. It's not particularly complex, but the spherical keyboards, Gilmour's guitar work, Steven's melodic vocals and its spatial sound texture are draws and fascinate. "Burning Sky" is an instrumental that starts slower and spacey with synthesizers, but soon after offers a strong guitar and the splendid drums of Harrison. It works in repetition of chords, yet, in each movement of the musical segments the textures are enriched by the sound effects. "Fadeaway" ends the album with delicate keyboard sounds, gentle guitar and Wilson's almost whispered vocals. It has a sad, solemn beauty that stays with us after the album is finished, making it a great closing track with its space atmosphere.Conclusion: "Up The Downstair" shows Steve Wilson displaying all his inventive side and technical ability in a very consistent album. Perhaps the great virtue of this work is the ability to create an absolutely unique experience, based on sound atmospheres notably influenced by Pink Floyd and Ozric Tentacles, integrating different styles in smooth compositions and great combinations of ethereal and traveling keyboards, climatic drums and space guitars. The emphasis on an atmosphere built around an addictive and connected set of tracks, while still possessive of a somewhat immature sound, was a step forward in relation to "On The Sunday Of Life..." and certainly a step in the right direction. With "Up The Downstair" Porcupine Tree shows why they belong to the most important prog rock bands of the 90's.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Porcupine Tree的早期作品，Steven Wilson以一人为核心主导创作，融合了氛围、电子、舞曲、krautrock、前卫摇滚与太空摇滚等多种元素。专辑在青年式的开放探索与成熟匠意之间不断游走，合成器与吉他交替推进，Pink Floyd式的空间感与电子节拍相互渗透。歌曲结构兼具流行化的简洁旋律与实验性的声音处理，部分短篇曲目如引子段落承担过渡与铺垫功能。整体制作理念预示了乐队后期更为精炼的声音走向，是一张在类型融合上具有前瞻意识的前卫摇滚作品。

items._cn_summary: 这是突尼斯乐队 MYRATH 在2019年发行的专辑《Shehili》，延续了前作《Legacy》以中东和北非音乐元素融合前卫金属的路线。乐队将阿拉伯音阶与传统金属编排结合，交响化编曲层次丰富，制作精良。评论者特别指出主唱 Zaher Zorgati 嗓音富有力量与控制力，是金属乐界被低估的歌手之一，代表作《You Lost Yourself》充分展现了这一特点。整体而言，这张专辑在前作基础上有所推进，旋律钩子更强，同时保持了鲜明的地域色彩与世界音乐融合特色。

items.excerpt: Joy Division’s studio recordings can feel sealed inside negative space: precise, cavernous, and fixed within the severe architecture Martin Hannett built around them. Onstage, that architecture sweated and buckled. Stephen Morris’s drums surged forward with machine-like force; Peter Hook’s high bass carried melody like an alarm; Bernard Sumner’s guitar cut cold through the open air; and Ian Curtis danced at its centre, pulling each song toward the unstable border between discipline and collapse.
items.body: Joy Division’s studio recordings can feel sealed inside negative space: precise, cavernous, and fixed within the severe architecture Martin Hannett built around them. Onstage, that architecture sweated and buckled. Stephen Morris’s drums surged forward with machine-like force; Peter Hook’s high bass carried melody like an alarm; Bernard Sumner’s guitar cut cold through the open air; and Ian Curtis danced at its centre, pulling each song toward the unstable border between discipline and collapse. For decades, that other Joy Division has survived in fragments—radio broadcasts, soundboard tapes, audience cassettes, bootlegs, grainy film, and the memories of rooms long gone. That scattered history is now being gathered on an unprecedented scale. Joy Division have announced Eternal (Live), a monumental 14CD/2DVD archival collection arriving on September 25 via Warner Music. Its audio discs contain 192 tracks drawn from 16 performances recorded between March 1979 and May 1980, all mastered at Abbey Road Studios, while the two DVDs collect more than two and a half hours of concert film. Warner describes Eternal as the band’s first official collection of live concert recordings. That wording speaks to its scale and organizing principle rather than the absence of officially released live material. The posthumous 1981 double album Still paired studio outtakes, non-album recordings, and rarities—including “Exercise One,” “Ice Age,” “The Sound of Music,” “The Only Mistake,” “Something Must Break,” “Dead Souls,” and “Glass”—with Joy Division’s final concert at Birmingham University’s High Hall on May 2, 1980. The complete eleven-song set included the only known live performances of “Ceremony” and “Decades” before ending with “Digital.” Still also preserved the band’s cover of The Velvet Underground’s “Sister Ray,” recorded at London’s Moonlight Club on April 2, 1980. Later releases such as Preston 28 February 1980 and Les Bains Douches 18 December 1979 documented further portions of the band’s stage history. Eternal also follows Joy Division’s previous major archival box set, Heart and Soul, released in 1997. That four-CD collection gathered nearly all of the band’s studio output—including Unknown Pleasures, Closer, singles, and compilation appearances—across its first two discs. The third assembled demos, rough mixes, radio sessions, and rehearsal recordings, while the fourth presented selected live performances, including ten songs from the Factory concert of July 13, 1979, and five from the Lyceum on February 29, 1980. Eternal returns to those nights with fuller presentations and newly heard sources. Rather than replacing Heart and Soul, the new collection functions as its live counterpart: where the earlier box mapped Joy Division’s recorded canon, Eternal traces the songs changing from room to room and night to night. The collection begins at London’s Hope and Anchor on March 1, 1979, more than three months before the release of Unknown Pleasures, and ends with Joy Division’s final performance at High Hall in Birmingham on May 2, 1980. Between those points, it moves through youth clubs, Factory nights, festivals, European radio broadcasts, London venues, and provincial halls, following the group across the final fourteen months of its existence. Two performances are presented from previously unreleased recordings. The Hope and Anchor set has been assembled from two unheard audience tapes—one made by Jonathan Crabb and another by an unidentified taper—while the seven surviving songs from Acklam Hall on May 17, 1979 also come from a Crabb audience recording. Three further performances contain newly heard sources. The band’s July 13, 1979, appearance at Manchester’s Factory arrives from a previously unheard soundboard recording. The first nine songs from the Lyceum in London on February 29, 1980, are newly available, followed on the disc by two additional performance tracks and five soundcheck recordings. At the Moonlight Club on April 2, 1980, “The Sound of Music” comes from an audience tape, while six songs—from “Wilderness” through “Dead Souls”—are drawn from a mostly unheard desk recording. They join the already familiar Still-issued cover of “Sister Ray” to complete the surviving eight-song document of that night. Eternal does not attempt to disguise the uneven physical history of these recordings. Its sources range from direct soundboard tapes and broadcasts by France Inter and the Dutch broadcaster VARA to audience cassettes made by Crabb, Malcolm Whitehead, Duncan Haysom, Andy Hooper, and Tim Bayes. Some performances are matrices combining multiple tapes; others retain the distance, room noise, and rough edges of a single audience source. The result is less a conventionally polished live album than a documentary map of Joy Division moving through different rooms, crowds, and stages of its rapid evolution. The chronological sequence also reveals how quickly the repertoire changed. The early 1979 sets place “Exercise One,” “Leaders of Men,” “Glass,” “Ice Age,” and “The Only Mistake” beside material that would define Unknown Pleasures. By the summer, “Dead Souls,” “Wilderness,” “Atrocity Exhibition,” and “Autosuggestion” have entered the performances. As the collection crosses into 1980, songs destined for Closer—“Passover,” “Twenty Four Hours,” “Heart and Soul,” “Isolation,” “The Eternal,” and “Decades”—begin occupying more of the stage. Some nights emphasize clipped economy; others allow the songs to stretch and scrape against their own structures. Setlists shift continually, sometimes from one evening to the next. “Love Will Tear Us Apart” moves from an emerging song into a recurring centerpiece, while “Atmosphere” appears amid sets that still close with the blunt force of “Interzone,” “Warsaw,” or “Digital.” The final audio disc returns to the band’s last concert at Birmingham University’s High Hall, performed sixteen days before Curtis’s death and previously issued in full on Still. The concert opened with Joy Division’s only known live performance of “Ceremony.” For Eternal, the first minute of the song is taken from an audience recording by an unidentified taper, after which the sound-desk source takes over. The set then moves through “Shadowplay,” “Passover,” “New Dawn Fades,” “Isolation,” and the only known Joy Division performance of “Decades,” before ending with “Digital.” The first preview from the collection is “Transmission,” recorded at Les Bains Douches in Paris on December 18, 1979, for a France Inter broadcast. Morris’s drums keep the song locked in constant forward motion, while Hook’s bass cuts a severe melodic path beneath Sumner’s guitar and Curtis’s repeated command to dance. The familiar 2001 live album bearing the Les Bains Douches name combined nine Paris performances with material from the Paradiso in Amsterdam and the Effenaar in Eindhoven. Eternal separates those dates, presenting the sixteen-song Paris broadcast, the seventeen-song Paradiso set, and the sixteen-song Effenaar recording as three distinct documents. Listen to “Transmission (Live Les Bains Douches, Paris, December 18, 1979)” below: The visual archive is comparably extensive. The first DVD includes a new 2026 edit of Joy Division — A Malcolm Whitehead Film, incorporating 1979 rehearsal material and three songs filmed at Bowdon Vale Youth Club. It also contains the band’s two performances from the BBC programme Something Else—“Transmission” and “She’s Lost Control”—broadcast in September 1979. Its centrepiece is the previously unseen Plan K concert in Brussels from October 16, 1979. The footage is presented first with its original 1979 audio and then as an eleven-song reconstruction made in 2026. That second version uses recordings from Les Bains Douches for most of the set, with “Twenty Four Hours,” “Atrocity Exhibition,” and “Interzone” sourced from the Paradiso performance. “Love Will Tear Us Apart” appears only in the original-audio presentation. The second DVD gathers two concerts from Manchester’s Apollo Theatre, recorded on October 27 and 28, 1979, along with soundcheck footage from the same period. Portions of those performances were used for Factory Records’ Here Are The Young Men, released on VHS and Betamax in 1982; Eternal returns to the surviving reels to present considerably more of both nights. The physical collection is housed in a 12-by-12-inch lift-off-lid box with artwork by Warren Jackson, Peter Saville, Howard Wakefield, and Brett Wickens. Its cover uses Wolfgang Tillmans’s photograph Sirius Through a Defocused Telescope, 2023, in which the brightest star in the night sky becomes a blurred, prismatic bloom suspended against black. A 16-page booklet includes personal notes by poet Simon Armitage and photography by, among others, Anton Corbijn and Kevin Cummins. The complete 192-track audio edition will also be available digitally. The announcement arrives alongside a renewed examination of the band’s archive. Ian Curtis: Insight, an exhibition of handwritten lyrics, photographs, personal letters, ephemera, and objects from the Ian Curtis archive at the John Rylands Library, runs at New York’s Voltz Clarke Gallery through July 22. Joy Division and New Order will also be inducted together into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November. Eternal (Live) is out September 25 via Warner Music. items._cn_summary: 本文报道了Joy Division即将发行的现场录音合集Eternal (Live)，收录1979至1980年间16场演出的192首曲目，全部在Abbey Road Studios完成母带处理。文章着重指出这支乐队在现场与录音室之间的反差：录音室作品中Martin Hannett所建构的严谨、阴冷声学空间，在现场转化为更粗粝、更有冲击力的能量——Stephen Morris的鼓点如机器般推进，Peter Hook的高位贝斯如警报般鸣响，Bernard Sumner的吉他切割空气，Ian Curtis的舞蹈则居于崩解边缘。合集并非取代1997年的Heart and Soul，而是其现场对应物：前者描绘乐队的录音室经典全貌，后者则追踪同一批歌曲在不同场地的演变轨迹。文章将此次发行置于Joy Division已散落各处的现场历史（电台广播、录音带、观众私录、盗录影像）之中，强调其作为官方首次系统性现场录音合集的规模与意义。

items.body:
Mor Elian's first vinyl release on Fever AM since 2022, 'Built In Waves' is a taut set of dancefloor-ready house psychedelia that never overlooks the importance of bass.

Elian's got a reputation to uphold. Not only has she blessed her Fever Am label with some of its most memorable bangers - just check 'Double Dip' or its predecessor 'Diva Test' - but she moved into a different zone entirely last year when she released her debut album 'Solid Space', forming weightless ambient textures to hover between the frenetic rhythms. 'Built In Waves' is a comeback of sorts, then, that re-affirms her dedication to the dancefloor, with a selection of four techy, twitchy bangers that'll do the job whether you're in Berlin or Bogatá. 

The title track welds brain-tickling synths and Errorsmith-like vocaloid effects over skittering, syncopated percussion that Elian routinely interrupts with hand drums, constantly sculpting the low-end into a pulsing, momentous thud. And the cheeky 'Get Ready With Me' is even better, a jittery 'Spastik' tribute at first that Elian wakes up with rasping 'Flat Beat'-style bass before the EP concludes with the Panorama Bar-ready ass shaker 'Ondulations'.
items._genre: tech house / electronic / dancefloor / experimental house
items._cn_summary: Mor Elian在Fever AM厂牌发行的EP《Built In Waves》收录四首聚焦舞池的技术性house作品，标题曲将刺激神经的合成器与类似Errorsmith的vocaloid效果叠加在碎拍与手鼓交错的节奏结构上，低频被持续塑造成脉动式的重击。'Get Ready With Me'以类似'Flat Beat'的嘶哑贝斯线展开，起初向Plastikman的'Spastik'致敬，节奏紧张而不失趣味。终曲'Ondulations'则呈现Panorama Bar偏好的律动风格。该EP延续了Elian此前在该厂牌推出的如'Double Dip''Diva Test'等作品路线，同时呼应了她去年首张专辑《Solid Space》中对氛围质感的探索，但整体重心回归于适合柏林等地下俱乐部场景的实用舞曲。

items.body:
Following 2024's avant-prog-Americana song cycle 'Viewfinder', guitar deity Wendy Eisenberg goes chamber pop on their self-titled latest, tipping their hat to Judee Sill, Gillian Welch, Van Dyke Parks and Joanna Newsom.

When they relocated from rural Western Mass to Brooklyn in 2020, Eisenberg was hit with a wave of longing for the open landscape they'd left behind. They were drawn to classic country and folk records, perfectly poised offerings from Willie Nelson and John Hartford and lavish pop-folk records from Jimmy Webb and Van Dyke Parks as well as the weirdo fare of Richard Dawson et al. So when 'Viewfinder', a way of deconstructing the experience following eye surgery in 2011, was finished, Eisenberg started writing "genuinely folk songs" and swapping out their usually showy, complex performance for a form of relative simplicity that they explain is inherently strange all the same. Prog becomes folk, basically. And they're not on their own; more eaze handles the lush string arrangements, playing pedal steel and synthesizer, and a loose band forms around that axis, with drummer Ryan Sawyer and bassist Trevor Dunn.

But despite the personnel, it's resolutely Eisenberg's album. Their voice sounds unrestrained, capturing the era they're referencing and their own emotional (and physical upheaval). It's fragile but strangely warm on the country-tinged Jim O'Rourke-like 'Will You Dare' and hypnotic on the baroque 'Meaning Business', a track they wrote in the wake of David Lynch's death as the antithesis of the "Lynchian" aesthetic. And they should really get their flowers for this one; Americana, especially now, is teetering on a precipice, almost knocked off the edge by half-assed, churned attempts and underwritten pastiches. Eisenberg's an attentive listener and someone who's surrounded themself with similarly sensitive ears, people who are able to fill their heart and their sound so what we hear is as byzantine as a Gastr del Sol record but sounds as effortless as John Prine's 'Angel From Montgomery'. If you loved Joanna Newsom's 'Ys' and have never found anything quite as satisfying, this is the one.
items._genre: chamber pop / avant-folk / americana / baroque pop
items._cn_summary: Wendy Eisenberg在2024年前卫民谣专辑《Viewfinder》之后转向室内流行风格，以自身命名新作。搬离马萨诸塞州乡村至布鲁克林后，对开阔地貌的思念促使他们沉浸于Willie Nelson、John Hartford、Jimmy Webb、Van Dyke Parks等经典乡村民谣与华丽流行民谣唱片，并将过往炫技复杂的演奏方式置换为相对简化的形式。more eaze负责弦乐编排、踏板钢 pedal steel与合成器，Ryan Sawyer打鼓、Trevor Dunn弹贝斯。专辑中Eisenberg的声音舒展而脆弱，《Will You Dare》带有乡村韵味类似Jim O'Rourke，《Meaning Business》则在David Lynch逝世后以巴洛克风格作为所谓Lynchian美学的对立面呈现。将前卫元素编织入民谣传统之中，结构复杂却听感自然流畅，为当前缺乏深度的美式民谣领域带来具有自觉意识的回应。

items.body:
One of the most distinctive and legendary vocal/dub albums of all time, recorded in 1981 by the “dub dentist” Keith Hudson, ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is now back in circulation for the first time in over 20 years, when it was first given overdue flowers via Basic Channel And Honest Jon’s ‘Basic Replay’ programme. It still burns with a rare energy, making it an untouchable, foundational text for the ages.

Keith Hudson (1946-1984) was one of dub reggae’s most distinctive innovators, renowned for a run of classic solo albums and productions for U-Roy, Big Youth, Ken Boothe and Horace Andy between 1972 and his untimely passing in 1984. However, Hudson's late period is where the real imperial juice can be found, a time that saw him move from Jamaican to London and New York studios, applying his unfathomable production style to a heavily americanised strain of vocal Soul. ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is the pinnacle of that late period, an album that builds layer upon layer of alchemical brilliance.

Hudson’s combination of hooks and complex, highly unusual production is really unlike anything else from the period, or since, crooning in a soul mode made more haunting by a discreetly judicious application of tape FX, endlessly heavy subs, and mixing desk tricks deployed to delirious, almost psycho-acoustic effect.  The album was originally meant to feature one of Hudson's teenage sons to voice the dubs, but in the event the Love Joys, Wayne Jarrett, and inimitably Hudson himself featured at the microphone, with the dozen cuts co-produced by Wackies founder Lloyd ‘Bullwackie’ Barnes - the only collaboration between the two producers. It was originally issued on Hudson’s own label, Joint International, with subsequent pressings on Basic Replay in 2003, making it increasingly sought-after in the years since. 

Alongside reggae’s first concept album, ‘Flesh of My Skin, Blood of My Blood’, ‘Playing It Cool’ remains one the genre’s most important and unusual releases, picking up new disciples with every new wave of listeners taken aback by its stark, brooding blooze and brittle, spectral rendering.
items._genre: dub reggae / vocal dub / experimental dub / soul fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张1981年的专辑是Keith Hudson晚期创作生涯的巅峰之作，由他与Wackies厂牌创始人Lloyd Barnes联合制作。Hudson从牙买加转向伦敦和纽约录音棚，将dub制作手法应用于美式灵魂乐风格的人声演唱。专辑以层层叠加的复杂制作著称，融合了钩子旋律与非常规的混音技术，大量使用磁带效果器、超低频低音和调音台手法，营造出近乎迷幻的声学空间。演唱部分原计划由Hudson儿子担纲，最终由Love Joys、Wayne Jarrett及Hudson本人完成。整张专辑呈现出冷峻、阴郁的布鲁斯气质与幽灵般的频谱质感，与Hudson另一张被视为牙买加雷鬼首张概念专辑的《Flesh of My Skin》并列为该类型最重要的作品。

items.body:
New Dream Machine 12" from Dutch producer Kennedy.

"Kennedy continues to sketch out imaginary worlds where thoughts and sensations are converted into sound via the power of machines. On this fifth instalment of Hi-Tech Soul, the Dutch producer channels fragments of midnight memories and daytime visions into something tactile yet elusive. As with previous chapters, the process remains shaped by surprise as hands and hardware entwine in a quiet, freeform dialogue.

The music itself drifts rather than drives, unfolding like shifting cloud forms that never quite settle. Loose, frayed house patterns hover in a state of flotation as basslines anchor just enough to stop everything dissolving completely. Each track has a sense of elevation where melodic synths filter through the mix like heavenly sunbeams breaking overhead. There's a constant progression to something that never comes, instead leaving you free to find your own meaning as textures blur into something soft, indistinct and gently euphoric.

A pure state of celestial suspension, 'Dream 5' is the newest offering in a series that takes you to a weightless world of infinite interpretations."

items.body:
Gary Sullivan, host of WFMU's Bodega Pop, pools his Brooklyn and Queens finds on this crunchy anthology, collecting early 20th century Russian music that was prized by first-generation Russian New Yorkers.

Time's frozen on 'Let Me Perish Without Return', a set of noisy ballads, music hall standards and folky reflections that map out the experience of the diaspora who immigrated from the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union as the home they knew transformed beyond recognition. Sullivan combed thrift stores in Forest Hills, Brighton Beach and Gravesend to find these intriguing cues, and pieces together a story that's shared by half a million New Yorkers. The remnants of Russian life are still visible on the surface of these neighborhoods, and the music helps us understand the culture a little more deeply. It's not particularly familiar material, but it makes for fascinating listening - especially if you've rinsed the rest of the Death is Not the End catalog.
items._genre: folk / archival / world / early 20th century Russian
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由WFMU电台主持人Gary Sullivan策划，从布鲁克林与皇后区的旧货店中淘选出沙俄帝国末期至苏联早期的老唱片，汇集嘈杂的民谣、歌厅曲调与带有乡愁色彩的作品。唱片聚焦于十九世纪末至二十世纪初从俄帝国及苏联移居纽约的犹太与东欧移民群体，折射出离散族群在故土剧变之际的文化记忆。Sullivan在Forest Hills、Brighton Beach、Gravesend等社区的二手店中搜寻这些鲜少被听见的素材，拼贴出五十万纽约客共同的移民故事。作为Death is Not the End厂牌的发行，它带有明显的档案挖掘与文化研究意味，声音虽不华丽但充满历史质感，为理解纽约的俄裔文化提供了独特窗口。

items.body:
Bitchin' Bajas' Cooper Crain and Chicago mainstay Bill MacKay follow 2023's hazed 'Foreign Smokes' with another blunted blend of kosmische, West Coast new age, psychedelia and folk rock.

If you like Bitchin' Bajas, particularly their collaborations with Natural Information Society, there's a damn good chance that 'Stash' will hit you right in the third eye. We already know the Crain and MacKay are weathered players and we already know that their minds are in sync; 'Stash' picks up where its predecessor left off, providing a cinematic answer to the duo's obsession with classic American rock, German psych, vintage British folk, French exotica, Arab pop and Bollywood music. It's not subtle, but with just two basic instruments - Crain flips between organ and synth, while MacKay plays guitar - they don't have the need to pussyfoot. 'Stash' is never overworked, it's the result of two friends jamming out, plugging their instruments into a mixing desk and recording to 8-track to get the grit the material needs.
items._genre: kosmische / psychedelic / new age / folk rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Bitchin' Bajas成员Cooper Crain与Bill MacKay合作的专辑，是2023年《Foreign Smokes》之后的延续之作。两位芝加哥音乐人以管风琴、合成器和吉他两件乐器为基础，融合了德国宇宙音乐、加州新世纪、迷幻摇滚和民谣摇滚等多种元素，还涉及经典美式摇滚、英式民谣、法式异国情调、阿拉伯流行和宝莱坞音乐的影响。录音方式直接而质朴——两位朋友即兴演奏，通过调音台直接录入八轨磁带，刻意保留粗糙的颗粒质感。专辑呈现出电影化的空间感，不追求精雕细琢，而是以原始的化学反应为核心。对于熟悉Bitchin' Bajas与Natural Information Society合作的听众来说，这种双人心意相通的创作状态是这张专辑最核心的吸引力。

items.body:
The ever-unpredictable FaltyDL plays true to form with a diverse volley of ambient techno, electro-pop and steaming club missions, this time for London’s Hooversound.

‘Body Me’ is basically the best yet on Naina & Sherelle’s label, giving ample room for NYC’s Drew Lustman aka FaltyDL to really flex his restless range and inch-tight tekkerz.If you’re here cos it’s Hooversound, you’re probably after the uptempo stuff, which comes at the back of the EP in a gnashing, Autechrian mazza, ‘Neurology Department’, and the peak time bullet ‘Dungeon Dungeon Remix’ - a dead strong testament to his ability to balance horsepower momentum with romantic musicality. 

The rest plays to his other strengths; the OG ‘Dungeon Dungeon’ is notably slower than the remix, more in step with weirdo Berlin techno, while the pendulous electro-hyperpop of his title track harks to his early days as a key cog of the post-UKF sound, and ‘A World’ takes it fully airborne on a sort of proggy breakbeat trance tip wth broad appeal, again thanks to his timeless grasp of modernist club romance.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由纽约制作人FaltyDL为伦敦厂牌Hooversound发行，展现了他在多种电子风格间的灵活穿梭能力。作品横跨氛围 techno、电音流行与俱乐部舞曲，并在EP后段以Autechre式的高强度碎拍曲目和高峰时段子弹节奏混音版满足快节奏舞池需求。前半部分则呈现出更内省的特质：原始版Dungeon Dungeon放慢节奏，偏向柏林实验techno的怪异质感；标题曲在电子hyperpop的摇摆律动中透露出UK post-dubstep时期的影子；A World则以渐进式breakbeat与trance元素实现升空体验。整张作品在力度与浪漫音乐性之间维持了良好平衡，体现出制作人对现代俱乐部美学的成熟掌控。

items.body:
Arvo Pärt has become something of a yardstick by which contemporary sacred music has been measured, and 'Alina' is arguably his most loved and imitated piece of work. 

Für Alina was first performed in Tallinn in 1976, and has become one of Pärt’s most-loved and widely appreciated works - regarded by many as an early, defining example of his signature tintinnabuli style. In the years since its release, Pärt has become the most performed living composer in the world, his approach to religious music seeping deep into our cultural landscape, from the avant garde to the mainstream.

Rendered with nothing more than piano and violin, this definitive ECM version from 1999 features Vladimir Spivakov, Sergej Bezrodny, Dietmar Schwalke and Alexander Malter providing alternate versions, handpicked by Pärt himself from recordings that were originally several hours long. It’s a masterclass in simplicity; an almost painfully beautiful rendering of emotional landscapes that, in the wrong hands, could have (and has, on many occasions, by so many) turned to schmaltz.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了阿尔沃·帕尔特最为人熟知的作品《Für Alina》及其他作品的多个钢琴与小提琴版本，由作曲家本人从数小时的原始录音中亲自挑选整理。评论指出，这些作品的演奏回归极度简洁的编制，却在极简的音符中构建出情感丰沛的内在张力，避免了同类神圣音乐常见的甜俗倾向。帕尔特的钟鸣式作曲技法在钢琴触键的克制与小提琴的克制呼吸中得到充分呈现，体现出作曲家对宗教情感与抽象形式之间平衡的独特理解。作为其创作生涯中的里程碑式作品，此版本的稀缺性在于作曲家亲自参与编排，提供了权威的诠释参照。

items.body:
Prolific Canadians Priori & Project Pablo, aka Jump Source, refract fine strains of deep house, indie-pop, dub and techno-pop on an expansive LP ft. guest vox by billy woods, CFCF & Loukeman and advised to admirers of Luomo, Nick Léon, Rosa Terenzi & D. Tiffany, Galcher Lustwerk.

Building on a decade of Jump Source 12”s for Pacific Rhythm and their self-titled label, Francis Latreille & Patrick Holland skip to the former’s mothership, NAFF, for the project’s variegated debut album. The range and subtle recombinant steez of ‘Fold’ plays deep into the duo’s role at the core of Canada’s renowned club sound, which has emerged over the past decade with canniest updates and refinements of ‘90s to ‘00s US, UK x EU house, techno, trance and beyond. All the above can be heard stripped for parts and reassembled according to classic club lust and galvanised with slick production sure to see it gather air miles.

Tune to tune they fine-tune nuanced aspects of style and pattern, from tweaked darkroom electro-house with over-the-shoulder vox in ‘Nice & Edgy’ calling to mind Cheap & Deep Productions, to the pearlescent ambient-pop of ‘Close’ ft. POiSON GiRL FRiEND. Standouts are registered in the deep house of ‘Empty Bars’ that finds cult rapper billy woods out of context on a groove co-produced with Nick Léon, and in the echoes of Canadian click-house pioneer Akufen on ‘Affect’ ft. Loukeman, thru the brisker deep techno-house of ‘Fade City’ ft. Deaton Chris Anthony, and the Luomo-esque, connoisseurs choice of ‘A Dull Knife’ faced by Harmony Index.
items._genre: deep house / techno-pop / dub / ambient pop / electro-house
items._cn_summary: 这是加拿大双人组Jump Source的首张全长专辑，由Priori与Project Pablo合作完成。专辑在NAFF厂牌发行，延续了他们此前在Pacific Rhythm发行的十年12寸单曲积累。整张作品将九十年代至千禧年的美国、英国及欧洲house、techno、trance等俱乐部元素拆解重组，呈现出融合deep house、indie-pop、dub与techno-pop的复合面貌。制作手法精细，曲目之间在风格与律动模式上做微调，从暗室electro-house到珍珠光泽的ambient-pop均有涉及。客座阵容包括说唱歌手billy woods、制作人Nick Léon、CFCF、Loukeman及Deaton Chris Anthony等，为俱乐部化的底色增添人声层次与跨界质感。整体定位偏向精致俱乐部音乐，融合意识明显，但在实验性与声音设计的极端程度上面向主流舞曲审美。

items.body:
Part 1 of a 12" series featuring Beatrice M.’s 'Sinking', the rudely aerodynamic debut LP where Tectonic's franco-british hope flexes a signature balance of ruff & smooth, building on a solid reputation earned via 12”s with her label, Bait, plus Tempa and Darwin’s SPE:C.​

Dubstep is not necessarily an album genre: beyond scant examples from the likes of Burial, Shackleton, or 2562, 12”s and DJ sets serve the sound in best context. However, Beatrice M.’s grasp of subtle sensuality and propulsive traction patently ends itself well to the format on ’Sinking’, with rolling, stepping and skanking permutations that deftly dance in the space between dubstep, proper, and its close-related cousins - UKG, broken beat, dub techno - with a finely measured proprioception of space, weight and pressure. 

Along with 2562’s recently dispensed ‘Lost Dubs 2006-09’, ’Sinking’ is arguably the best thing on Tectonic in recent memory, with a sound that revels in more ambiguous club suss. It’s the type of release primed for cans/buds as much as big cones, proving she’s equally adept at sublime tension, as in the languid ‘Ever’, as propelling a dance in the Martyn-esque wriggler ‘Motion’, and offbeat hood of ‘Disco Corner’.
items._genre: dubstep / UKG / broken beat / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英法双重背景制作人在Tectonic厂牌发行的首张全长作品，承接了其在Bait、Tempa及SPE:C等小厂牌积累的口碑。评论指出dubstep通常更适合12寸单曲和DJ set形式，但Beatrice M.对微妙感官张力和推进节奏的把控使全长专辑成为可行的呈现载体。作品在dubstep本体与邻近风格之间游走，融合了UKG的碎拍律动、broken beat的切分感以及dub techno的空间感，在重量与压力之间保持精确平衡。专辑中既有如《Ever》般缓慢铺陈的松弛段落，也有如《Motion》般带有Martyn式弹性质地的舞曲，以及《Disco Corner》般的异化离拍曲调。整体被定位为Tectonic近期最具暧昧俱乐部质感的发行之一，适合耳机细听与大系统重放两种场景。

items.body:
Sun worship dub house strollers from Belgrade’s Estray & Devon-based Federsen for his trustworthy Alt Dub Records.

Glyding farther along a label path taking in gems from veterans CV313 and Beppu, and fresh faces Thomas + James, the ‘Dubalearic EP’ trades in effortless strains of atmospheric club buoyancy that speak to the producer’s roots in a rhizome of European and US dub techno labels and clubs. 

Their aerodynamic title tune fathoms classic touches of M-Series and E2-E4 in its pendulous sway and effusive dub chord froth, next to the trim trot of ‘Isla Dub’, whereas ‘Mareas Tranquilas’ goes leagues deeper on the square bassed low end movement, and the lustrous deep house dub of ‘Sombras de Ibiza’ dreams of bronzed skin in slinky motion.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP收录了来自贝尔格莱德的Estray与德文郡的Federsen合作的四首dub house作品，延续了二人根植于欧洲与美国dub techno厂牌脉络的制作路径。标题曲以悬浮般的氛围感律动展开，融合了M-Series与E2-E4时代的经典dub chord质感；《Isla Dub》节奏更为紧凑精炼；《Mareas Tranquilas》深入方形低音的深沉律动层；《Sombras de Ibiza》则呈现光亮松弛的deep house dub纹理。整体制作风格倾向于舒适流畅的氛围俱乐部音乐，强调律动与空间感的有机结合，并未追求激进的声音实验，而是在dub techno传统框架内进行精心的氛围构建。

items.body:
Wisdom Teeth boss Facta returns to his label after recent LP ‘Gulp’ (2025) with a more upfront club EP spanning bustling dubstep to swingeing minimal house and bashy bleeps ’n bass voiced by Warrior Queen & Killa P.

Arriving with support by the likes of Ben UFO, Batu, and Gilles Peterson, ‘Witness’ catches the ‘floor in ductile diversity. ‘T66’ rides prevailing Latin club breezes with a deftly whisked blend of sub-heavy halfstep synced to triplet samba drums, whistles and bugged-out vox; ‘witness’ whips bristling drums into something like Villalobos reworking Basement Jaxx; and ’SLoPE VIP’ feels kinda like one of Nicolette’s early, dare-to-differ Shut Up and Dance gems, with JA dancehall mic controller Warrior Queen and UK grime don Killa P carrying the spirit of Ragga Twins on a rude breakstep.
items._genre: dubstep / minimal house / jungle / bass / club
items._cn_summary: Facta 在自家厂牌推出的这张 EP 以俱乐部舞池为核心，横跨多种低音音乐风格。'T66' 将拉丁俱乐部节拍与半步低音融合，桑巴鼓组、口哨声与人声采样交织；'witness' 以细密鼓机驱动，呈现出极简浩室与碎拍舞曲的折中质感；'SLoPE VIP' 则邀请牙买加舞厅麦克风掌控者 Warrior Queen 与英国 Grime 艺人 Killa P 助阵，碎拍节奏承载 Ragga Twins 式的粗粝能量。整张作品在低音与俱乐部舞曲的交叉地带游走，风格跨度大但内核统一于舞池功能性，邀请 Ben UFO、Batu、Gilles Peterson 等 DJ 站台支持，体现了伦敦地下俱乐部场景的当下美学走向。

items.body: On February 13, 2026, Sub Rosa Records released Gendarme de la Libertad, a digital album featuring music composed by David Toub with performances by pianist Stephane Ginsburgh. This is an hour of piano music, solidly in the minimalist tradition that, according to the liner notes: “… reflects today’s anxieties and uncertainty.” Gendarme is music with a strong moral viewpoint. If the task of contemporary music is to reflect the critical issues of our time, then Gendarme de la Libertad accomplishes that. There are two tracks on the album of 30 minutes each. The first incorporates spoken words from a 1964 speech by Dr. Ernesto (Che) Guevara before the United Nations. The second track was written for open instrumentation but is performed here on piano. Both pieces reflect the driving intensity of classic minimalism yet also remind us that nuance can be present in musical patterns. The title track of the album is Gendarme de la Libertad for Speaker and Piano. This was composed in 2020, the same year as the murder of George Floyd while in police custody in Minneapolis. David Toub has reached back to the 1964 words of Che Guevara as the social commentary to accompany his music. Gendarme is a solo piano piece and the performer speaks, not sings, the text by Guevara. The original speech was, of course, delivered in Spanish; for this album, both the original Spanish and English translations are used. The liner notes state that “The words are applicable beyond their original intent and historical setting; they should be spoken plainly.” Indeed.The spoken words are connected to the music, yet they seem to flow independently above it. The piece begins with several fragments of spoken phrases that build with repetition into a single complete sentence. This invites the listener to collect the phrases and parse their meaning while anticipating the finished statement. This added mental processing adds to the weight of the words and amplifies their meaning. The piano parts of Gendarme de la Libertad open with a series of slowly repeated four-note arpeggios that start deep in the lower register and rise upward, creating an indefinite, uncertain feeling. Soon more notes are added and the rhythms shift slightly, becoming less regular. After a minute or so there is a brief pause, one of several that are sprinkled through this piece. The tempo then increases and the phrasing becomes more active and purposeful. The pianist speaks: “Those who demand their legitimate rights… as free men…” This is repeated and now “…are the guardians of freedom.” is added. This continues with various spoken parts of the text that are repeated for emphasis. The piano accompaniment is always moving, and this supports a growing sense of importance.At 5:35 another a simple arpeggio of single notes is heard and these morph again into set of repeated moving lines. The spoken text is now heard in Spanish, with parts repeated for emphasis. The rapid delivery of the words in Spanish heighten the urgency of the message. Some dissonance now seeps into the harmony, building tension. The repetition of the musical phrases is varied slightly, keeping the listener engaged. By 13:00 the music has turned solemn and the spoken Spanish has finally delivered the text in it’s entirety: “Those who kill their own children and discriminate a\daily against them because of the color of their skin; those who let the murderers of blacks remain free, protecting them, and furthermore punishing the black population because they demand their legitimate rights as free men – how can those who do this consider themselves guardians of freedom?” As the second half of the piece continues, a series of somber notes ring out like a mournful church bell. Parts of the text are in repeated again in both Spanish and in English. The piano accompaniment proceeds in a series of quiet solemn tones. This pensive feeling contrasts very effectively with more animated first half. The last five minutes returns to powerful chords in the bass with a single dominant note in the higher register. There is a fateful feeling in this. Now the tempo increases and the notes above become discordant, renewing the sense of tension. English text spoken “ they demand their legitimate rights as free men”. The piece ends suddenly, but leaves a heavy sense of responsibility in the air. Gendarme de la Libertad reminds us that the struggle for human rights is long and costly, and that we ourselves must bend its arc towards justice.The second track of the album is Duophony for Open Instrumentation, also from 2020. This was originally written for open instrumentation but is performed here by Stephane Ginsburgh on piano. Duophony is a resolute minimalism consisting of repeating cells of 16th notes in unison in two staves. There is a driving tempo but no counterpoint. Intriguing changes in the harmony can be detected with careful listening. There is a pounding urgency to the repeating rhythms and the forceful dynamics amplify a sense of power. The higher notes weave in and around the chords in the deep lower registers and this engages the listener. Always repeating, the density of the lower chords thicken and thin beguilingly. The robust playing of Stephane Ginsburgh and the elegant sound of the Bӧsendorfer provide a strong foundation for this piece.At 10:15 the tempo slows slightly and a single repeating upper note now dominates the texture. The notes continue repeating in unison, but with less urgency and a more reflective feeling. The dominating high note pounds like a hammer. As the repetition continues, slight changes in the pitch of the upper notes is heard. This sustains interest and simultaneously builds tension. The bass line also changes and evolves into a repeating melody line. As the piece proceeds, the tempo slowly decreases, adding a bit of drama. The bass lines growl along as before and the highest notes are often replaced by pitches in the middle registers. This evolves into a more settled feeling, and towards the finish it feels as if the energy in the music has been slowly drained away. Duophony ends as it was heard, in strict unison. For all the structural stasis of the piece, one is left with the impression of having heard a fair amount of variety. Toub has crafted solid listener interest from his spare minimalist materials, sustained by the muscular playing of Stephane Ginsburgh.If Gendarme de la Libertad brings a message of hope for the future using the words and musical forms of the immediate past, then it points to the poverty of our commitment to justice in the present. Toub and Ginsburgh have rendered an eloquent artistic statement that guides us forward. Gendarme de la Libertad is available from Sub Rosa by digital download. The post David Toub: Gendarme de la Libertad for Speaker and Piano – CD Review appeared first on Sequenza21.
items._cn_summary: David Toub的《Gendarme de la Libertad》由Sub Rosa厂牌发行，钢琴家Stephane Ginsburgh演奏，是两张各约30分钟的简约主义钢琴作品。标题曲为钢琴与人声朗诵而作，人声部分截取切·格瓦拉1964年在联合国的演讲片段，以西班牙语原版与英语翻译交替呈现，文本片段经重复累积成完整语句，邀请听众在等待中拼合语义。钢琴声部以低音区的四音琶音开场，逐步上移并改变节奏规律，制造不确定感，随后力度与速度逐渐增强，与不断重复的政治话语形成张力呼应。第二曲原为开放乐器编制，此版以钢琴演绎。两首作品均试图在极简重复的框架中容纳对当代社会议题的道德表态，节奏驱动性强，同时保留音型内部的细腻变化。作为政治意识浓厚的当代古典作品，其观念表达清晰，但在声音实验层面更接近传统简约主义的延伸而非前沿突破。

items.body: Review by The Crow — A breathtaking journey where stoner rock embraces progressive grandeur!Released in 2017, Reflections of a Floating World saw Elder pushing even further beyond the formula perfected on Lore. The band's stoner foundations remain unmistakable, but they are increasingly wrapped in progressive rock, psychedelia and vintage keyboard textures. Rather than chasing immediate hooks, Elder focus on atmosphere, intricate arrangements and immersive compositions, resulting in their most overtly progressive album to date.Sanctuary immediately expands the musical horizons of its predecessor, introducing Mellotron-like textures and an even more sophisticated approach before concluding with a beautiful space rock finale. The Falling Veil raises the bar even higher, combining memorable stoner riffs with adventurous songwriting and a psychedelic middle section before reaching a wonderfully epic conclusion. Staving Off Truth maintains the momentum through another captivating journey, while Blind stands as the album's masterpiece. Its irresistible opening riff, majestic instrumental passages, Mellotron-filled verses and even touches of Hammond organ perfectly capture Elder's evolution into a fully fledged progressive rock band without sacrificing their heavy roots.The only real stumble comes with Sonntag, an instrumental that feels more like an extended jam than a fully developed composition. While it provides a change of pace, it interrupts the album's remarkable momentum and contributes little beyond stylistic variety. Fortunately, Thousand Hands immediately restores the record's grandeur. Its outstanding opening riff, beautiful acoustic guitar passages and triumphant atmosphere provide a thoroughly satisfying conclusion.Conclusion: what makes Reflections of a Floating World so special is its unique ability to evoke places, landscapes and adventures through music alone. Few bands can transform riffs into such vivid mental imagery, and Elder achieve that effortlessly throughout most of the album. While it sacrifices some of the immediate catchiness of Dead Roots Stirring and Lore in favor of greater sophistication, the reward is a richer and more immersive listening experience. Apart from one minor misstep, this is another outstanding chapter in one of modern heavy music's finest discographies.Best Tracks: Blind, The Falling Veil, Sanctuary.
items._genre: heavy prog / stoner rock / psychedelic rock
items._cn_summary: 这张2017年专辑标志着Elder从stoner rock向更明显的progressive rock领域迈进。乐队保留了沉重的riff基础和psychedelic质感，同时大量引入Mellotron风琴、复古键盘音色和Hammond organ等复古元素，营造出空间感与沉浸感。整体编排偏向氛围营造而非直接抓耳的hook，歌曲结构复杂且具有叙事性，吉他与键盘的交织构建出史诗般的段落。评论特别称赞《Blind》和《The Falling Veil》等曲目将沉重riff与progressive结构完美结合。唯一不足是器乐曲《Sonntag》更像即兴jam而非完整作品，打断了专辑的整体流畅性。整张作品以音乐唤起画面与场景的能力见长，是一支重音乐乐队向progressive rock成熟蜕变的代表作。

items.body: All the world lay at your feet Does it mean anything Float a leaf upon the sea And set off drifting Octavian Winters turn their gaze upward on By the Stars, a swooning pop ballad that reveals the San Francisco band at its most lush and otherworldly. Released ahead of their appearance at Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig, and produced once again by William Faith, the single drifts away from the darker angles of Elements of Air into a slower, more spacious form of grandeur. The song moves as if carried by tide and starlight, with toms beating beneath luminous guitar lines and low, patient bass, each element arranged with the care of someone reading a map by candlelight. Ria Aursjoen’s voice gives the track its immense vertical reach. She seems to draw its horizon wider with each phrase, rising from intimacy into something almost celestial. Around her, Stephan Bryan Salit’s guitar glows in long, fine arcs, Jay Denton’s bass supplies a deep undertow, and Randy Gzebb’s drumming keeps the song moving with the quiet insistence of oars against black water. In its soft majesty, By the Stars brings to mind Strange Boutique, Cocteau Twins, Enya, and a little Mazzy Star, though Octavian Winters treat those references as distant constellations rather than fixed coordinates. “The song has the feel of a sea voyage,” says Ausjoen. “The images for me were always ones of the vastness of the sky and the sea, and the feeling of the magnificent beauty of the world. The call and answer vocals are like two people calling back and forth across a valley. It’s meant to encompass that feeling of transcendence when you take a meta view of life and of the natural world, and just fall into the beautiful patterns of it all.” The lyrics look past worldly power toward the vast indifference and mercy of nature. Gold, bones, leaves, sea, stars, and northern lights become images of surrender, as if the self, stripped of possession and certainty, might find release in drifting. The song carries grief without turning heavy, placing human fracture against a sky too immense to answer back. “The song is symmetrical in 3 parts that are about life stages,” Ausjoen explains. “In the first verse, it says “throw your gold into the sea and set off drifting”, in the middle it’s “float a leaf upon the sea and set off drifting’ and finally “throw your bones into the sea and set off drifting”. It’s about not being afraid, taking the next step, whether that’s when you are young and setting out on your path, or when you are older and shrug off other people’s opinions and follow your own way, or at the end of life when you drift away and let your spirit go.” “I remember playing an all-ages show in Northern California, looked up mid-song and saw these two young goth girls at the front of the stage with tears streaming down their faces,” recalls drummer Randy Gzebb. “That moment told me everything I needed to know about ‘By the Stars’. You know a song matters when it reaches people like that.” David Kruschke’s video extends that sense of transport into a strange, theatrical realm. Drawing from the expressionistic grammar of 1910s silent cinema, it begins in stark black and white, with a masked figure presiding over the frame like an antique omen. As the clip passes into full colour, the figure’s authority weakens, and the band appears suspended in another dimension, performing inside a vision where beauty outlasts fear. Watch the video for By The Stars below: Octavian Winters have built their reputation on tightly wrought songs that move from moonlit expanse to dark post-punk drive, matched by enveloping live performances. Their 2023 debut EP, The Line or Curve, now leads toward a William Faith-produced sophomore EP, following Wave-Gotik-Treffen and A Murder of Crows, with Absolution ahead. Listen to By The Stars below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: 旧金山乐队Octavian Winters的《By The Stars》是一首梦幻流行的慢板作品，从此前专辑的暗色棱角转向更辽阔、更舒缓的壮丽形态。Tom鼓点铺底，吉他以绵长弧线闪烁，贝斯提供深沉暗流，人声从中音区攀升至几乎超凡脱俗的高度。歌词围绕向大海抛掷黄金、落叶、骸骨的三段对称结构展开，呈现生命不同阶段的释然与漂流意象。主唱将其比作海上的远行与跨谷呼唤，鼓手则回忆北加州演出时两位哥特少女落泪的瞬间，证明作品的情感穿透力。制作由William Faith再次操刀，音乐节亮相前释出，作品借鉴Strange Boutique、Cocteau Twins、Enya与Mazzy Star，但将其作为遥远星座而非固定坐标来运用。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)
items.label: Analog Africa
items._genre: African funk / Afro-Cuban / vodun music / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 厂牌推出贝宁传奇乐队 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 与歌手 Antoine Dougbé 在1977至1982年间的作品合集。Dougbé 以 Vodun 仪式为创作根基，其标志性的 Cavacha 节奏由打击乐手 Belobi Meridjo 从火车节奏中提炼而来，后广泛影响1970年代中期的刚果流行音乐。乐评着重分析录音时代对音色塑造的影响——塑料质感的吉他与新出现的合成器构成底色，但仍扎根于70年代律动之中。相较于 Poly-Rythmo 此前推出的几张精选，本作的古巴 son 影响更为明显，尤其在开篇曲目中体现充分；刚果伦巴的渗透也清晰可辨，如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，闪亮吉他与高帽主导的密集律动交织，中段吉他分向展开再回归合成器底层。整体呈现一段虽短暂却能量充沛的非洲律动历史切片。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.

A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣圈内经验丰富的主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多取材于传统音乐，乐手各自带来不同视角处理素材。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗粝的小跑节奏展示了主唱具有说服力的嗓音；唯一的原创曲目《Nordgård》由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口琴与风笛提供了强劲的推进力。传统曲《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以扬琴营造精致底色，末曲《Ormsé》则将口簧、笛与弦乐交织成富有弹跳感的器乐片段，呈现出别致的不对称美感。整体弥漫着古老而略带粗糙的氛围，展现了乐队超出新手的成熟度，为后续全长专辑埋下伏笔。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这是西班牙吉他手 Dani Jané 的第三张专辑，融合了弗拉门戈、加泰罗尼亚民谣、古典音乐、爵士与诗歌文本。专辑以古典组曲结构开篇，前半段偏向器乐叙事，吉他与长笛、低音及打击乐形成节制而持续的对话；后半段融入家族传承的诗词文本，1938年的祖辈手稿被改编为伦巴，并附有 Whitman 诗作的西班牙语演唱。制作上以吉他和效果器、长笛与安第斯排箫、以及打击乐声部为核心，弗拉门戈人声作为点缀收束。整体呈现一种新一辈加泰罗尼亚学院派艺术家对弗拉门戈的重新诠释，将其视为多元影响中的一种而非唯一根基。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是比利时五件式乐器组合 Wûr 与瑞典无伴奏女声四重唱 Kongero 的跨界合作现场录音。Wûr 专注于重现数百年前的欧洲早期音乐，Kongero 则以北欧民间无伴奏人声闻名，两支看似风格迥异的团体在这张唱片中尝试融合各自传统素材，并加入一首原创作品。编曲强调声部与乐器之间的复杂交织，如《Drinking Like A Sweet Swede》中的人声和声叠搭于轻快器乐伴奏之上，而《Klosterjungfrun》则以缓慢、空气感十足的开篇营造私密氛围。整体演奏精度较高，现场录音的临场感被完整保留，但乐评所呈现的核心仍落在传统民谣与早期音乐的范围，未涉及电子化处理、即兴自由延伸或现代作曲技法的实验性拓展。

items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items.body: Review by rdtprog — This is a live performance recorded in June 2017 where the band played the full "I Me Myself" andsongs from "The Way," "The Lamplighter," "Insomnia," and 3 unreleased tracks. The stage setup ismade in a special visual design with projections to illustrate the contrast between shadow andlight. This live release explores different styles of music, from symphonic, space, and ambient. Youcan hear in some epic songs the influence of the song "Echoes" from Pink Floyd. There is a cinematicatmosphere throughout the show, which was the band's intention. Don't expect high-definition picturequality, but the music is the main highlight here. It's been a few years since I have listened tothe band's albums, so I was a bit surprised by the eclectic nature of the music here but verypleased with the whole live show. He's just sad that the band doesn't make any more music andstopped touring during the covid virus.

items.excerpt: Review by Hrychu — 1983 wasn't the best year for organic sounding symphonic prog rocking in the so called "WesternWorld". By the time Pablo: El Enterrador's sole opus came out, every 'big' prog player wanted tohave a streamlined arena pop sound to hit the radios and dance floors, and the only ones who weredoing the big overblown prog rock shtick, were from the poorer areas, like Eastern Europe, or inthis case South America, where the then-current radio trends were a few years behind. But I
items.body: Review by Hrychu — 1983 wasn't the best year for organic sounding symphonic prog rocking in the so called "WesternWorld". By the time Pablo: El Enterrador's sole opus came out, every 'big' prog player wanted tohave a streamlined arena pop sound to hit the radios and dance floors, and the only ones who weredoing the big overblown prog rock shtick, were from the poorer areas, like Eastern Europe, or inthis case South America, where the then-current radio trends were a few years behind. But I'm gladhistory went the way it did! Because this album is superb. The songs are really well written andperformed. The band did their thing while balancing between the the two following tropes: catchyhooks and the compositionally dense extended progressive rock bits. I personally believe that it'snot easy to maintain that balance and end up with falling to the pitfall of either having a popalbum with too much unfitting prog fusiony workouts or a prog album filled with simplified hook-driven padding. That's where Yes failed when they came out with Going For The One. That's whereGenesis failed, when they did And Then There Were Three, imo.Speaking of Genesis: the piano player Omar Lopez really went to impressively great lengths on howmuch that late 70's Tony Banks Yamaha CP80 tone could be emulated. It doesn't sound just like awannabe, at times I'm genuinely under the impression of Banks' rig being remotely channeled toArgentina. However, the Genesis similarities more or less end there and they aren't as obvious inother aspects of the sonic palette. Jose Maria Blanc's Rioplatese Spanish vocals are a totallydifferent beast to Phil Collins' mannerisms or even Kim Beacon's Elton John influenced vocal work onACF by Tony Banks. In contrast with Genesis' snappy, rhythmical and straight to the point pop/rockapproach and maybe just occasional jazz fusiony moments here and there, the songwriting and chordchange choices on Pablo: El Enterrador are much more on the mellow and soulful jazz fusion side,with frequent seventh/ninth chord ornaments and swinging solos. At times the sound reminds me moreof the keyboard-dominated Italian prog groups like Festa Mobile, Sensitiva Immagine or Locanda DelleFate than of Genesis.Unless you happen to own the original pressing of the LP on vinyl, in perfect condition, you're outof luck in terms of the sound quality. The master tapes were lost so all the reissues of the album,whether digital or vinyl were sourced from a really badly preserved LP copy, run through quitedestructive de-noising on top of that. Shame.

items._cn_summary: 这是1983年阿根廷乐队Pablo El Enterrador唯一的专辑，在西方主流摇滚转向流行竞技场化的背景下，他们坚持了交响前卫摇滚路线。乐评将其与Yes和Genesis的转型期作品对比，认为该专辑在旋律钩子与复杂编曲之间取得了平衡，未陷入简化流行化或生硬融合的陷阱。键盘手Omar Lopez精确模仿了Tony Banks晚期Yamaha CP80的电钢琴音色，甚至让乐评联想到意大利键盘主导的前卫团体如Festa Mobile、Sensitiva Immagine和Locanda Delle Fate。Jose Maria Blanc使用里约普拉坦河地区西班牙语演唱，旋律与和声选择偏向柔缓的灵魂爵士融合路线，频繁使用七和弦与九和弦装饰，融入摇摆式独奏。乐评遗憾指出母带已佚失，目前所有再版均来自保存状况不佳的黑胶翻录，音质受损严重。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — I feel that this is the album where their newer sound fully took form. Taking their more focused songwriting based form of power prog metal with symphonic and oriental textures, I believe they took the place of the sexier side of the prog power metal world that Kamelot had with Roy Khan in the band. Overall the songwriting is pretty fantastic, with each song having great hooks, musicianship and masterclass vocals from Zaher Zorgati. While it has a more focused sound, there are moments where Malek Ben Arbia & Anis Jouini are able to show off some nice technical guitar and bass interplay. The production is pretty great too, even if on the CD version there's a massive drop in volume after the intro instrumental. The track I'd recommend is Believer.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — The third chapter in Rivers of Nihil's tetralogy of albums representing the four seasons is theambitious and sombre progressive death metal opus 'Where Owls Know My Name', which is the recorddepicting autumn. This is a relentless conceptual album that offers a relatively accessibletechnical sound replete with aggressive riffs, soothing saxophone solos, fabulous mellotroninterludes, and overall sophisticated arrangements. Furthermore, Rivers of Nihil combine beautifullyharsh vocals with clean ones, and often include atmospheric, keyboard-laden passages, which byitself echoes the poignant sound of retro prog. Ideally, this album reminisces the unthinkablemusical marriage between Camel and Meshuggah - emotive melodies, introspective lyrics andpsychedelic undertones are combined with an overt technicality and death metal dynamics.Now, such eclectic extreme metal albums often remain misunderstood, and I believe it is preciselybecause of the fusion of two disparate musical universes. Yet 'Owls' offers an elegant and evocativesound that bridges these two universes in a masterful way, even if the production style on thisalbum is rather old-school. Of the ten tracks appearing on this LP, there are two shorterinstrumentals that serve either as an introduction (the first track) and an interlude (track six),while all of the remaining eight songs feature vocalist Jake Dieffenbach who basically delivers acrushing performance all throughout. Some of the excellent compositions on this record include 'TheSilent Life', which is a song that combines the brutality of Rivers' riffs with their extravagantprog pedigree, and captures the first of several gorgeous saxophone solos. We then have 'A Home', asong that is slightly darker, with a dense and heavy writing, and the epic 'Subtle Change', which isan eight-minute-long track with a complex structure and some hauntingly moody parts, and remains oneof the band's most progressive-minded pieces. The instrumental 'Terrestria III: Wither' isinteresting interlude, once again playing with that ominous atmosphere that the album thriveswithin, while the final minutes feature no less excellent songs like 'Death Is Real' and the near-perfect title track. What I appreciate the most about 'Owls' is the incorporation of psychedelic,fusion, and prog elements as well as the moody metallic sound, which to me makes this one of Riversof Nihil's most remarkable releases to date.
