items.body: Jacqui Hunt “Desiderium” is the new album from Australian vocalist Jacqui Hunt, of Single Gun Theory, released on June 26, 2026 through QUSP. The 11-track “Desiderium” is her first solo album in 18 years, issued on CD, limited-edition vinyl and digital. Jacqui Hunt brings an ethereal, electronic sound that mixes cinematic synths with piano and organic instrumentation. She describes the album as “like stepping out of your body for a while and grounding back to earth — floating on a synth wave while holding the raw reality of a simple piano. The bones that connect to the human voice like a string of air as it floats to the ether and returns to base.” Inside Jacqui Hunt ‘Desiderium’ “Desiderium” runs 11 tracks: “Desiderium,” “Look At The Sky,” “Planet,” “Cecilia,” “Cape Of Light,” “This Love,” “Temple Of Illumination,” “Follow Me Here,” “Cycles,” “Mother” and “Alice Magic.” Hunt recorded the album at QUSP Studios in Sydney, handling vocals, keys and production. Brian Conolly added synth, bass and guitar and engineered the record, Laurence Pike played drums, and Daniel Denholm contributed zither, strings and cello and mixed the album. Michael Lynch mastered it. The closing track also appears as “Alice Magic (K.I.M. Remix),” reworked by Kim Moyes of The Presets. The album is out on CD, limited-edition vinyl and digital. Hunt released an official video for “Planet”: About Jacqui Hunt Jacqui Hunt is an Australian vocalist who co-founded the electronic group Single Gun Theory in Sydney in 1986 with Kath Power and Pete Rivett-Carnac. The band released “Exorcise This Wasteland” in 1987, “Millions, Like Stars in My Hands, The Daggers in My Heart Wage War” in 1991 and “Flow, River of My Soul” in 1994, and was discovered for the Canadian label Nettwerk by Tom Ellard of Severed Heads. Hunt also sang on Delerium‘s album “Karma” (1997), the project of Bill Leeb and Rhys Fulber, contributing to the track “Euphoria (Firefly).” Her debut solo album, “Auraphonic,” appeared in 2008. “Desiderium,” released on June 26, 2026, is her first solo album since, and arrives 40 years after she co-founded Single Gun Theory.
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚歌手 Jacqui Hunt 暌违十八年后发行第二张个人专辑，由悉尼 QUSP Studios 录制。整体以电子合成为骨架，融入钢琴与原声乐器，营造出空灵、漂浮的电影感氛围。Hunt 亲自包办人声、键盘与制作，Brian Conolly 补充合成器、贝斯与吉他并担任录音，Laurence Pike 负责鼓，Daniel Denholm 演奏齐特拉琴、弦乐与大提琴并完成混音。专辑共十一曲，结构松散、偏氛围化，闭合曲另附 The Presets 成员 Kim Moyes 的混音版本。文中未涉及对具体编曲或声响设计的深度评论，内容以信息发布为主。整体偏向氛围电子与人声结合的跨界作品，与实验/暗潮口味有部分交集但实验性有限。

items._cn_summary: 这张1975年由Alan Silva、Bobby Few与Frank Wright三位爵士乐手合作录制的专辑《Solos Duets》，采用自由爵士与即兴演奏形式。曲目通过独奏与二重奏的组合展开对话：Frank Wright以次中音萨克斯与低音单簧管呈现粗粝的即兴表达，Alan Silva则横跨低音提琴、小提琴与钢琴三件乐器，Bobby Few负责钢琴部分。录音分散在法国马西、兰斯与巴黎三地完成，时间跨度涵盖1975全年，体现了自由爵士即兴创作与录音现场性的紧密结合。整张专辑展现了欧洲自由爵士圈子在上世纪七十年代中期的创作面貌，演奏家们在乐器配置与组合方式上做了灵活安排。

items.body:
After a few trips ‘Around the Sun’ Mr Fingers returns to the ‘floor with a definitively broad selection of deep house and acid aces betraying the sound’s links with soul jazz as much as Italo disco and ambient synth musics.

‘Leev Ur Mynd’ is the prescriptive title of Larry Heard’s 7th studio LP in his OG mode, which lands just over 40 years since his early 12”s initiated a sea-change in club music. On a dozen cuts the veteran effortlessly ushers debonaire dancefloors to his command, from proper ChItalo acid peacockery in ‘Plastic Nightmares’ to the piquant electro-soul flow of ‘Replicate’, and covering the finest spectrum of styles & patterns within a theme in between. 

His influential mastery of the 303 results in thee juiciest acid on the LP title tune, then tweaked to a charming type of bloozy jig in ‘Barndance’, and woven into the album’s tuffest jam ‘Menagerie’, or more subtly riding the piano-led glyde of ‘April Rain’, whereas the rest tends towards his equal bias for slicker soul-jazz and Afro-Latinate slink. Deeper lounge lizards will get theirs in the syncopated shimmy of ‘The Happening Thing’ and the sublime vocal chops of ‘When You Need Me’ and ‘All I Need’, thru the frankly sexy ‘Tension’ and that chef’s kiss twinkle of percussion and choral pads in ‘Ribbons.’

What a G?! Tip!
items._cn_summary: 这是Larry Heard以Mr Fingers名义发行的第七张录音室专辑，距离他最早的12寸唱片问世已逾四十年。专辑收录十二首作品，横跨芝加哥酸House、Italo disco、ambient合成器音乐与灵魂爵士等多个领域。他标志性的TB-303在标题曲、Barndance、Menagerie、April Rain等曲目中以不同形态出现，涵盖酸性律动的饱满绽放、布鲁斯式迷醉摇摆、以及嵌入钢琴柔光旋律中的细腻运用。其余曲目倾向于灵魂爵士与非洲-拉丁元素的融合，The Happening Thing的切分律动、When You Need Me与All I Need的人声切片采样、Tension的暧昧质感、以及Ribbons中打击乐与合唱pad交织的精致编排，共同勾勒出一位资深制作人对舞曲美学的整体把握。

items.body:
Originally titled 'In a Minor Groove' and released in 1958, Dorothy Ashby's 'Plays for Beautiful People' is an early quartet recording from the legendary harpist.

Early on in Ashby's career, a decade before 'Afro-Harping' allowed her the opportunity to explore more idiosyncratic territory, she was still attempting to make a name for herself on the modern jazz and bebop circuit, working alongside saxophonist and flautist Frank Wess and rattling through the standards. And 'Plays for Beautiful People' is among the best of her early collaborations, featuring Roy Haynes on drums and Herman Wright on bass, alongside Ashby and Wess. And although it's mostly covers - there's versions of Cole Porter's popular 'You'd Be So Nice To Come Home To' and the 'Roberta' standout 'Yesterdays', plus a swinging version of the 'Flying Colors' song 'Alone Together' - there's a couple of Ashby's originals thrown in for good measure.

Opener 'Rascality' presents her virtuosic harp playing without interruption, aptly backed up by Wess's breathy flute tones and we can't believe 'It's A Minor Thing' hasn't been sampled to death yet. Because Pete Rock already cut Ashby's version of 'Bohemia After Dark' to ribbons on his 'Return of the SP1200 Vol. 2' LP.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是竖琴演奏家Dorothy Ashby在1958年发行的早期四重奏录音，原名《In a Minor Groove》，属于她在现代爵士和bebop领域的起步阶段作品。专辑中她与萨克斯/长笛演奏家Frank Wess、鼓手Roy Haynes、贝斯手Herman Wright合作，以翻唱爵士经典为主，涵盖Cole Porter的《You'd Be So Nice To Come Home To》、《Yesterdays》以及《Alone Together》等曲目。开头曲《Rascality》展示了Ashby的竖琴技艺，配合Wess气息绵长的长笛音色，而《It's A Minor Thing》和《Bohemia After Dark》等曲也曾被嘻哈制作人Pete Rock采样。作为Ashby探索个人风格之前的作品，这张专辑展现了传统爵士四重奏框架内的扎实演奏，但尚未进入她后来在《Afro-Harping》中所呈现的更具个性与融合色彩的音乐领域。

items.body:
On his mean solo debut for Samurai, Naarm’s prolific Pugilist exerts rollicking sidespins on  jungle tekno, D&B, and electronica FFO Tim Reaper, Nebuchadnezzar, DJ Gonz.

With over 40 releases to his credit for a host of key dance stables - 3024 thru Trule and Rupture London - Pugilist arguably coughs up some of his strongest for Geoff Presha’s leading-edge D&B label. He gets right inside the slipstream space between DJ Gonz and Nebuchadnezzar on the twitchy, rolling jungle tekno futurism of ‘Rune’, and snaps to fiercest upfront tech step mutation with added hydrodynamic pressure on ‘Pyre’, whereas ‘Woven’ trims it right back to sinuous modular synth arp and glyding pads  tucked to an effortless, brisk velocity, and ‘Machiavellian’ lest the breaks loose in a wraithlike echo of OG jungle tekno.
items._genre: jungle / drum and bass / electronica / tekno
items._cn_summary: 这是澳大利亚墨尔本制作人Pugilist在Samurai厂牌的首张个人专辑，汇集了他多年来在3024、Trule、Rupture London等地下舞蹈厂牌的创作经验。整张作品围绕丛林Tekno与鼓打贝斯展开，在DJ Gonz与Nebuchadnezzar式的锐利节拍与Nebuchadnezzar的滑流空间之间游走。'Rune'呈现出抽搐式的滚动丛林未来主义，'Pyre'则将技术步态推至最凶猛的突变形态并加入液压般的重压感。'Woven'回归精简，以蜿蜒的模块化合成器琶音与滑翔式pad铺陈出轻盈迅捷的氛围，'Machiavellian'则放开碎拍，营造出OG丛林Tekno的幽灵般回响。专辑整体在速度感与氛围之间持续切换，但评论内容较为简短，对专辑全貌与制作细节的揭示有限。

items.body:
Recorded between 1961 and 1963 and released on Impulse! Records in July 1963, Impressions documents John Coltrane’s classic quartet with pianist McCoy Tyner, bassist Jimmy Garrison, and drummer Elvin Jones.

"Two selections — “India” and “Impressions” originate from the group’s November 1961 engagement at the Village Vanguard, where the quartet was joined by Eric Dolphy on alto saxophone, bass clarinet, and flute and second bassist Reggie Workman.

These are paired with the studio recordings “Up ’Gainst the Wall” (recorded September 18, 1962) and “After the Rain” (recorded April 29, 1963 at Van Gelder Studio in Englewood Cliffs, NJ), the latter featuring Roy Haynes on drums.

Issued during the same period as albums including Coltrane and Live at Birdland, Impressions forms part of Coltrane’s early-1960s Impulse! discography, demonstrating the quartet’s unique power in both expanded live performance and studio contexts.

Verve’s Acoustic Sounds Series features transfers from analog tapes and remastered 180-gram vinyl in deluxe gatefold packaging."
items._genre: hard bop / post-bop / free jazz / modal jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了约翰·柯川经典四重奏在1961至1963年间的录音，包括两段来自Village Vanguard的现场演出（Eric Dolphy助阵）以及两段录音室作品。专辑呈现了柯川四重奏在扩展编制现场表演与录音室语境中的独特力量，曲目涵盖“India”“Impressions”等经典之作，以及“Up 'Gainst the Wall”和“After the Rain”。本次再版采用Verve的Acoustic Sounds系列，以模拟磁带转录并重新母带处理，180克黑胶豪华双折包装发行。内容偏重发行信息陈述与厂牌技术规格介绍，对音乐本身的艺术分析较少。

items.body:
Chicago Footwork’s keynote series hails the nu and old skools - RP Boo, Jana Rush and DJ Spinn thru The Era Footwork Crew, DJ Jalen, and Bancal - on a hard hour of club pressure.

Absolutely no messing about here, everyone serves the most potent, upfront examples of Windy City knees-up. There’s 18 to get thru so let’splay faves: it’s heavily front loaded with the taut footwork-drill-jungle pressure of DJs Chad, Taso, Gant-Man & DJ Spinn on ‘Goofiez’, and overproof levels of cone-blowing bass in ‘Back It Up’ by DJ Chad & Jana Rush, while DJ Manny ideally simmers the heat on a dream meeting of ’94 jungle and ’26 footwork in ‘Freakout’. DJ Spinn & Moondoctor keep the hyper soul burning in the jazz-fusion type chord chops and hollers of ‘2 Da Moon’, and DJ Jalen stakes out a futurist ring of fire in the jabbing panic sequence ‘Redzone’, MoonDoctor goes double dark with the gothic minor key motifs of ‘Good Morning’, and Mel G neatly seals the US-UK thing with a slice of psych-soul-style footwork jungle in ‘Sweet as Gold’.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦芝加哥Footwork俱乐部场景，收录十八首作品，融合新锐与老牌制作人。整体风格以高密度的切分节奏、低频冲击和俱乐部压力为核心，曲目如DJ Chad与Jana Rush合作的《Back It Up》展现强劲低音，DJ Manny的《Freakout》将九十年代jungle与当代footwork并置，DJ Spinn与Moondoctor的《2 Da Moon》则在jazz-fusion和弦切分中延伸灵魂律动。Mel G的《Sweet as Gold》以psychedelic-soul质感串联英美footwork与jungle脉络，MoonDoctor的《Good Morning》以哥特小调动机走暗色路线。整体制作扎实，呈现明确的芝加哥地域风格，但在声音实验性上偏向类型内部深化，未做大幅度跨领域拓展。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — After a series of EPs and singles in the early 2020s, most of which were arrangements of traditional or traditional sounding British Isles folk, this London quintet released a debut full length album which inevitably seemed more mature than your typical coming out production. Moreover, with 2 members of latter day JETHRO TULL lineups, they had studied under the right masters, albeit well past their peak. But to suggest a pure bloodline here would be to shoehorn a half century of influences whether personally lived or appreciated after the fact.Thus when I listen to this 70 minute opus with a Welsh GPS address but no Welsh lyrics I can discern, I hear mashups of the distant and recent past, from TULL (with more conventional and palatable vocals than even 1968 Ian) to CLANNAD to TEMPEST to MAGO DE OZ, NIGHTWISH and TORNAOD, to CIRCULUS and THOBY LOTH, but always being themselves. While some veers a tad towards silly Tolkienisms, so did our shrouded heroes, time and again, so we can forgive ALBION for these indulgences, not to mention for taking the same name as a consummate Polish neo prog group (is there any other kind?) as well as a primeval more closely allied UK folk rock project THE ALBION BAND, a group I cannot mention without plugging their 1978 masterpiece "Rise up Like the Sun".Even if part of ALBION's prog credentials stems from a librarian's over the glasses glance at track and album length, which can be accused of bloat (also not an unfamiliar concept in our realms), this is still a catchy yet solemn blend of prog, folk, and metal, best shepherded by "Pagan Spirit", "The Dream of Rhonabwy", "Finding Avalon", "Black Lake", "Llyn Y Fan Fawr". As much as these impress, it's the tribute to the great Canadiana singer/songwriter STAN ROGERS in a debauched version of his "Barrett's Privateers" that hits escape velocity. While Rogers, who died in an Air Canada crash in the early 1980s, was always voluntarily constrained by his wordsmithery that required every meaning wrung out of every phrase, ALBION wisely chooses to instead rely on a hard rock arrangement that only fortifies Rogers' legacy while perhaps hotwiring their own. I'm going to round up from roughly 3.5 stars because I genuinely appreciate the attitude here, and it delivers much more of a musical itinerary than mere descriptions promised. Lake house music for those who resent their neighbors.

items.body: When life feels painfully empty, fantasy rushes in to occupy the space. Reinvention begins to resemble transcendence: the promise that the ordinary self might be remade into something larger, stranger, and seemingly indestructible. Yet when dissatisfaction hardens into appetite, self-invention can become self-erasure. The search for meaning may offer a taste of power while quietly stripping away the person who began it. Berlin newcomers Void Queen give that hunger a hard, low-slung pulse on “Power Sip,” premiering below. Out now via Duchess Box Records, the track is the first single from the band’s forthcoming debut EP, I Wanna Know, arriving on August 21. After a brief buildup, “Power Sip” locks into a brisk, bass-driven charge. The song sits at the intersection of Penetration’s melodic punk urgency, Au Pairs’ bass-led post-punk tension, and The Runaways’ rough-edged rock ’n’ roll swagger. Pounding drums and a forceful low end provide its physical momentum, while restless guitar textures gather around Vilte Stasiuleviciute’s smoky, emotionally charged vocal. Her delivery shifts from measured restraint toward mounting urgency as the arrangement moves between melodic clarity and gritty intensity. Lyrically, the song turns that hunger inward. Suspended between illusion and reality, it examines the urge to transform the ordinary into something extraordinary, even at the cost of losing oneself in the process. False immortality, emotional isolation, and self-confrontation converge in what Void Queen calls “a story about becoming everything you once swore you’d never be.” Listen to “Power Sip” below: Void Queen formed in Berlin in March 2024 following a last-minute lineup change. Guitarist Tobi Rachuj and drummer Merlin Niklasch were playing together in another project when their singer withdrew shortly before a scheduled concert. Stasiuleviciute stepped in as a temporary replacement, but by the trio’s second rehearsal, they had already written their first original song, “Suga.” Longtime friend Helge Siara initially helped the group record demos in his rehearsal-space studio before joining permanently on bass. Those early DIY sessions yielded the band’s first releases, including “Suga,” “Seventeen,” and “Six Feet Underground,” capturing the raw intensity that would become central to Void Queen’s identity. Momentum came quickly. After early performances in Copenhagen, Void Queen sold out a headline show at Berlin’s Badehaus less than a year after forming. A live session and interview on Fritz FM, along with coverage in Tagesspiegel, further established the group within the city’s underground guitar scene. The forthcoming I Wanna Know EP expands upon the dark energy of those early recordings, placing emotional vulnerability within explosive rock dynamics. The release further sharpens the qualities already present in “Power Sip”: driving rhythms, atmospheric tension, melodic immediacy, and a refusal to settle inside rigid genre boundaries. “Power Sip” is out now via Duchess Box Records. Stream the single here. Following their recent appearance at Berlin’s Fête de la Musique, Void Queen will perform at Rocktreff Open Air in Berlin on July 3. items._cn_summary: 柏林新晋乐队Void Queen首张EP首支单曲聚焦虚假不朽与情感孤立主题。歌曲以贝斯驱动的急促节奏为基础，融合Penetration的旋律朋克冲劲、Au Pairs的后朋克张力与The Runaways的摇滚粗粝感。鼓击与低频构成物理性推进力，失真吉他纹理包裹主唱低沉而情感充沛的人声，演绎从克制逐步升级为紧迫感。歌词内省式地审视将平凡转化为非凡的渴望，即使以自我消亡为代价。乐队2024年3月因临时换将而组建，DIY录音诞生首批作品，凭早期现场迅速在柏林地下吉他场景建立地位。EP在Duchess Box Records发行，延续早期录音的暗黑能量，将情感脆弱置于爆发性摇滚动力学中，拒绝被固化的类型边界所限定。

items.body: New dark electro-pop artist THEA (aka Teodora Pindaru) announced a debut single, “Ghost in the Machine“, with a videotoday June 25, 2026. A streaming release is expected on July 2, 2026. The THEA “Ghost in the Machine” single was produced and managed by the Tomato Music Lab project and offers a cinematic dark/electro-pop track. “Ghost in the Machine” deals with the boundary between technological alienation and human vulnerability. THEA adds: ““Ghost in the Machine” is a track that presents itself as an unsatisfactory answer to the question “Who am I?”. When the question “Who am I?” arises in the mind, the track offers a series of assumptions, hasty concepts, and false myths characteristic of a mind new to the art of introspection. Driven by fear and ignorance, the person moves within themselves to search for themselves, but there is no light, no instructions, and no guide. The person observes certain repetitive mental behaviors, seeks control, experiences torment and frustration, to the point of questioning their own existence.” About THEA THEA is the musical project of Teodora Pindaru, an artist and singer from Transylvania, Romania. Her work touches the region’s geography, history, and post-regime transition period. Her music combines dark pop and experimental electronic elements. The project is built around a collaboration with Tomato Music Lab, which develops the production and electronic sound design. Over these arrangements, THEA adds vocal melodies and lyrics focused on introspection, memory, and psychological tension. The debut single “Ghost in the Machine” is set for a video release on June 25, 2026 and a streaming release on July 2, 2026.
items._cn_summary: THEA是来自罗马尼亚特兰西瓦尼亚的艺术家Teodora Pindaru的暗黑电子流行项目，首支单曲《Ghost in the Machine》以电影化的暗黑电流行曲式探索技术异化与人类脆弱性之间的边界。歌词层面聚焦于内向自省、记忆与心理张力，呈现面对'我是谁'这一根本追问时意识中的恐惧、执念与反复行为。制作由Tomato Music Lab负责电子声音设计与编曲，THEA本人叠加人声旋律与词作。该项目扎根于特兰西瓦尼亚的地理、历史及后政权转型期的文化语境，将地域文化记忆融入暗潮与实验电子的混合声响中。作为新晋艺人的首支单曲，整体呈现概念驱动与氛围营造并重的制作方向，电子质感与暗黑人声形成统一表达，显示出一定的艺术自觉，但在声音实验性与创新深度方面尚需更多作品来验证。

items.body: HAAi has released the single “DIGITiSE” and announced a new album of the same name, due 9 October 2026 on Mute. The London-based, Australian-born producer, DJ and songwriter, born Teneil Throssell, issued the title track on 24 June 2026 as the first single from the 10-track record, which Mute will release on vinyl and digitally. HAAi “DIGITiSE” is a dancefloor-oriented companion to her 2025 album “HUMANiSE”. HAAi ‘DIGITiSE’: release details and tracklist “DIGITiSE” runs to 10 tracks and continues directly from “HUMANiSE”: the closing track of the 2025 album fades out on a choir that returns on the opening track of the new record. HAAi has described the album as the predecessor’s “bigger, ravey sibling”, adding that “DIGITiSE holds the hand of HUMANiSE and walks it to the club.” She tied the project to her DJ work: “DIGITiSE was created with intention: I wanted to make music I could play when I DJ. I wanted it to sonically spread across multiple lanes in the way I would play an all night long set.” The album brings in new collaborators alongside returning ones. New voices include Echonomist, Skybreak and Cantoalegre, a children’s choir from Medellín, Colombia, while Pat Alvarez, ILA, James Messiah and Kaiden Ford have worked with HAAi before. Martin Falck, who has worked with Fever Ray and The Knife, led the album’s visuals. The tracklist is: “RE-HUMANiSE” (feat. Kaiden Ford and ILA), “Printerlude”, “Ignition” (feat. Echonomist), “Depth Perception”, “DIGITiSE” (feat. Pat Alvarez), “Technology”, “HUMANiSE Radio”, “THANK U”, “I Wanna Feel Like Someone” (feat. James Messiah) and “Talking Walls” (feat. Skybreak and Cantoalegre). Mute releases the album on 9 October 2026 on vinyl and digital, with pre-orders open. The title track features producer and songwriter Pat Alvarez and arrived on 24 June 2026 with a video. HAAi placed the song at the center of the album, calling it “the nucleus of the whole album. It’s a nod to the dance floor. A space of belonging and connection. Listen loud.” The single is available across streaming platforms, and the clip streams as HAAi – “DIGITiSE” (Official Video). About HAAi HAAi is the project of Teneil Throssell, an Australian-born, London-based DJ, producer and songwriter. She released her debut studio album “Baby, We’re Ascending” on 27 May 2022 through Mute, a 13-track record with guests including Jon Hopkins and Hot Chip’s Alexis Taylor. In November 2023 she compiled an edition of the “DJ-Kicks” mix series for !K7 Records. Her second studio album, “HUMANiSE”, followed on 10 October 2025 on Mute, preceded by the singles “Satellite”, “Can’t Stand To Lose”, “Hey!” and “Stitches”. That album set out themes of community and connection in a digital age, built around HAAi’s own vocals and guests including Jon Hopkins, Alexis Taylor and the choir Trans Voices. “DIGITiSE”, her third studio album, extends that work toward the dancefloor and arrives on Mute on 9 October 2026, a year after “HUMANiSE”.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是HAAi为DJ演出场景量身打造的作品，延续其2025年专辑的脉络，定位为'更大、更狂野的俱乐部兄弟篇'。制作上强调多轨并行编排，意图覆盖整夜DJ set的不同能量区间。专辑邀请了多位合作者，包括哥伦比亚麦德林儿童合唱团Cantoalegre，为电子框架注入人声层次。曾与Fever Ray和The Knife合作的Martin Falck负责视觉设计，与HAAi过往的实验电子美学保持一致。作为Mute厂牌发行的俱乐部导向作品，在电子音乐范畴内具有一定制作水准，但整体取向更偏舞曲实用性而非深度实验探索，合作者阵容为其增添了跨文化与跨风格的潜力。

items.body: Ego Bliss, an electronic act from Tijuana, Mexico, have released the album “Afterlife” through Infacted Recordings. The twelve-track record is out now on CD and digital, and streams on Bandcamp. The band brings a dark synth-pop sound that mixes electro and futurepop elements, built on club-driven rhythms, synth atmospheres and cinematic textures. “Afterlife” runs twelve tracks: “Inception,” “Consequence,” “Always And Never,” “Fragile,” “Afterlife,” “We Fall,” “Ascend,” “Moments,” “Ego Nation,” “Downfall,” “The World at Your Feet” and “Afterdeath.” Afterlife by Ego Bliss The title track “Afterlife” leads the album: About Ego Bliss Ego Bliss is an electronic project from Tijuana, Mexico, and a recent signing to Infacted Recordings, the German label founded in 2001 and run by Torben Schmidt that works in electro, synth-pop and futurepop. Before joining Infacted, the project issued earlier work through the Mexican label Sector Industrial Producciones; Side-Line reviewed the EP “Future” and the album “What The Future Holds”. According to the label, “Afterlife” was shaped over about two and a half years and draws on themes of loss and change. The album is the project’s first release for Infacted Recordings, following its earlier work on Sector Industrial Producciones.
items._cn_summary: Ego Bliss 来自墨西哥蒂华纳，是一支电子项目，通过德国独立厂牌 Infacted Recordings 发行了专辑《Afterlife》。整张专辑共收录十二首曲目，制作周期约两年半，围绕失落与变迁的主题展开。音乐风格以暗黑合成器流行（dark synth-pop）为核心，融合 electro 与 futurepop 元素，依赖俱乐部导向的节奏框架、合成器氛围铺陈以及电影化的声效纹理。专辑曲目包括《Inception》《Consequence》《Fragile》《Afterlife》《We Fall》等，标题曲作为开篇引领整体氛围。此前该项目的作品由墨西哥厂牌 Sector Industrial Producciones 发行，《Afterlife》是其加入 Infacted Recordings 后的首张专辑。整体定位偏向类型化电子场景内的常规制作，具有俱乐部实用性与一定的氛围深度，但在声音设计的实验性或跨界融合方面缺少明显的突破。

items.body: Hunter As a Horse, the project of South African musician Mia van Wyk, will release the debut album “Paradise Lost” on Metropolis Records on July 24, 2026. The twelve-track album follows five singles issued on the label. Hunter As a Horse bring a cinematic strain of electronic dark-pop that mixes alternative, dream-pop and nu-goth elements, built on Mia van Wyk’s vocals and dark, atmospheric production. “Paradise Lost” runs twelve tracks: “Here’s To All The Ones,” “Kiss of Death,” “Object,” “Obey,” “Masochist,” “The Fortress,” “Paradise Lost,” “Go To Bed Now,” “Leviathan,” “Lighthouse,” “Dark Sky” and “Dead Things.” It gathers the singles van Wyk has released since signing to Metropolis Records in early 2026 – including “Lighthouse” and “Here’s To All The Ones” – alongside new songs. Paradise Lost by Hunter As a Horse van Wyk described the record as a single, connected work: “It was the first time I really started thinking in terms of a connected body of work, so it felt natural to take that further with “Paradise Lost”. It is designed to be heard as one piece, even though the songs are quite different individually.” On its themes, she added that the album “deals with my shadow, my transformation and my inner architecture, and I have tried to show what is deep inside myself.” The title track “Paradise Lost” leads the album: About Hunter As a Horse Hunter As a Horse (HAAH) is the project of South African musician and vocalist Mia van Wyk, based in the Western Cape. Over roughly a decade she has self-released singles and EPs that pair electronic production with dark, cinematic arrangements, moving between alternative, electronic and dream-pop. Her 2025 EP “Anathema” marked a shift toward a connected body of work, a thread she carried into “Paradise Lost.” Songs by Hunter As a Horse have appeared in television series including American Horror Story, Riverdale and Elite, and the film “Wander Darkly.” After signing to Metropolis Records in early 2026 and releasing five singles, van Wyk gathers that run on her first full-length album, due July 24, 2026.
items._cn_summary: 南非音乐人Mia van Wyk以Hunter As a Horse之名在Metropolis Records发行首张全长专辑《Paradise Lost》，收录十二首作品，将另类、梦幻流行与新哥特元素融合于电子暗黑流行的框架中，以人声与暗色氛围制作为骨架。她将此前发行的五支单曲与新作汇为一体，强调专辑作为整体叙事的连贯性，主题围绕内心阴影、蜕变与内在结构展开。制作上以电影化的暗黑电子编排见长，歌曲曾在《美国恐怖故事》《河谷镇》等影视作品中出现。文本内容偏新闻发布性质，缺乏对具体音乐技法的深入剖析，但作为来自非洲南部、带有暗潮气质并融合多元流行元素的独立项目，仍具有一定的跨界实验色彩。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / freeform rap
items._cn_summary: 这是一张在芝加哥南区的街道上完成的田野录音作品，声音记录者Ian Brennan邀请了二十五位遭受枪支暴力影响的居民参与录制，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家前廊，正处于机场降落航道下方，街区内有流浪犬出没。录制当天恰好遇上特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队。项目强调没有任何音乐叠加，所有声响均来自现场环境。文中特别指出主动讲述者反而最缺乏说服力，而那些不情愿开口的人道出了最动人的故事。一位长者在讲述失去两个儿子后情绪崩溃，反复道歉，但作者认为社会才是真正需要道歉的一方。项目收益将捐给致力于以公共卫生方式终结暴力的公益机构。作品本身介于田野录音与口述记录之间，含少量自由式说唱。

items.body:
In 2026, I was invited to join the Silkroad Ensemble, the international collective directed by Rhiannon Giddens, as a musician (frame drums, violin, and voice) and contributor of new arrangements and compositions. Following an initial workshop and preview performance in New York in January 2026, the project will unfold through a North American tour in March 2026, featuring nine concerts alongside workshops and community outreach activities across the United States, as part of the new program
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
. The tour will continue later in the year with further residencies and performances in North America and Europe.
There are musical projects that are built around a repertoire, others around a geography, and others still around a specific aesthetic vision. The Silkroad Ensemble belongs to a different category: it is a living organism built around an idea. A simple and radical idea at once�that music can be a real space of encounter between cultures, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a daily, concrete, lived practice.
Founded in 1998 by Yo-Yo Ma, Silkroad has never been an ensemble in the traditional sense. There is no fixed lineup, no stable repertoire. Instead, it is a community of musicians from different traditions, chosen not only for their technical excellence, but for their ability to inhabit a threshold�the space between rootedness and transformation. Each musician brings with them a language, a sound, a memory. What matters most is the willingness to place that language in dialogue with others, without hierarchy.
In recent years, the project has been guided by Rhiannon Giddens, one of the most powerful and deeply insightful voices in contemporary music. Her presence gives the work a clear direction: the goal is not to create an artificial synthesis of traditions, but to create the conditions for each tradition to speak fully, and to transform through encounter. Rhiannon possesses a rare kind of leadership�one that never imposes itself, but quietly shapes the space, both musically and humanly.
Entering this context means immediately finding yourself in a space where musical identity is not something to defend, but something to offer. The pizzica, the frame drums, the violin I carry with me are no longer only instruments of a local tradition, but elements in a broader conversation, where every sound is heard both for what it is and for what it might become.
It is within this space that my participation in Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual began to take shape. Even before the music itself, what stands out is the quality of listening. A real, deep listening, in which every musical gesture is at once personal and collective. This, perhaps, is the true nature of Silkroad: not simply an ensemble, but a place. A circle. A space where music returns to what it has always been�a form of relationship.
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
Music as Refuge and Resistance
The word sanctuary can be understood in many ways: refuge, protected space, a place where it is still possible to pause, to listen, to rebuild a sense of community.
Working on this project in the United States today carries a particular weight. This is a country marked by deep and increasingly visible tensions, where public discourse is often shaped by fear, by closure, by the idea that identity is something to be defended against someone else. The same tendency can be seen elsewhere�in Italy, across Europe, and in many parts of the world. The rise of nationalism, ongoing wars, and increasingly restrictive migration policies contribute to a climate in which separation begins to feel like the natural order of things.
Within this context, finding yourself in a room each day with musicians from Morocco, India, Japan, Armenia, Scotland, Congo, Italy, and the United States becomes something very real. Each person brings their own history, their own sound, their own way of inhabiting music. What emerges is not a fusion of identities, but their coexistence.
The taranta, Gnawa music, Indian classical tradition, American folk music�these practices were never conceived merely as forms of entertainment. They were born as tools to accompany moments of transformation, to help individuals and communities move through crisis, grief, healing, and renewal.
Sanctuary begins with this understanding. With the idea that music can still be a space where encounter is possible without the need to simplify or protect oneself. A space where listening becomes an act of trust.
Something simple and real happens: people from different parts of the world breathe together, listen together, and build something that did not exist before. In a time that often pushes toward division, this act acquires a different weight. It becomes, in its own quiet way, a form of resistance.
Entering the Circle
The first rehearsals are always a delicate moment. I took part in an initial workshop in Ireland last December, with a smaller group�Rhiannon, Mazz, Francesco, Niwel, and myself�and then a second workshop with the full ensemble in January, followed by a beautiful preview performance in New York on January 10, 2026, as part of the Winter Jazz Fest.
At that stage, there is no shared language yet. You observe each other, you play, you try things, you listen. What strikes you immediately is the extraordinary musical and human level of the people involved. They are incredible. Not only great instrumentalists, but musicians who have developed a deep relationship with their own musical traditions, and who have learned to question them, to keep them flexible and alive.
The Hawaiian bassist Shawn Conley, for example, moves effortlessly between bow and pizzicato, shifting from a lyrical, singing tone to remarkable rhythmic agility, using the instrument with a freedom that easily recalls the expressive range of a cello.
Beside him, Scottish harpist Maeve Gilchrist brings a presence that is both refined and fearless. Beyond a complete mastery of everything one might expect from the harp�the luminous, almost celestial sound�she possesses an extraordinary rhythmic and harmonic awareness, and a musical curiosity that allows her to make bold, unexpected choices without hesitation.
Armenian cellist Karen Ouzounian represents the very highest level of classical tradition, but with something more: a strong personal voice, a deep compositional sensibility, and a lyrical approach to improvisation that makes every gesture feel necessary.
With Francesco Turrisi, who like me comes from Italy, we already share a longer history. Yet I remain constantly struck by his ability to move between radically different instruments�accordion, piano, frame drums, string instruments�with complete naturalness. His immense musicality is not tied to any single instrument, but to a broader understanding of sound, form, and structure.
Congolese guitarist Niwel Tsumbu is simply one of the finest guitarists I have ever encountered. His relationship with the guitar transcends the instrument itself. He brings together a deep knowledge of African musical traditions, an innate rhythmic sensibility, refined harmonic awareness, and an extraordinary improvisational freedom.
Kaoru Watanabe embodies, in a profound way, the idea that tradition is also a choice. Japanese and American, he moves fluidly between cultural languages with a rare balance of respect, discipline, and expressive freedom. His playing is never a reproduction of the past, but its living continuation.
With Mehdi Nassouli, on guembri and voice, I feel a particular closeness. Like me with pizzica, he belongs deeply to a specific musical world�in his case, the Gnawa tradition of Morocco. Yet his experience has given him an equally deep ability to engage in dialogue with other musical languages, without ever losing the center of his own sound.
Sandeep Das�s presence on tabla is a constant point of reference. He is, quite literally, a guru of Indian music, and yet his authority never creates distance. On the contrary, he makes every interaction feel natural, effortless, both musically and humanly.
Japanese percussionist Haruka Fujii brings an extraordinary level of precision and listening. Her virtuosity is never displayed for its own sake, but always placed in service of the music, strengthening the cohesion of the ensemble.
American violinist and vocalist Mazz Swift embodies a rare combination of strength and openness. Their voice and violin move fluidly across genres and traditions, grounded yet constantly searching, expanding the expressive space of the group.
And then there is Rhiannon. It is difficult to find a single word that captures her presence. She is a complete musician�singer, instrumentalist, composer, dancer, and leader�but above all, she possesses a clarity of vision that holds everything together and inspires everyone around her. Her leadership does not operate through control, but through listening. She creates a space in which each musician can fully express themselves, while contributing to something larger than any individual voice.
Common Ground
"Common Ground" is the pizzica I wrote for the Silkroad Ensemble. I use the word �wrote� with caution, because the piece truly exists only through the creative contribution of each musician involved. I laid the foundations: the rhythm, the groove, the structure, the overall architecture, and the fixed melodic and harmonic elements. But what makes it alive is the way each musician inhabits it.
The idea first emerged during the workshop in Ireland. At that stage, we were still searching for common ground, a way of being together musically without renouncing our individual identities. It felt natural for me to bring the rhythm of pizzica�my familiar and chosen refuge, my Sanctuary.
Back home, I began to develop that intuition, shaping a structure that preserved the physical and rhythmic core of the tradition, while remaining open enough to allow each musician to find their own place within it. We worked on the piece during the workshop in the United States, and performed it live for the first time in New York, just days later, at the Winter Jazz Fest.
It was extraordinary to witness how naturally each musician entered that rhythm without hesitation. No one was trying to imitate something that did not belong to them. Instead, each voice emerged clearly, freely coexisting alongside the others.
In that moment, I understood that the piece had found its true meaning. It was no longer simply the pizzica I had written, but a shared space. A Common Ground laid beneath our feet.
Experiences like this change you in subtle but lasting ways. The energy they transmit, the enthusiasm, the renewed sense of trust in the future�all of it remains.
A few years ago, I was in Adelaide to perform at WOMAD with Justin Adams, and the night before our concert I had the chance to attend a performance by Billy Bragg. At one point, he said something that has stayed with me ever since: �Music does not have the power to change the world. But it can make you believe that the world can be changed.�

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Still Life" is a double album live release by US progressive metal act Fates Warning. The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in October 1998. It bridges the gap between Fates Warning�s eighthand ninth full-length studio albums "A Pleasant Shade of Gray" (1997) and "Disconnected" (2000).Disc 1 features a live performance of the full "A Pleasant Shade of Gray" album while disc 2features six tracks from the band�s four 1988-1994 albums and "Prelude to Ruin" from "Awaken theGuardian" (1986). So, basically songs from all Ray Alder fronted Fates Warning albums (up untilthen) and one track from a John Arch fronted Fates Warning album.As if a full performance of the 51:56 minutes long concept album "A Pleasant Shade of Gray"including all sub-tracks wasn�t enough, Fates Warning have also opted to include a live performanceof their second longest epic, the nearly 21 minutes long "The Ivory Gate Of Dreams", so it�s safe tosay Fates Warning are firing on all cylinders on "Still Life". As for the remaining tracks it�salways hard to satisfy every fan when you are eight albums into your career and that career isdivided into two chapters with two different vocalists, but I�d say that tracks like "The EleventhHour", "Monument", and "Point Of View" belong here just fine and the nod towards the Arch-frontedera of Fates Warning with "Prelude to Ruin" is a nice touch too, although hearing Ray Alder sing thesong takes some getting used to. He does a great job though and provides the song with his ownidentity.Fates Warning was down to a trio at this point (Lead vocalist Ray Alder, Drummer Mark Zonder, andguitarist Jim Matheos), but on "Still Life" they are assisted by three session musicians and themusical performances are on a high level throughout. Bassist Joey Vera (who would soon become apermanent member of Fates Warning) sings harmony vocals, which is an important detail as a lot ofFates Warning�s songs feature harmony vocals and choirs. The audience helps the best they can toothough. The best example of that is probably when they sing the beautiful and epic wordless part on"The Eleventh Hour". I�m getting goosebumps because it feels like being there in that venue withthem. There�s some great audience participation all the way through "Still Life" and it�s a livealbum which actually feels like it was recorded live without too many overdubs despite featuring anexcellent live production job. "Still Life" is upon conclusion a high quality live album from FatesWarning and a 4 star (80%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._cn_summary: 这张双碟现场专辑收录了Fates Warning在现场完整演绎1997年概念专辑《A Pleasant Shade of Gray》的全过程，加上选自1988至1994年间四张专辑的六首曲目，以及一首由John Arch时期过渡到Ray Alder主唱的《Prelude to Ruin》。演出时乐队虽仅剩三人核心阵容，但通过三位客座乐手补全编制，Joey Vera的和声尤为关键。整张专辑制作精良，观众参与度高，现场感真实自然。尽管评论给予四星评价，但对偏好前卫实验与即兴融合的听众而言，这仍属于传统前卫金属范畴内的常规现场作品，创新性有限。

He sings it close and cracked, the rasp catching as he switches between English, Pidgin and Twi. Produced by longtime collaborator Joker and released through EMPIRE, the single sits inside PUMA’s World Cup campaign for Ghana, whose Black Stars reach their fifth FIFA World Cup this summer across the United States, Canada and Mexico. The song returns to what Black Sherif has written about since Konongo, the mining town in Ghana’s Ashanti Region where he grew up: getting through long odds, holding on to belief, and carrying his people with him. He brought afrobeats, highlife and asakaa, the Ghanaian drill sound, together early on, and the new single works from the barest version of that: a guitar figure, a low synth bed and his voice. “Find A Way” follows “SWAGGA“, his return to hip-hop after he was named Artiste of the Year for the second time at the 2026 Telecel Ghana Music Awards, and it arrives as he moves toward his biggest New York headline show yet, at the Hammerstein Ballroom on 1 August. At 24, Black Sherif is already Ghana’s most-streamed artist: his debut The Villain I Never Was has passed three billion streams, and IRON BOY, released in 2025, has crossed one billion. items.body: In today’s musical landscape, the duo format represents one of the most fascinating and demanding artistic challenges. It is not merely a matter of combining two virtuosos, but of creating a third musical identity born from setting aside individual ego in favor of a shared artistic breath. When this alchemy truly occurs, the acoustic space expands, transforming the intimacy of chamber music into soundscapes of almost orchestral breadth. It is within this delicate yet rigorous balance that the artistic journey of Carmelo Imbesi and Carmen Zangarà unfolds. The Imbesi Zangarà Duo defies rigid categorization: their musical identity is a prism through which the classical tradition is refracted, engaging with the sensibilities and expressive needs of the present day. Their performances give the guitar a warm, eloquent narrative voice capable of crossing stylistic boundaries and exploring new sonic territories with both naturalness and artistic awareness. Research into historical repertoire, neoclassical writing, crossover projects, social engagement, and theatrical performances devoted to the aesthetic experience intertwine with complementary expertise ranging from writing and coaching to teaching and music business. A duo, an artistic hub, a family. At a time when artistic identities are often shaped by easy categorization and immediate consumption, Carmelo and Carmen have chosen a different path—one founded on deep listening, meticulous attention to timbre, and continuous personal growth. The following interview explores a partnership that is intellectual before it is instrumental, offering insight into the artistic and human vision of two musicians who have built a coherent career spanning performance, research, composition, and education. Every story begins with a meeting. When your paths first crossed, did you immediately sense that your musical chemistry was something special—something that made you feel performing together was your natural direction? Everything happened in an incredibly spontaneous way. From the very first notes we played together, there was an immediate musical understanding. We never felt the need to negotiate between our individual identities in order to find balance; our sound emerged naturally, almost instinctively. That chemistry revealed itself through a shared breath, a dialogue that from the very beginning went far beyond technique and the written score. It was a genuine mutual recognition. We quickly realized that our encounter was much more than an academic collaboration—it answered a deep artistic necessity. The direction revealed itself naturally, allowing music, intuition, and our human connection to guide the journey. On your website you write: “Today we are a Family, and Music is our Home.” It is a phrase that evokes belonging, mutual care, and shared purpose. How has your personal and emotional journey influenced your artistic growth? Is there a boundary between everyday life and professional discipline? The evolution of our personal relationship is one of the essential foundations of our music. We believe it is difficult to bring genuine expressive truth to the stage without first living and nurturing it in one’s own life. We do not seek a strict boundary between everyday life and professional discipline. On the contrary, our shared life strengthens our artistic rigor. Because our relationship is built on trust, listening, and profound mutual understanding, we can be completely honest, demanding, and disciplined during rehearsals. There is no need for filters or defenses. For us, professional rigor is simply an extension of the care, respect, and responsibility we share as artists, musicians, and family. Your research focuses on overlooked repertoire and forgotten works. Through critical editions and carefully curated recordings, you have collaborated with numerous publishers and record labels. When approaching a rare score, how does your process of “translation” unfold? How do you balance historical authenticity with expressive freedom so that centuries-old music can still speak to contemporary audiences? For us, the idea of “translation” extends far beyond merely deciphering a manuscript or transcribing it into modern notation. Examining historical sources, understanding period performance practices, and correctly interpreting musical notation are essential steps, reflecting our academic background in music history and performance analysis. However, scholarly research alone risks producing little more than a museum piece—flawless from a philological perspective, yet lacking genuine expressive vitality. This is precisely where editing and, above all, recording become the meeting point between rigorous scholarship and artistic sensitivity. Every fingering, articulation, and tonal choice is a conscious attempt to restore voice and meaning to these works, allowing them to engage with modern listeners. Our goal is not simply to preserve a musical heritage, but to make it alive once again—so that audiences may experience the enduring relevance of music written in another era. Your live performances range from classical recitals across Europe and Asia to crossover projects and incidental music, eventually evolving into a more hybrid theatrical form. This journey led to Sulle note della Bellezza(“On the Notes of Beauty”), a concert-reading devoted to the aesthetic experience that combines music, poetry, philosophy, visual art, and faith, blending Carmelo’s theatrical background with Carmen’s vocal performances. What inspired this artistic hybridization? How does your role change when you become not only performers but also creators and directors of the entire stage experience? And what does Sulle note della Bellezzarepresent? For us, the stage has always been a place of absolute truth and communication. We perform because music completes us and allows us to express who we truly are; therefore, live performance is simply the natural extension of that necessity. When the need for expression becomes stronger, the boundaries between artistic languages naturally dissolve, and art becomes a single communicative flow. This inspired us to create a format capable of moving beyond the sometimes rigid rituals of the traditional concert, embracing instead a more immersive form of communication that could simultaneously engage both the emotional and intellectual dimensions of the audience. When we are no longer simply performers, our theatrical perspective expands to embrace spoken word, gesture, lighting design, and even silence. This creative freedom also brings greater responsibility, as every element contributes to the audience’s overall experience. Within this space, the guitar enters into dialogue with acting and singing, while our individual artistic backgrounds merge into a unified scenic vision. Sulle note della Bellezza is the culmination of this journey. It seeks to restore a sense of wonder and the experience of the sublime through philosophy, poetry, visual art, and spirituality. It is neither a traditional concert nor a theatrical reading, but rather a narrative journey in which words evoke images, the guitar creates sonic landscapes, and the voice opens an emotional space. Ultimately, it represents our artistic manifesto: the belief that art should not merely represent reality but become a living relationship between people, artistic languages, and the many dimensions of human experience. Since 2021 you have been part of INRI Classic’s roster, releasing original compositions such as Rainy Sunset – Memories from a Picture, Tears of War—inspired by the Russian-Ukrainian conflict and acknowledged in a personal letter from Pope Francis—and the intimate Whispers. What led you toward original composition, and how does the neoclassical language enable you to transform personal experience into music? Our desire to compose emerged naturally from our work as performers. As interpreters, we continually devote our sensitivity to bringing other composers’ music to life, but eventually we felt the need to express ourselves directly. The neoclassical language provided the ideal vocabulary: an intimate, essential, and deeply evocative style capable of combining the aesthetics of the classical tradition with a more immediate, cinematic dimension. Our work in incidental music has also played an important role in shaping this artistic direction. Each of these compositions reflects a different aspect of our journey. Rainy Sunset is deeply connected to our roots, translating into music the melancholy and beauty of sunsets suspended between Sicily and Calabria. Tears of War looks outward, born from our sense of helplessness in the face of contemporary conflict. Whispers, instead, turns inward, exploring the quiet voices of the mind and the fragility that belongs to every human being. Through composition, our guitars cease to be solely instruments of interpretation and become a means of giving voice to our own experiences, emotions, and reflections. It is a journey we continue to explore, one that remains very much alive. Returning to the letter you received from Pope Francis in response to Tears of War, this recognition highlights a vision of music that goes beyond aesthetics to embrace moral and civic responsibility. This perspective also emerges in Carmelo’s essays for Quinte Parallele, where he reflects on professional ethics, the dignity of the musical profession, and the educational role of teaching. How does this ethical awareness influence your daily choices, and what do you believe is the artist’s social responsibility today? Pope Francis’ letter was an unexpected and deeply moving gift. More importantly, it confirmed something we had already felt: even two guitars, when played with genuine intention, can become a language of peace and dialogue in a historical moment marked by conflict. Tears of War was born precisely as our refusal to remain silent. The same sensitivity informs the reflections we publish in Quinte Parallele. We believe music cannot be separated from the human context in which it is created. Virtuosity, visibility, and social media metrics are tools—not goals. We believe that contemporary artists have an ethical responsibility. We feel called to protect the humanity of our work, to preserve the dignity of those who listen and those whom we teach. Being musicians today also means choosing not to remain neutral—to use beauty not as self-celebration, but as a space for awareness, dialogue, and positive change. In a musical world increasingly driven by specialization, you have developed a career in which the guitar is at the center of a much broader system of artistic and professional skills. Alongside your concert activity, you are involved in entertainment law, publishing and recording collaborations, music journalism, Carmen’s soul singing projects, and coaching for musicians. How do these different dimensions coexist within your work? One of the most common misconceptions is that broadening one’s expertise inevitably distracts from music itself. For us, the opposite is true. Every field of study enriches the way we understand and experience our profession. Our background in entertainment law and music business, together with our work as journalists and essayists, enables us to view the industry from multiple perspectives, remain constantly informed, and collaborate with publishers and record labels more consciously. Before being a professional advantage, it is a source of artistic independence. Carmen’s vocal projects broaden our expressive horizon and keep us open to different musical languages. Connecting all these experiences are coaching and neuroscience. They have provided practical tools for developing our mindset, organizing our work, managing performance anxiety, communicating more effectively with our students, and preserving our balance both as a couple and as professionals. Ultimately, these different facets are not separate careers but expressions of a single artistic vision. They allow us to shape our path with greater awareness while remaining faithful to our identity. Speaking of education, from teaching at the Conservatory to founding the J.K. Mertz Academy, your work integrates neuroscience, coaching, and arts management. In a system that often emphasizes technical mastery while leaving students unprepared for the realities of professional life, your approach seems to offer a much broader perspective. How does this philosophy translate into practice? Music education often separates technical mastery from the practical realities of an artistic career, producing highly skilled performers who are not always prepared for the challenges of professional life. Our goal is to provide students with an education that supports every stage of their artistic journey. Our complementary areas of expertise were developed precisely to meet this need. Through coaching and neuroscience, we help students understand their mental processes, manage performance anxiety, and define meaningful goals. Through biomechanics and posture, we teach them how to care for their bodies—their most valuable instrument. Through entertainment law and arts management, we provide the essential knowledge needed to navigate today’s music industry with greater confidence while protecting their professional rights. For us, teaching music means much more than training performers. It means helping students become independent, responsible professionals capable of building sustainable careers while remaining true to their artistic identity. Finally, what is the essential message of the Imbesi Zangarà Duo? Always remain curious. Study everything—every experience has value. Reject hatred. Respect your identity and defend it at all costs. And never forget that the only thing that truly matters in making great music is Love. discover Imbesi Zangarà Duo’s music here: The post Sound, Research, and Vision: The Human and Artistic Journey of Carmelo Imbesi and Carmen Zangarà (Imbesi Zangarà Duo) first appeared on Modern Classical Music.

items.body: Pyrroline‘s “Ambiguity” is the electro-industrial project’s sixth album, announced for release on Electro Aggression Records as a Digipak CD. The label has opened pre-orders and lists the album as twelve tracks. “Ambiguity” is also available digitally through the Electro Aggression Records Bandcamp page. “Ambiguity” arrives five years after the double-CD “Struggling”. Across twelve tracks, the album moves through themes of transition, doubt, technological change and the effects of war. Named tracks include the title song, “Eventually”, “Ulysses” and “Already Defined?”. Ambiguity by PYRROLINE “Ambiguity” combines cold synthetic textures, driving rhythms and atmospheric soundscapes “with lyrics that remain deliberately open, fragmented and tense”. The label has shared a video from “Ambiguity” on YouTube. The CD edition is a Digipak; pre-orders are handled through the label. About Pyrroline Pyrroline is an electro-industrial and old-school EBM project made up of Arnte on vocals and Schmoun on synths and chants. The duo records for Electro Aggression Records, a label established in 2011 that focuses on old-school EBM and electronic-industrial music. Side-Line has covered the project’s earlier Electro Aggression Records releases, including “In the Dawn of Freedom” and the double-CD “Struggling”, the latter the project’s fifth album. With “Ambiguity”, Pyrroline returns to the label for a sixth full-length.

items.body: Nachtmahr “Imperivm” is the new studio album from the Austrian industrial and EBM project Nachtmahr, released on June 26, 2026 through Trisol Music Group. The record is issued as a CD in an A5 digipack with booklet, and it follows the 2024 album “Verboten!“. “Imperivm” holds ten tracks and opens with “Wer Wind sät”. The full tracklist is “Wer Wind sät”, “Unterwerfung”, “Nie zurück”, “Das Böse”, “Stärker als ihr Hass”, “Infantil”, “Der Schlaf”, “Willenlos”, “Offenbarung” and “Neue Ufer”. This is the solo project of Thomas Rainer, who has run it since 2007 alongside his work in L’Âme Immortelle. About Nachtmahr Nachtmahr is an Austrian industrial and EBM project founded by Thomas Rainer in Vienna in 2007. Rainer started the project as an outlet for harder material while working as a resident DJ at Club Pi in Vienna, and ran it in parallel with L’Âme Immortelle, the darkwave duo he formed with Sonja Kraushofer in 1996. The first release, the EP “Kunst ist Krieg”, appeared in 2007 through Trisol Music Group. Studio albums followed with “Feuer Frei!” in 2008, “Alle Lust Will Ewigkeit” in 2009 and “Semper Fidelis” in 2010. The project became known for militaristic visuals and lyrics centered on power and control, presented across albums, EPs and live shows. The project kept that output running through the EP “Widerstand“ in 2018 and the picture-vinyl reissue of the mini-album “Mädchen in Uniform” in 2019. The project returned in 2020 with “Flamme“, issued the double album “Unbeugsam” in 2023, and released “Verboten!” through Trisol on November 1, 2024. With “Imperivm”, released on June 26, 2026, Nachtmahr extends that Trisol run into a new studio album, its first since “Verboten!”.

items.body: Real Farmer “Live at The Dalby Cafe” is a new four-track live EP from the Dutch band Real Farmer, released on June 26, 2026 through Strap Originals. The “Live at The Dalby Cafe” EP and a full performance video were captured at the Dalby Cafe in Margate, the first in a series of Strap Originals curated sessions. Real Farmer bring a post-punk-adjacent sound that mixes DIY punk, angular art-rock and noise. Real Farmer ‘Live at The Dalby Cafe’: the live EP “Live at The Dalby Cafe” holds four tracks: “Heart Out,” “Missing Link,” “The Pressure Of Others” and “Once More.” According to the band, the session was recorded in a single continuous take at the Dalby Cafe in Margate, filmed by Roger Sargent with audio by Jason Stafford. The EP follows the band’s second album, “Two Wrongs Don’t Make A Right,” released on May 1, 2026 through Strap Originals. Real Farmer shared the full performance video: Real Farmer 2026 tour dates According to Strap Originals, Real Farmer will support The Sisters of Mercy on the September dates in Spain, part of a run of European shows across the rest of the year. items._cn_summary: 这是1996年德国厂牌abRECt发行的限量卡带专辑，仅制作40份，附录像盒、小册子、海报及艺术作品。从收录信息来看，这是一张典型的地下噪音作品，十首曲目围绕创作者描述的概念展开：自然环境的异化、人类对变形的过度强化、古老关联的不可达，以及草与钢、脓液与金属之间的虚构联结。音乐呈现为不结构化的声响，描绘想象中的黄色荒原景观。专辑风格契合暗潮与工业范畴，但其文本仅为唱片信息记录加艺术家自述，缺乏实质性乐评内容，无法深入评估其声音设计的独创性与艺术价值。限量发行与手工包装体现了90年代欧洲地下实验音乐的美学倾向，但就文本信息而言，可供参考的内容极为有限。

items.body:
Smacking that sweetspot between grime, techno, bassline and soca, Anthoney J Hart (East Man, Imaginary Forces) aka Basic Rhythm delivers a full-bore pack of rampers for Bristol-via-Berlin’s bassbin overlords, Sneaker Social Club.

Active in a vein of uchronic, ‘nuum-bending invention since the 2010’s, but with roots reaching back to ‘90s pirate radio, Hart’s decade-straddling steez yields the crankiest horsepower as Basic Rhythm on ‘8 Bar Techno’. Hewing hard to the brief, he dissects and recombines styles & patterns with a fiercely upfront quality, trampling on putative borders with a rudeboy alacrity that works a treat on up-for -it ‘floors.

The durable torsion of OG jungle tekno and its myriad derivations are twisted into tensile girders, variously splitting the difference between 4/4 grime and hard groove techno in ‘the title tune, or panel-beating sublow into rictus bashiness on ‘Weed Killer’, while firing killer rounds of vocal cuts including the dancehall-grime of ‘Vibez’ with NyNy, or electroid drill with Lyrical Strally and Eklipse.

Along with the precision-tooled rufige of ‘Kонец века’ with Moscow Legend, the mutant soca gallop o ‘Ice cold’, and diesel-fuelled grime-techno of ‘More Pricks than Kicks’, or the dive-bombing darkness of ‘The Deluge’, it’s a hard set for discerning 140BPM shotters, and surely one of Basic Rhythm’s deadliest.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Basic Rhythm（Anthoney J Hart）发行于Bristol系地下厂牌Sneaker Social Club。Hart将grime、jungle、soca与硬核techno拆解重组，以4/4节拍为骨架，把低音线锻造成承重钢梁，搭配dancehall唱段和说唱人声切片，呈现出高度功能化的俱乐部武器。评论强调其风格融合的活力和派对效果，形容作品具有破坏类型边界的粗糙能量和rudeboy式的直率态度。整体定位明确为针对140BPM舞池的重型低音发行，是一张技术熟练但更偏向类型杂糅而非深层实验的舞池工具集。

items.body:
Back by demand - 2nd hand copies are known to trade for triple figures - Cindy’s timeless suite of sexy, hazed dream-pop is acutely tipped to anyone who holds a flame for Julee Cruise, Voice Actor, Lynch, Enya, Bianca Scout, Vince Clarke...

‘I’m Cindy’ is a chef’s kiss of effortlessly slow, seductive lo-fi songwriting that practically smushes earlobes with its heavenly marriage of Kai Hugo's faded production lustre and singer, Blue LoLãn’s range of whispered sweet nothings and harmonised coos. In the years since its original release it’s taken on a life of its own as a go-to succour for lovers of blissed-out, cinematic waft with equal measures of soft-focus, nostalgic FM synths and details that caress and crack in all the right, tender places. 

Conceptually derived from Palmbomen II’s ‘Memories of Cindy’ session of 2017, the 13 tracks find marbled whorls of sensual fascination within that LP’s fantasy reminiscence, here expanded into a spectrum of LA-via-Antwerp dream-pop like Johnny Jewel meets Alex Zhang Hungtai on the synth and sax pearl ‘Another’ or lip-smacking cruiser ‘Justin’, thru a Voice Actor-esque ‘Voice Message’ and the gossamer FM synth fronds that wrap it up on ‘Maybe Because It’s Over Now’, whilst secreting shimmers of Vince Clarke ballads in ‘2y & 6m’, and acid-laced lo-fi machine crack shades away from Maria Minerva on ’Never Let Me Go’.

No brainer!

items.body:
A more Manhattan than Manhattan itself blend of critic-friendly rock, snotty sleaze-punk and weed-headed loser rap, Chanel Beads' debut album is Dimes Square pressed to wax.

Helmed by engineer and musician Shane Lavers, Chanel Beads are indicative of a very contemporary wave of New York City-centric art and music; they're that side of the pond's bar italia, in other words. The difference is that 'Your Day Will Come' is innovative in its own way. Sure, there are traces to be found of Pitchfork-favored indie's past: NYC legends Gang Gang Dance and The Dirty Projectors, for example. But Lavers muddles his influences with references to Talk Talk, Cocteau Twins and Harold Budd, Steely Dan and Prefab Sprout, rapping over the results like he's just been co-signed by Drain Gang. 

It's not particularly easy to digest but it is intriguing, thrusting forth a sturdy snapshot of the almost comically maligned Dimes Square scene, a "post-ironic" subculture that sat at the intersection of art, podcasting and internet culture. Whether you can handle that depends on your trivia, your tolerance and your general level of interest, we reckon. If you're into Elias Rønnenfelt's last record, 'Your Day Will Come' should at least press a few of the right buttons.

items.body:
LA musician Aaron MF Olson debuts on Country Thyme Records - his second ‘songs for singing’ album in just over a decade of releasing music.

"Aaron’s a sweet fellow. He can be salty on occasion, but it’s put to good use here. His songs mix satiric, confessional and experimental lyric modes and his music’s cut from a fine cloth of head-in- formed, classically sweet and soft pop/rock modes. Most of all, Songs Album II is music for listening.

To listen to and to play music; that's been his highest aim, for most of his life. His high school band was a post-rock group that morphed into a surf music outfit; he’s been similarly guided by such polarities ‘n congruities in the time since. He’s released four albums of “Baywatch Krautrock” with LA Takedown, and played and recorded in many other projects, including but not limited to his experimental Music Tracing Ensemble, exotica collective Other Delights, Bedouine, Coffin Prick, Papa M, Tommy Peltier, Vetiver and “L.A.’s Most grateful Dead cover band,” Richard Pictures. Aaron’s solo credits include 2020’s switched-on essay, Ranchera '22 {Synthesizer Interpretations of the Songs of José Alfredo Jiménez} and the 2022 New Age release, For Dorothy. He does film/television composition too; most recently, the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack for Matt Hewitt’s indie horror film, Hoagie. Life’s not cheap, and so far as hard work goes, making music is fun.

If all this implies a wide palette of input/output, Songs Album II has it in reserve, framed scrupulously in a sequence of nice, light folk/rock ditties, their spacey-yet-precise arrangements colorfully blowing up the songs’ personal values: by definition, perfect listening! It’s Aaron, on most acoustic and electric guitars and basses, keyboards, harmonica, synth & vocals, Robin MacMillian on drums, Tara Milch, flute; Michael Sachs, clarinets; Luke Csehak, bassoon & trumpet; additional guitars & vocals from Blue Broderick, Bart Davenport and Wayne Faler; keyboards & vocals from Andrew Dorsett and vocals by Matt Popieluch, making Songs Album II a collection of widescreen, hi-def songs and sounds.

Aaron’s voice is light-toned, gentle and tunefully raspy, falling somewhere between Jack Nitzsche, Van Dyke Parks, Robert Wyatt, and personal inspirations John Simon, Stephen Pastel, Jim O’Rourke and Kermit’s nephew, Robin. And Emmett Otter! Not a bad bunch to be sharing the water with. He came late to singing; 2021’s Songs Album was literally provoked into being. He’d was down with COVID, a lifeless, cold week, sweating it out… and immediately afterwards, he finished several already-conceived songs, wrote the rest, got it all done in weeks — a post-fever fervor! Without trying to, Aaron came around to Songs Album II in the EXACT same way, after another bout of demon COVID. He’s a singer/songwriter who’s been known to dream musical passages, with a couple on this record in delightful proof — welcoming the hand of the mystic upon him.

The “no particular theme” implied by the title is only part so. It’s no concept album, unless the concept is “album, of songs,” but there ARE themes to be found here, feels and emotions crystalized around this lifetime of listening. With moments of sound laced into song, functioning both as toe-tapping sweet melodies and near-Joycean full-function index of personal reference, Aaron MF Olson’s Songs Album II is music meant for listening to in the spirit of listening, and higher calling. And singing along!"

items.body:
Featuring MØ, Quiet Light, Koilwood, Helena Gao and others, Copenhagen duo A Good Year's second album is another slick set of trip-hop inspired Danish pop from the reliable Escho stable, home of Smerz, Astrid Sonne, Iceage and Snuggle.

Albert Hildebrand and Tobias Laust Hansen didn't have a fixed idea in mind when they started work on 'Play'. As the title suggests, it emerged from just playing, improvising with each other and shuttling recordings back and forth between their collaborators. "The music became a vessel for connection," they explain. "A way to reach to people we admire, but also a way to create a social element within these sometimes introverted jams." And their approach leads to an uncommonly light set of almost-pop; it's still as neatly polished as anything from the fertile Copenhagen scene, but there's a willing naivety that allows breathing room, a way for errors to slip in and humanize the material in the face of AI perfection.

Fine collaborator Koilwood shows up on the charming 'Back of a car', whispering softly over Hildebrand and Hansen's skipping lo-fi beats and skeletal instrumentation and Tiffi Malmgren lends her voice to early highlight 'Flight', a slo-mo trip-hop dream that's lifted by the duo's tape-warped piano vamps and hazy textures. And Malmgren returns with Major Lazer collaborator MØ (yep it was her on 'Lean On') on the album's stand-out 'Blue Flame', an electrified indie anthem that makes good use of the Danish singers' unique, recognizable voices. Scandi pop lovers, this'll hit the spot.

Copenhagen group Liss' 2022 album, 'I Guess Nothing Will Be The Same' on Escho. 

"Danish four piece Liss' debut album in the hopes of creating a lasting legacy for late lead singer Søren Holm''s life, love and talent. Although recording began many years prior, the album was only finished shortly before Holm tragically passed away in May 2021. From the most recent release "Boys In Movies ft. Nilüfer Yanya", which oscillates gorgeously between dark, grungy guitar chords and a sunny, optimistic ear worm of a chorus, to "Exist", an ethereal plea with hints of a hymn in the vocal stacks, the record shows all the transfixing sides of Liss with extraordinary heart."

items.body:
MIKE's 10K imprint continues the trans-Atlantic conversation with the latest solo album from UK rapper Jadasea, featuring guest appearances from John Glacier, duentita, Anysia Kym and MIKE.

Following an acclaimed run of collaborations with MIKE (on 2024'a 'Old Earth' EP), Anysia Kim (on 2023's 'Pressure Sensitive') and Brooklyn-based producer Laron (on 'The Corner: Vol. 1'), Jadasea hones in on a suitably brittle sound on 'Holly Grove', rapping over a sequence of shortform instrumentals led by detuned synths and paper-thin trap beats. It's engaging gear, but comes into its own when Jadasea provides room for his guests: the throwback 'Intrinsick' is uses Kym's chorus perfectly, while John Glacier wakes up 'Lemon Cherry' with her deadpan reflections. On 'Entrance', duendita hands Jadasea the hook he's been missing, and on 'Collateral' MIKE's charisma gives the album a much-needed shot of adrenaline.

items._cn_summary: 法国电子音乐人Madeon暌违七年推出的第三张专辑以摇滚姿态回归，开篇便呈现吉他riff驱动的电子车库风格，融合了新世纪disco的律动感与新浪潮的怀旧色彩。曲目如'Car Crush Baby'带有Fischerspooner式的合成器质感，与Eric the Architect合作的'Super Platinum'则走向朋克放克路线。整体定位为新电子（nu-electro）流派，在舞曲架构中嵌入摇滚吉他元素，旋律直白且琅琅上口。虽然以舞曲节拍为骨架，但手法偏向主流舞池审美，旋律优先级高于声音探索，在实验性与先锋性层面着墨有限。

items.body: German melodic electro act Chrom have re-released the 3CD set “Electro Synthetic Decay” on Out Of Line. The collection gathers three of the band’s albums and returns to print after about two years. The triple-CD set compiles “Electroscope,” “Synthetic Movement” and “Peak & Decay,” all previously released on Out Of Line, across 33 tracks. It was first issued in April 2022 and had been out of print for more than two years before this re-release. A megamix drawn from all three albums is available. About Chrom Chrom is a German melodic electro and synth-pop act formed in 2007 by Christian Marquis and Thomas Winters. Winters left the project in 2022, and Marquis has continued it since. The band’s run of albums on Out Of Line includes “Electroscope,” “Synthetic Movement” and “Peak & Decay,” the three records now collected on “Electro Synthetic Decay.” Chrom last appeared on Side-Line with the single and video “Paralysed” in 2024. The 3CD reissue brings the band’s first three Out Of Line albums back into print in a single set.
items._cn_summary: 本文是对德国乐队 Chrom 三碟合辑《Electro Synthetic Decay》再版的资讯性报道，由独立厂牌 Out Of Line 发行，将《Electroscope》《Synthetic Movement》《Peak & Decay》三张专辑共 33 首曲目合并再版。文章以纯新闻稿形式介绍发行背景、乐队沿革及成员变动（Thomas Winters 于 2022 年离队，Christian Marquis 继续运营），附带三张专辑串烧 megamix，并未对音乐本身进行实质性评论或分析。从音乐定位看，Chrom 属于旋律化电子与合成器流行范畴，带有 EBM 工业电子色彩，与实验、前卫或学术性音乐路线存在一定距离，文章缺乏对声音设计、制作手法或艺术价值的深入探讨。
